title: Bitfarms announces first delivery in growth expansion plan, adding 205 PH/s of new computing power
summary: Bitfarms announces the first delivery of 4,100 new generation miners for Phase 1 of its Sherbrooke computing center, expected to add approximately 205 PH/s of Bitcoin-focused computing power. This expansion will increase the company's total computing power to ~525 PH/s and improve operational efficiency. The T3 miners, manufactured by Innosilicon Technology Ltd., will utilize green surplus energy and are not subject to recent tariffs on Chinese goods.

title: Better battery, Night mode, 'slofies' and other cool things coming to Apple's new iPhones
summary: Apple unveiled new iPhones, Apple Watch, and services, focusing on improved battery life, camera features like Night mode and "slofies," and an always-on display for the Apple Watch Series 5. The article details five key announcements, including new gaming and video subscription services that are affordably priced.

title: General Motors vs. Tesla: Software Engineer Pay
summary: This article compares software engineer salaries at General Motors and Tesla, highlighting the significant pay gap. It discusses the competitive landscape for autonomous driving talent and notes that tech companies like Facebook, Amazon, and Google offer substantially higher compensation packages, posing a challenge for traditional auto manufacturers like GM in attracting top talent. The piece underscores the "talent war" in the autonomous vehicle space and the necessity of high compensation to secure skilled engineers.

title: You might have never heard of America's top-paying company
summary: Palo Alto Networks, a cybersecurity company, has been identified as America's highest-paying company in Glassdoor's latest ranking, offering a median total pay of nearly $171,000 annually. This figure surpasses well-known tech giants like Facebook, Google, and Microsoft. The company's focus on a growing industry—cybersecurity and cloud services—contributes to its high demand for talent and generous compensation.

title: Drone Deliveries Coming Soon, as Wing Unveils Plans for First-of-its-Kind Trial with FedEx and Walgreens
summary: Wing Aviation LLC, an Alphabet company, is collaborating with FedEx Express and Walgreens to launch a first-of-its-kind drone delivery service in Christiansburg, Virginia, next month. This pilot program, part of the U.S. DOT's Unmanned Aircraft System Integration Pilot Program, aims to enhance last-mile delivery, improve access to health care products, and create new growth avenues for local businesses. FedEx customers and Walgreens customers within designated zones will be able to receive packages and over-the-counter medicines via drone.

title: Introducing Movado Connect 2.0 - Powered with Wear OS by Google
summary: Movado announced its new Movado Connect 2.0 smartwatch collection, powered by Wear OS by Google. This next-generation timepiece features an innovative design with cutting-edge technology, available in 15 styles for women and men and two sizes (40mm + 42mm). The smartwatches, starting at $495, boast customizable dials, interchangeable straps, and a suite of features including activity tracking, GPS, heart rate monitor, and NFC payments with Google Pay.

title: McDonald’s uses Alexa and Google to help with hiring
summary: McDonald's is implementing a new voice-activated job application system using Amazon's Alexa and Google Assistant to streamline hiring. This initiative, dubbed McDonald’s Apply Thru, allows job seekers to start applications through voice commands and is part of a broader technology push by the company to attract employees in a tight job market. The feature is available in multiple countries and aims to help McDonald's fill constant staffing needs across its 38,000 restaurants worldwide.

title: Phishing attacks abusing appspot.com and web.app domains on Google Cloud
summary: Zscaler ThreatLabZ has identified a rise in phishing attacks leveraging Google’s Appspot.com and Web.app domains. These sophisticated campaigns utilize SSL certificates from Google and employ well-designed login pages to spoof brands like Dropbox, Microsoft, and DocuSign, aiming to steal user credentials. The attackers use evasion techniques, including external JavaScript files, to bypass detection by analysis engines.

title: The Merged Taboola-Outbrain Wants to Take on Facebook and Google
summary: Taboola and Outbrain have announced a merger agreement aiming to create a stronger alternative to advertising giants Facebook and Google. The combined entity will have over 2000 employees and projected revenues of $2 billion in 2019, with Taboola's CEO Adam Singolda leading the new company. Outbrain shareholders will receive a 30% stake and $250 million in cash.

title: How Amazon.com moved into the business of U.S. elections
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has significantly expanded its presence in the U.S. election technology sector since 2016, with over 40 states using its services for various election-related functions and both major political parties relying on its cloud. While offering secure and cost-effective solutions for election administrators, this centralization raises concerns among security experts about potential vulnerabilities and the impact of a single major breach. Amazon maintains its systems are reliable and faults in past data exposures were due to customer errors, even as it continues to face scrutiny over its growing influence.

title: Fertility benefits company Progyny starts strong after IPO
summary: Progyny, a Manhattan fertility benefits management company, saw its shares surge on its first day of trading on Nasdaq after an IPO that raised about $82 million. The company aims to address limited fertility benefits offered by employers and considers its profitability and public listing a way to elevate its stature in the industry. Progyny covers 1.4 million members across approximately 80 employers and reported $4 million in net income and $103.4 million in revenue in the first six months of the year.

title: HP Takes Printers Into the Cloud With Workpath, Command Center
summary: HP Inc. is introducing HP Workpath and HP Command Center to bring its multifunction printers into the cloud era, offering new revenue streams and customer loyalty opportunities for channel partners. Workpath enables app development for printers to simplify business processes, while Command Center provides cloud-based management and enhanced security for MFPs. These innovations aim to reduce labor for IT, improve security posture, and create new service offerings for partners like ImageNet Consulting.

title: Future of Streaming Entertainment Starts Today with Launch of NVIDIA SHIELD TV, Starting at $149
summary: NVIDIA has launched its next generation of SHIELD TV, starting at $149, comprising two new models: SHIELD TV and SHIELD TV Pro. These devices feature the new Tegra X1+ processor, delivering 25% more performance, and support Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos for enhanced visual and audio experiences. The new SHIELD models also utilize AI upscaling for HD content to 4K resolution and offer access to a wide range of streaming, gaming, and AI capabilities.

title: Apple Revamping Smart Home Efforts After Falling Behind Amazon, Google
summary: Apple Inc. is increasing hiring for a team dedicated to developing new smart-home software and devices to compete with Google and Amazon.com Inc. This initiative aims to expand Apple's smart-home platform, encourage more third-party accessory integration with the iPhone and Siri, and explore new home device possibilities beyond the HomePod speaker.

title: Yext aims to end the spread of fake news about brands
summary: Yext launched its first ad campaign, in partnership with TBWA\Chiat\Day New York, to combat the spread of misinformation about brands online. The campaign introduces a fictional character, "The Man Without the Answers," to highlight the dangers of false information. Yext's platform helps businesses control their online information and deliver verified facts to consumers across major search networks.

title: Marin Software Research Finds Significant Growth in eCommerce Spend
summary: Marin Software's Q3 2019 Digital Advertising Benchmark Report reveals significant growth in eCommerce spend, primarily driven by Amazon Advertising and seasonal events like Prime Day, with a 115% year-over-year increase. Mobile search continues to dominate, accounting for nearly half of total search spend, indicating a shift towards localized mobile queries. The report highlights opportunities for marketers to optimize campaigns across various platforms, including non-eCommerce features like Instagram Explore Feed and Facebook Watch, as the industry enters a busy Q4 season.

title: What is an Ovintiv? Encana’s name change smacks of desperation
summary: Encana Corp.'s decision to change its name to Ovintiv Inc. is viewed as a desperate move by the author, who questions the efficacy of name changes in influencing stock performance. The article suggests that such changes often occur when companies are under pressure or struggling, and historically have not led to sustained improvements in share prices. It further implies that the name change, coupled with a move to the U.S., might be a cosmetic attempt to mask deeper business issues.

title: UPS Debuts Home Delivery of CVS Medicine by Drone
summary: UPS has expanded its drone delivery services beyond hospital campuses, completing its first revenue-generating home deliveries of prescription medicines from a CVS Health Corp. pharmacy in Cary, N.C. The company used autonomous drones monitored by remote pilots, lowering packages by a winch, and plans to further grow drone deliveries, especially in rural areas, to compete with rivals like Amazon and FedEx. UPS was the first company approved by the FAA for commercial drone flights under the broadest airline rules.

title: Google starts construction on $600M data center in unlikely burgeoning tech hub of New Albany, Ohio
summary: Google has begun construction on a $600 million data center in New Albany, Ohio, marking its third major tech facility in the area. The project is expected to be completed by early 2021 and follows investments from Facebook and Amazon, turning central Ohio into a data center hub due to significant tax cuts and strong electrical infrastructure. New Albany offered Google a substantial incentive package, including property tax abatement and waived fees, while the state of Ohio also provides sales tax exemptions for data centers.

title: An ETF to Consider as Alphabet Shuts Down Self-Driving Car Project

summary: Sonos has acquired the AI startup Snips for $37.5 million, aiming to integrate Snips' privacy-conscious conversational AI into its products. summary: ProServ Logistics, founded by former C.H. Robinson employees Brian Johnson and Dave Buhl, is starting to see the payoff of their long-term strategy. The author concludes by calling for tech companies to be held accountable for their role in facilitating the spread of destructive ideologies.

This disclosure comes as the EEOC for the first time required companies to include pay data.

summary: Big tech companies like Facebook and Google have fallen out of the Top 10 in Glassdoor's annual "best places to work" rankings. title: Buy or Sell a Car via Mobile with the New eBay Motors App
summary: eBay Motors has launched an all-new, automotive-focused app for Apple iPhone and Android, designed to streamline the buying and selling of vehicles. summary: Google Cloud and Palo Alto Networks announced an expanded strategic partnership to deliver new cybersecurity solutions. Palo Alto Networks will also run several of its services, including Prisma Access and Cortex, on Google Cloud Platform to offer increased visibility and security analytics for customers.

summary: Intel Corp. acquired Israeli AI chipmaker Habana Labs for approximately $2 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence silicon market. This acquisition is part of Intel's strategy to make its offerings essential to major silicon buyers and compete against companies like Alphabet's Google and Amazon's AWS, which are increasingly designing their own chips for data centers. Habana Labs is expected to operate independently for the time being.

title: Check Point finds flaw in WhatsApp that could allow group-chat crash
summary: Israeli cybersecurity firm Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. identified and helped fix a vulnerability in WhatsApp that could have allowed a malicious message to crash group chats for all members. Users would need to reinstall the app and delete the problematic group to regain access. WhatsApp has since fixed the flaw in version 2.19.58, and users are advised to update their app.

title: Nvidia debuts new DRIVE AGX Orin platform for autonomous cars and robots
summary: Nvidia has launched its new DRIVE AGX Orin platform, designed to power AI systems in autonomous vehicles and robots. The platform features the Orin system-on-a-chip, boasting 17 billion transistors and capable of 200 trillion operations per second, making it seven times faster than its predecessor. Didi Chuxing is already utilizing the platform for its Level 4 autonomous driving development, and Nvidia is offering free access to its DRIVE deep neural networks to other transportation industry customers to encourage adoption.

title: Amazon hits back at claims it’s abusing open-source software
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. has responded to criticism that it "strip-mines" open-source software projects by repackaging them as paid services. While AWS claims to be giving customers what they want and contributing significantly to open-source projects, some critics argue this practice undermines the sustainability of open-source companies, forcing them to compete against the very software they developed. Analysts suggest open-source companies must innovate and offer managed versions of their products to succeed against large cloud providers.

title: A new ad-tech merger takes aim at Google and Facebook's dominance
summary: Public ad tech companies Telaria and Rubicon Project have agreed to merge to create a stronger presence in connected television advertising and offer an alternative to "walled gardens" like Google and Facebook. The stock-for-stock merger aims to form a major independent sell-side ad platform, with Telaria stockholders owning about 47.1% and Rubicon Project stockholders about 52.9% of the combined company. This move comes as Google and Facebook face antitrust scrutiny, allowing the merged entity to target the growing CTV market more effectively.

title: Johnson & Johnson Announces Agreement to Acquire Remaining Stake in Verb Surgical Inc.
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced an agreement to acquire the remaining stake in Verb Surgical Inc., augmenting its digital surgery portfolio. This acquisition, following a successful collaboration with Verily, aims to make medical interventions smarter, less invasive, and more personalized by combining robotics, data science, and advanced instrumentation. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2020, enhancing J&J's leadership in the medical devices sector.

summary: Bilibili is actively expanding beyond its traditional anime, comic, and games (ACG) content to establish itself as a mainstream entertainment platform. title: Spotify to suspend political advertising in 2020
summary: Spotify Technology SA announced it would pause selling political advertisements on its music streaming platform in early 2020, including on its original and exclusive podcasts. This decision comes as campaigns for the U.S. presidential election intensify and other online platforms face pressure over misinformation and political ads, with Spotify citing a lack of robustness in its current systems to responsibly validate and review such content. The new policy will cover various political groups and content advocating for legislative and judicial outcomes, though it only applies to Spotify's ad sales, not embedded third-party content.

summary: Apple's stock concluded its strongest year in a decade with its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio reaching a historic high of 24.7, up from just over 13 at the beginning of 2019. This elevated P/E ratio makes Apple historically expensive compared to its past performance, although it remains below the average for the S&P 500 information technology index and many other megacap tech stocks. Factors like improved iPhone 11 expectations, anticipation of the 5G 2020 iPhone cycle, and strong wearable device performance have contributed to the increased valuation, according to Deutsche Bank analyst Jeriel Ong.

summary: MTBC, a provider of cloud-based healthcare IT and revenue cycle management solutions, announced the acquisition of CareCloud, a cloud-based practice management EHR platform. The deal was completed on a cash-free, debt-free basis and is expected to drive growth and operational efficiencies for the combined entities.

summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos is expected to encounter significant protests from local merchants during his visit to India. The protests coincide with Bezos's participation in Amazon India’s "smbhav" event, highlighting growing resentment against the company's business model in a critical market.

title: The Mighty Apple, Google, Tesla, Dell and Microsoft in “the dock” - A Look At the Child Labour Lawsuit
summary: A landmark class-action lawsuit has been filed against Apple, Google, Tesla, Dell, and Microsoft, alleging their complicity in child labor practices within the cobalt mines of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Complaints have been filed against Grindr and several ad-tech companies, highlighting the potential for severe privacy violations and the need for stricter enforcement of data protection laws.

summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella asserts that capitalism is in jeopardy if businesses fail to address climate change, emphasizing that corporations must find profitable solutions to planetary problems. This stance aligns with a growing trend of companies and investors prioritizing sustainability alongside financial performance.

title: Swiping their way higher: Visa, Mastercard could be the next $1 trillion companies
summary: Visa and Mastercard are rapidly increasing in market value, with stocks up roughly 50% in the past year, leading some to believe they could be the next $1 trillion companies by 2023. Their growth is driven by the global shift towards cashless financial transactions and online shopping, with both companies holding significant shares of the credit and debit card market. Despite potential risks from increased competition and regulation, both firms are actively seeking acquisitions to boost their financial technology integration.

title: In Pictures: Indian-origin CEOs of top tech companies
summary: This article showcases prominent Indian-origin CEOs leading top technology companies globally. It highlights individuals like Arvind Krishna (IBM), Sundar Pichai (Google, Alphabet), Satya Nadella (Microsoft), Shantanu Narayen (Adobe), Jayshree Ullal (Arista Networks), Sanjay Mehrotra (Micron), George Kurian (NetApp), and Sandeep Mathrani (WeWork), detailing their backgrounds and roles within their respective companies as of early 2020. The article emphasizes the growing presence and influence of Indian-origin leaders in the tech industry.

title: Starbucks improves customer experience with AI
summary: Starbucks is enhancing its customer experience through the deployment of AI-equipped hardware and analytics. The company plans to install 4,000 AI-enabled Mastrena II espresso makers in 2020 and is leveraging its Deep Brew AI engine to understand customer preferences better and increase efficiency. These efforts, combined with significant growth in its loyalty program and digital customer base, are contributing to improved service, brand loyalty, and new offerings.

title: 10 ETFs with over 10 million dollars in assets under management
summary: This article lists 10 Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) each managing over $10 million in assets, emphasizing the diversity in their management styles and performance metrics despite similar asset sizes. It provides details on each ETF including their symbols, AUM, NAV, management fees, inception dates, and top holdings, offering insights for potential investors. The data was collected from Bloomberg, ETF.com, and Yahoo Finance between December 31, 2019, and January 10, 2020.

title: Beam Therapeutics shines in $180m IPO
summary: Beam Therapeutics, a genomic medicine developer backed by Alphabet, Editas, and Bio Palette, successfully completed an upsized $180 million IPO, pricing shares at $17.00. The company increased its share offering to nearly 10.6 million and plans to use the proceeds to fund R&D, clinical trials, and drug discovery. Previously, Beam Therapeutics secured significant funding rounds from investors including GV, Eight Roads Ventures, F-Prime Capital, Hillhouse Capital, Temasek, and Arch Venture Partners, which was its largest pre-IPO shareholder.

title: Uber is ready to join the FANG camp, analyst says after earnings
summary: Following its latest earnings report, an analyst suggested that Uber Technologies Inc. is ready to join the ranks of major internet companies like Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Google. RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney proposed the acronym FANGU, adding Uber, as the company works towards profitability and leverages its scale. This optimism led to an 8% increase in Uber's stock price on Friday morning.

title: Wells Fargo ends forced arbitration for sexual harassment complaints
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. announced it will no longer require arbitration for employee sexual harassment complaints, making it the first major U.S. bank to do so. This change follows discussions with stakeholders including Clean Yield Asset Management, which had submitted a shareholder proposal focused on the practice. The decision is seen as a significant step in addressing misconduct in the #MeToo era, as forced arbitration has often been criticized for obscuring complaints and protecting repeat offenders.

title: Expedia stock rises 10% as travel giant cites focus on core operations following executive shuffle
summary: Expedia's stock rose over 10% after reporting fourth-quarter earnings that beat profit expectations, driven by a renewed focus on core operations and efficiency improvements. This comes after an executive shuffle in December, with Chairman Barry Diller and Vice Chairman Peter Kern now projecting double-digit Adjusted EBITDA growth for 2020 despite Coronavirus uncertainties, and targeting $300-500 million in cost savings. The company also reported increased revenue and gross bookings, and aims for improved revenue growth and margin expansion in the coming years.

title: Google Has Banned Almost 600 Apps For Pushing “Disruptive” Ads
summary: Google has banned nearly 600 Android apps and their developers from the Play Store and its ad networks due to "disruptive" mobile ads and ad fraud. This crackdown, supported by new detection technology, targets apps that display ads when not in use or lead to inadvertent clicks, with many of the banned apps originating from developers in China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and India. Google is also refunding affected advertisers.

title: Beyond ESG: How Individuals Can Influence Corporations
summary: This article discusses how individuals can influence corporations beyond traditional ESG investing by leveraging their consumer choices, employment decisions, and advocacy. It highlights the rise of stakeholder capitalism and provides examples of how customers, employees, suppliers, communities, and shareholders have successfully pressured companies to adopt more responsible practices, leading to positive corporate behavior and potentially superior stock returns.

title: J&J’s Ethicon mostly fends off Intuitive Surgical’s robotic surgery patent challenge
summary: Johnson & Johnson's Ethicon subsidiary successfully defended most of its robotic surgery tool patent against a challenge from Intuitive Surgical. The Patent Trial and Appeal Board found that Intuitive failed to prove the patent was obvious, upholding 25 of 28 claims. This decision highlights the ongoing intellectual property disputes in the competitive robotic surgery market, where J&J and others are challenging Intuitive Surgical's dominance.

title: LatAm telecoms group with Luxembourg HQ posts profit
summary: Millicom International Cellular SA, a Luxembourg-headquartered telecom company, reported a profit of $149 million in the last year, reversing a previous loss, primarily driven by acquisitions in Latin America. The company significantly expanded its presence in Central and South America while largely divesting from its African markets. Despite political and competitive challenges in some regions, Millicom benefits from geographic diversification and its strong market position in the countries where it operates.

title: Google has removed almost all Cheetah Mobile apps from the Play Store
summary: Google has reportedly removed almost all Cheetah Mobile apps from the Play Store due to the developer's history of ad fraud, disruptive apps, and data collection issues. While Google has not officially confirmed a ban, the timing coincides with their announcement of removing 600 apps for similar violations. Cheetah Mobile is now offering its apps as APK downloads directly from its website, bypassing the Play Store.

title: !Alphabet's Waymo scores $2.25B in first outside funding
summary: !Alphabet's self-driving car unit, Waymo, secured its first external funding round, raising $2.25 billion. This investment marks a significant milestone for the Mountain View-based company, which originated from Google's autonomous vehicle project in 2009. The funding will likely accelerate the development and deployment of Waymo's autonomous vehicle technology.

title: Waymo launches delivery service after raising $2.25 billion
summary: Waymo is expanding its services by formally launching Waymo Via, a delivery service utilizing its autonomous vehicles and Class 8 trucks, after successfully raising $2.25 billion from a group of outside investors. This move is a natural extension of its autonomous drive technology, with initial routes opening along the I-10 corridor connecting Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas. The company, an Alphabet unit, also plans future growth in California and other markets for its self-driving car technology.

title: Waymo gets US$2.25 billion from investors to power self-driving expansion
summary: Self-driving car company Waymo has raised US$2.25 billion in its first external funding round to fuel its global expansion. The capital came from a diverse group of investors including Silver Lake, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, and Mubadala Investment, alongside its parent company Alphabet Inc. This funding will support the deployment of the Waymo Driver worldwide, as the company competes in the rapidly evolving autonomous driving market.

title: HPE Confirms Discover Conference Still On, Cancels ‘Most’ Events Through April
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has decided to proceed with its annual Discover Las Vegas and Discover More London conferences, despite canceling or postponing most other events through April due to coronavirus concerns. Partners have expressed support for HPE's decision, emphasizing the need to continue business while taking prudent precautions. The company plans to shift resources to digital engagement for customers and partners.

title: Go Above & Beyond With This ESG ETF
summary: The Global X Conscious Companies ETF (KRMA) offers investors a differentiated approach to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing. Unlike traditional ESG funds that merely exclude "sin stocks," KRMA focuses on companies that demonstrate financial performance in a sustainable and responsible manner, emphasizing stakeholders such as customers, suppliers, and employees. This methodology, rooted in the triple bottom line and long-term value creation, has led to KRMA outperforming the S&P 500 with less volatility since its inception.

title: McDonald's cancels in-person convention for worldwide franchisees due to coronavirus
summary: McDonald's has canceled its in-person biennial worldwide convention for franchisees, originally scheduled for Orlando, Florida, due to the coronavirus outbreak. The event will now be held virtually. This decision follows similar actions by other major companies like Starbucks, Target, and Google, as the number of U.S. COVID-19 cases continues to rise, impacting the travel industry.

title: Expedia Group, Booking Holdings spent more than $11B on marketing (mostly to Google) in 2019
summary: Expedia Group and Booking Holdings collectively spent over $11 billion on marketing in 2019, with a significant portion going to Google. Expedia Group increased its marketing spend by 6% to $6.03 billion, while Booking Holdings maintained a nearly flat spend at $4.97 billion. The article highlights how Google's growing presence in online travel forces OTAs to increase advertising to maintain visibility.

title: The Chief Information And Digital Officer Of AES Drives The Smart Grid And The Connected Enterprise
summary: Sanjeev Addala, Chief Information and Digital Officer of AES, discusses the company's digital transformation journey, focusing on customer-centricity, new business models, and revenue streams. He details the digital strategy across three business dimensions and five strategic themes, including connected enterprise, smart grid, and scaling a digital ecosystem. Addala also shares his perspective on the evolving CDO role and the importance of digital in driving growth and innovation for industrial companies.

title: Social Media Moves to New Era of Growth
summary: Social media platforms are entering a new era of growth, shifting focus from user acquisition to maximizing revenue per user through targeted advertising and innovative technologies. New avenues like social commerce and AR/VR are being explored to diversify revenue streams. This evolution includes in-app purchases, live-streaming commerce, and augmented reality experiences to further engage users and drive monetization.

title: Digital Asset Marketplace Apifiny Hires Execs from Google, Kraken & More, Plans Global Trading Service
summary: Digital asset marketplace Apifiny announced the launch of GlobalX, an API platform designed to enable institutional trading across multiple regulated exchanges with crypto-to-crypto and crypto-to-fiat pairs. The launch is spearheaded by three new executives with backgrounds from Google, Kraken, and AlphaPoint, aiming to simplify global trading for professional traders through a single account and onboarding process. GlobalX aims to break down barriers in digital asset trading by offering global execution from one account for unprecedented trading opportunities.

title: Microsoft Edge is becoming the browser you didn’t know you needed
summary: Microsoft Edge is introducing several compelling new features like Collections, Immersive Reader, and vertical tabs, aiming to elevate its status beyond just a functional default browser. While some features are still in preview, they offer significant enhancements for organization, readability, and user interface. Additionally, Edge gains exclusive 4K Netflix streaming support on Windows 10 and improved privacy tools.

title: BlackBerry uncovers hacker tools that it says opened data servers for a decade
summary: BlackBerry has released a report detailing how five separate groups linked to the Chinese government have been targeting Linux systems for a decade. These hackers have used novel techniques, including disguising malicious tools as advertising software, to exfiltrate vast amounts of data from servers. The report highlights a significant blind spot in cybersecurity, as Linux powers critical global infrastructure like stock exchanges and major cloud services.

title: Google Classroom sees a doubling user-base as more students work from home
summary: Google Classroom has seen its user base double to over 100 million due to the increase in online education during the pandemic, with significant growth in previously underserved regions like Italy and Indonesia. This surge is also boosting usage of other Google services like Meet and the broader G Suite for Education, which now has 120 million users. Despite the positive growth, Google continues to face privacy concerns and lawsuits regarding user data.

title: Apple and Google partner on COVID-19 contact tracing technology
summary: Apple and Google are collaborating on a joint effort to enable the use of Bluetooth technology for COVID-19 contact tracing, prioritizing user privacy and security. The solution will be rolled out in two phases, starting with APIs in May and then integrating functionality directly into underlying operating systems. This initiative aims to help governments and health authorities reduce the spread of the virus.

title: Barry Diller: Expedia normally spends $5 billion on ads but probably 'won't spend $1 billion' this year
summary: Expedia Group chairman Barry Diller announced that the company, which typically allocates $5 billion to advertising, will drastically cut ad spending to less than $1 billion this year due to the coronavirus pandemic. This decision reflects a broader trend of advertisers pausing or canceling campaigns amidst budget uncertainty, particularly in the travel industry. Shares in Expedia Group, whose brands include Hotels.com and Orbitz, were down 1% following the announcement.

title: NEC and Intermedia Announce Strategic Global Partnership: Press Releases
summary: NEC Corporation and Intermedia have formed a strategic global partnership to provide cloud-based Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS) and Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) solutions. This collaboration introduces NEC UNIVERGE BLUE CONNECT and ENGAGE, designed to help businesses of all sizes migrate to the cloud and enhance their communication and collaboration capabilities. The partnership leverages Intermedia's technology and NEC's global reach, aiming to meet the demands of a digital workforce and support remote operations.

title: Electronic Arts and Google Announce Partnership to Bring EA Games to Stadia
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) and Google have announced a partnership to bring five EA games to Google's cloud-based gaming platform, Stadia. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is expected to launch on Stadia by the end of 2020, with EA SPORTS FIFA and Madden NFL following in winter, and more games planned for 2021. This collaboration aims to provide new and innovative gaming experiences on the Stadia platform.

title: WOW! Launches WOW! tv+ in Cleveland and Mid-Michigan
summary: WOW! Internet, Cable & Phone launched its new IP-based video service, WOW! tv+, in Cleveland and Mid-Michigan. This Android TV-based platform offers live channel packages, cloud DVR, and access to an On Demand library, aiming to provide an enhanced viewing experience. The move signals WOW!'s shift to an IP-delivered video offering, leveraging its broadband network and supporting a more flexible content consumption model for customers.

title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt Cut Last Ties With The Company: Report
summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt officially severed all ties with Alphabet Inc. in February 2020, ending his 19-year tenure with the company. Schmidt, who had served in various executive roles since 2001, stepped down as a technology advisor, a move that coincided with his increased involvement in government roles. His departure also came amid criticism over his dual role as an advisor to the Pentagon while Alphabet competed for the JEDI contract.

title: Lawsuit Alleging Anti-Conservative Bias at Google Ends Quietly
summary: A high-profile lawsuit alleging anti-conservative bias at Google, initiated by former engineer James Damore, has come to a quiet end. Damore and co-plaintiffs, along with Google, requested dismissal of the suit, with terms of the agreement prohibiting further public comment. Despite the quiet end, Damore's lawyer asserts the lawsuit prompted Silicon Valley companies, including Google, to institute workplace rules protecting alternative viewpoints and resulted in policy changes regarding employee discussions of working conditions.

title: KeyBank to incorporate Kubernetes into digital transformation strategy
summary: KeyBank announced its plan to integrate Kubernetes technology into its data center operations to further its digital transformation efforts. This move, leveraging Google Cloud's Cloud Services Platform, aims to launch new features more quickly, efficiently, and securely for its customers. KeyBank anticipates that this will enhance velocity, reliability, and governance at scale for its banking services.

title: NextEra Energy: Agrees to supply 114MW to Google Energy
summary: NextEra Energy Resources, a subsidiary of NextEra Energy Inc, has signed a power purchase agreement with Google Energy, LLC, to supply 114 megawatts of renewable energy from its Story II Wind Energy Center. This agreement highlights Google Energy's commitment to emission-free energy and expands NextEra Energy Resources' significant wind power portfolio in North America. The Story II Wind Energy Center, which began operations in December 2009, will start supplying Google Energy with power on July 30, 2010.

title: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern: 'Google's a problem for everyone who sells something online'
summary: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern criticized Google for its dual role as a competitor and a major source of customer traffic, stating it's an issue for all online sellers. Kern indicated a shift in strategy for Expedia to reduce its reliance on Google and performance marketing by improving internal merchandising and customer understanding. These comments follow Expedia's quarterly earnings report where marketing expenses dropped significantly, and the company reported a major reduction in business due to COVID-19.

title: Google faces $5 billion lawsuit in U.S. for tracking 'private' internet use
summary: Google is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit seeking at least $5 billion for allegedly tracking users' internet activity through browsers set in "private" or Incognito mode. The lawsuit claims Google surreptitiously collects data through its various services, even when users believe their browsing is private. Google denies the claims, stating that it clearly informs users that websites might still collect information during Incognito browsing.

title: New $5 billion lawsuit accuses Google of tracking users in Incognito Mode
summary: A new $5 billion class-action lawsuit has been filed against Google, alleging that the company continues to track users even when they are browsing in Chrome's Incognito Mode. The complaint argues that unauthorized data collection through services like Google Analytics and Ad Manager violates federal wiretapping and privacy laws. Google has stated it will defend the claims, noting that Incognito tabs warn users that websites might still collect browsing activity.

title: Real Networks' AI Facial Recognition Software IDs Familiar Faces in Streaming Movies and Personal Videos
summary: Real Networks has launched two new AI-powered facial recognition products: StarSearch for identifying actors in streaming movies and TV shows on platforms like Netflix and YouTube, and RealPlayer 20/20 for organizing personal video collections by individuals. These tools aim to address the common user query of identifying faces on screen, leveraging Real's Secure Accurate Facial Recognition (SAFR) software, which boasts high accuracy and low bias. The company envisions expanding the technology to more streaming services and enhancing personal video organization.

title: How Snowflake is challenging the cloud-native database giants
summary: This article examines how Snowflake Inc. is competing with major cloud providers like Amazon Web Services, Google, and Microsoft in the cloud-native database market. It analyzes customer spending data from Enterprise Technology Research (ETR) to demonstrate Snowflake's strong spending momentum across all three major clouds and discusses its strategy of being cloud-agnostic and prioritizing engineering investments. The piece concludes that Snowflake's specialized focus and native cloud architecture position it well for continued growth and a successful IPO despite competition from giants with vast R&D budgets.

title: General Electric’s exit from lighting business is a warning to other players in the sector
summary: General Electric has sold its lighting division to Savant for $250 million, marking the end of its nearly 130-year involvement in the lighting industry. This exit is attributed to GE's failure to prioritize LED research and adapt to the commoditization of LED technology and the rise of Chinese manufacturers. The article suggests that other lighting companies must learn from GE's mistakes and invest in innovative LED applications beyond general illumination to avoid a similar fate.

title: Morgan Stanley's Gorman 'thrilled' with ETrade purchase
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expresses immense satisfaction with the acquisition of ETrade, highlighting the online trading firm's technology, digital banking capabilities, and management team. He plans to retain the ETrade brand, possibly as "ETrade powered by Morgan Stanley," recognizing its value to clients. Gorman believes the deal expands Morgan Stanley's online platform, diversifies the company, and strengthens its digital offerings, particularly appealing to a younger demographic.

title: Insight Partners to acquire senior Israeli venture fund Gemini V for $500 million
summary: Insight Partners is set to acquire the fifth fund of Israeli venture firm Gemini Israel Ventures for approximately $500 million. Gemini V's portfolio includes successful companies like WalkMe Inc., JFrog Ltd., Monday.com Labs Ltd., and Moovit App Global Ltd., which was recently acquired by Intel for $1 billion. This acquisition is part of a series of investments and deals made by Insight Partners in Israeli tech companies.

title: CEO of Gannett's operating company, Paul Bascobert, will leave company; Mike Reed assumes responsibilities
summary: Paul Bascobert, CEO of Gannett Co.'s operating company, is departing after his position was eliminated to streamline operations; Michael Reed, chairman and CEO of the overall public entity, will assume his responsibilities. Bascobert's departure is not due to any inappropriate action or business deterioration. The move comes as Gannett navigates significant financial pressures and a challenging media landscape, with plans to cut $300 million in annual costs.

title: Trump signs order freezing visas for foreign workers through the end of the year
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order freezing new visas for various foreign workers, including tech and low-skill jobs, through the end of 2020. This action, aiming to preserve jobs amidst the COVID-19 economic downturn, exempts specific essential workers but includes au pairs and certain other exchange programs. The policy is expected to face backlash from the business community and immigration advocates despite the White House's claim of saving or creating 525,000 American jobs.

title: Awash in “AI Platforms”
summary: This article discusses the booming market for "AI Platforms," noting the significant financial investments predicted for digital transformation software by 2025. It criticizes the proliferation of open-source "AI Platforms" which, while offering useful components, individually lack the comprehensive utility required to fully develop and operate enterprise AI and IoT applications. The author argues that many of these components were not designed to work together and highlights their commercial viability issues.

title: Apple, Google and chorus of tech business leaders slam Trump's new visa restrictions
summary: Tech giants Apple and Google, along with other prominent business leaders, criticized the Trump administration's new restrictions on work visas, including the H-1B and L-1 visas. Critics argue that these restrictions, implemented to free up jobs for American workers, will actually hinder job creation and economic growth. CEOs like Tim Cook, Sundar Pichai, Brad Smith, Marc Benioff, and Elon Musk all expressed disappointment, highlighting the positive contributions of immigrant workers to innovation and the U.S. economy.

title: Honeywell claims it has built the most powerful quantum computer ever
summary: Honeywell claims to have built the most powerful quantum computer to date, boasting a quantum volume of 64, double that of the next highest IBM quantum computer. While this achievement is significant for Honeywell's internal operations, researchers remain skeptical as the computer's six qubits cannot yet perform calculations beyond the capability of classical computers, unlike Google's 53-qubit machine that achieved quantum supremacy. Despite this, Honeywell views it as an important step towards integrating quantum computing into their industries.

title: Blackstone adds Google CFO Ruth Porat to its board of directors
summary: Blackstone Group Inc. has appointed Ruth Porat, Google's finance chief, to its board of directors. This move highlights Blackstone's strategic shift towards technology and growth investments. Porat has a distinguished background, having previously spent 27 years with Morgan Stanley and serving as CFO for Google and its parent company, Alphabet Inc., since 2015.

title: Blackstone Group: Alphabet CFO Ruth Porat Joins The Board (BX, GOOG, GOOGL)
summary: Alphabet CFO Ruth Porat has been appointed to the board of directors of Blackstone Group Inc. Porat brings extensive experience having previously served as CFO at Morgan Stanley for 27 years and overseeing Blackstone's IPO in 2007. She will be the third woman on Blackstone's board, joining Kelly Ayotte and Rochelle Lazarus.

title: LATEST TECH NEWS: Verizon joins others to boycott Facebook. 4 other things and a trivia you need to know today, June 26, 2020
summary: This article covers five key tech news stories from June 26, 2020, including Verizon joining the boycott against Facebook due to hate speech concerns, Egyptian edtech OTO Courses securing new investment, Waymo and Volvo partnering on electric robotaxis, the opening of applications for the AppsAfrica Innovation Awards 2020, and Amazon's reported acquisition of self-driving startup Zoox for over $1 billion. It also includes a tech trivia question and answer about the beginning of computer engineering.

title: Starbucks to pause advertising across social media to help stop hate speech
summary: Starbucks announced it will pause advertising on all social media platforms to help stop the spread of hate speech, following a growing movement to boycott social networks, particularly Facebook. While not explicitly naming Facebook, the move aligns with increasing pressure from civil rights organizations on platforms to adopt stricter policies against hateful content. Starbucks clarified it is not joining the "Stop Hate For Profit" boycott campaign but is undertaking its own review.

title: Special Feature: YouTube’s Evolution in the OTT Streaming Landscape...
summary: This article by Comscore and YouTube examines YouTube's significant growth within the evolving OTT streaming landscape, highlighting its increased reach in ad-supported households and substantial growth in CTV watch time. It also details how YouTube's unique user-generated content and extensive library are providing new opportunities for advertisers to target diverse audiences. The piece further explores emerging content consumption trends on the platform, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: fuboTV follows YouTube's lead, increases monthly subscription rate
summary: FuboTV is raising its monthly subscription rate from $60 to $65 for its family plan, and existing standard plan subscribers will be automatically moved to the family plan, increasing their rates from $55 to $65. This price hike comes alongside significant content changes, as fuboTV has dropped all Turner channels but added Disney channels, including ESPN, which will be available in August. The move follows a similar price increase by YouTube TV and suggests a potential trend in the streaming service market.

title: Waymo continues innovation efforts with self driving trucks
summary: Waymo Via, the self-driving truck subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., is continuing its efforts in autonomous trucking despite a shift in industry buzz. The company focuses on developing its advanced driverless technology and partnering with OEMs and fleets rather than operating as a fleet itself. Waymo aims to provide "driver as a service" and integrate its technology into trucks, with extensive testing underway in key shipping corridors.

title: HP reinvents the printer for the smart home
summary: HP has redesigned its Tango line of printers to integrate seamlessly into smart homes, moving away from traditional clunky designs. These new printers feature a minimalist design, fabric covers similar to smart speakers, and advanced smart functionalities, including control via the HP Smart app, voice commands with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, and automatic ink reordering through HP Instant Ink. The Tango aims to make printers more convenient and aesthetically pleasing for modern living spaces.

title: Live broadcasting platform Caffeine raises $113m in Series D funding round
summary: Live broadcasting platform Caffeine has successfully raised $113 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at over $600 million. The funding, co-led by Cox Enterprises, Fox Corporation, and Sanabil Investments, with participation from existing investors, will be used to fuel continued growth, onboarding entertainers, and differentiating its content from competitors like Twitch and YouTube. Caffeine, which launched out of beta in late 2019, has significantly grown its user base and content partnerships, including a notable exclusive deal with Drake and collaborations with major sports and entertainment brands.

title: Used Car Market Analysis Highlights the Impact of COVID-19- 2020-2024 | Increase in the Launch of New Models of Cars to Boost Growth | Technavio
summary: Technavio forecasts the global used car market to grow by 34.53 million units during 2020-2024, at a CAGR of almost 6%, driven by the increased launch of new car models. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, drivers, and the impact of COVID-19, including market segmentation by product and geography, and profiles key vendors. It highlights the adoption of Industry 4.0 as a significant growth factor.

title: Google, Deutsche Bank Agree to 10-Year Cloud Partnership
summary: Google and Deutsche Bank have entered a 10-year cloud partnership, with Google providing cloud computing capabilities to Germany's largest lender. Deutsche Bank anticipates a cumulative return on investment of €1 billion ($1.1 billion) from this alliance, considering it both a revenue growth and cost-saving initiative. This deal represents a significant win for Google in the financial sector, as European banks increasingly adopt cloud solutions to modernize their IT infrastructure.

title: New Joker variant hits Google Play with an old trick
summary: Check Point Research has identified a new variant of the Joker malware, a premium dialer and dropper spyware, on Google Play. This variant employs an older PC-based technique of hiding its malicious dex file using Base64 encoding to evade detection. The malware allows unauthorized subscription to premium services, and Check Point advises users to uninstall infected apps, check bills, and install security solutions.

title: Tracking Google’s Globe-Spanning Flights
summary: A Tech Transparency Project (TTP) investigation reveals that Google and its executives have accumulated a fleet of aircraft responsible for spewing hundreds of millions of pounds of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, despite the company's public commitment to fighting climate change. The analysis of FAA data shows over 9,200 flights since 2005, totaling more than 13 million miles, including many short trips that could have been driven and flights to luxury vacation spots. This extensive private air travel contradicts Google's environmental claims and offers insights into its business and lobbying activities.

title: NVIDIA Now Most Valuable US Chipmaker, Intel Falls Behind
summary: NVIDIA has overtaken Intel to become the most valuable U.S. chipmaker, with its market capitalization reaching $251.3 billion compared to Intel's $248.2 billion. This surge is attributed to NVIDIA's strong financial performance, its dominance in gaming and data center markets, rapid adoption of its GPUs in AI, efficient cost management, and robust cash flow. The company's stock has shown exceptional growth, rallying 73.7% year-to-date and over twenty-fold in the last five years.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook No.2 on 2019 highest paid list at $133.7 million
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook ranked second on the 2019 highest-paid executive list with $133.7 million, largely due to an equity grant he received in 2011. Elon Musk topped the list with $595.3 million, primarily from a pay deal tied to Tesla's valuation. The article highlights the significant compensation packages in the tech industry compared to other sectors like finance.

title: Rackspace Technology Files For IPO Four Years After Going Private
summary: Rackspace Technology, a managed cloud company, has filed for an initial public offering four years after going private. The company, which recently rebranded, aims to re-enter the public stock market, having transformed from a competitor to a partner of public cloud giants. Rackspace reported $2.44 billion in revenue in 2019 with a net loss of $102.3 million.

title: WeRide starts testing driverless autonomous vehicles in Guangzhou
summary: WeRide has commenced testing driverless autonomous vehicles on public roads in Guangzhou, making it the first company in China and the second globally to do so without safety operators inside the cars. This move brings WeRide closer to its goal of providing fully driverless robotaxi services to the general public in Guangzhou by 2021. The company, founded in 2017, already launched robotaxi services in November 2019 and has integrated its services with Alibaba's mapping provider AutoNavi.

title: ‘Reflection of our confidence’: Google to pump $10bn into India
summary: Google announced it will invest $10 billion in India over the next five to seven years through a digitisation fund, focusing on equity investments, partnerships, and infrastructure. This significant commitment highlights Google's confidence in India's digital economy and its rapid growth in apps and software platforms. The investment aims to expand internet access beyond English and other regional languages and includes a focus on artificial intelligence and education.

title: Google announces $10bn investment in 'digital India'
summary: Google has announced a $10 billion investment in India over the next five to seven years through its Google for India Digitisation Fund. This funding aims to boost India's digital infrastructure, help businesses go digital, and leverage technology for social good, reflecting Google's confidence in the country's growing digital economy. The investment comes shortly after India banned several Chinese apps, creating a potential void for Silicon Valley giants to fill.

title: Google to launch 3 more tech certificates on Coursera
summary: Google is launching three new tech certificates on Coursera in data analytics, project management, and user experience design, costing $49 a month and taking three to six months to complete. These certificates aim to help workers affected by the coronavirus pandemic find jobs, with Google funding 100,000 need-based scholarships and considering completion equivalent to a four-year degree for relevant internal roles. This initiative expands on Google's existing IT support certificate program and includes plans for a hiring consortium, apprenticeships, and integration into high schools and community colleges.

title: Google faces lawsuit over tracking in apps even when users opted out
summary: Google is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging that it tracks user activity on hundreds of thousands of mobile apps, even after users have disabled "Web & App Activity" tracking in their Google account settings. The lawsuit, filed by Boies Schiller Flexner, claims Google uses its Firebase software to collect this data for product improvement and ad personalization, violating federal wiretap and California privacy laws. This is the second such lawsuit from the firm against Google, following an earlier claim about Chrome's Incognito mode tracking.

title: Barr condemns Disney and Hollywood for 'kowtowing' to China | William Barr
summary: US Attorney General William Barr criticized Disney and other Hollywood studios for allegedly "kowtowing" to the Chinese Communist Party, accusing them of prioritizing short-term profits over American values. Barr highlighted instances where Disney reportedly apologized for a film about the Dalai Lama and allowed Chinese officials a role in Shanghai Disneyland, while Hollywood studios allegedly tweaked scripts to appease Beijing. He also extended his criticism to US technology companies, calling them "pawns of Chinese influence" for their operations in China.

title: Veteran VC Kittu Kolluri has $216 million more to invest through his new firm, Neotribe
summary: Kittu Kolluri, co-founder of Neotribe, has closed a second fund totaling $216 million, significantly up from their $130 million debut. Neotribe focuses on investing in early-stage companies with breakthrough technologies and aims to fill a gap in the venture capital landscape, investing between $2.5 million and $5 million. Kolluri emphasizes their conviction-based approach, working closely with founders, and focusing on deep tech, data science, and engineering to solve complex problems in enterprise IT, robotics, diagnostics, and clean energy.

title: Uber pledges to double company’s Black leadership by 2025
summary: Uber Technologies Inc. has pledged to double its Black leadership by 2025, joining other tech giants in setting measurable goals for racial and economic justice. The company will also implement anti-bias training, tie executive compensation to diversity metrics, and support Black-owned businesses. This initiative follows the company's 2019 diversity report, which showed Black leaders made up only 3.3% of those with a director title or higher, despite Black employees representing 9.3% of the total U.S. workforce.

title: Global digital and social media usage July 2020 — everything you need to know
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of global digital and social media usage in July 2020, highlighting increased digital activity due to the pandemic. Key findings include over half the world now using social media, evolving search behaviors with a rise in image recognition and social network influence, and the enduring impact of WFH and video conferencing. It also covers milestones for Instagram and LinkedIn, challenges for TikTok after an Indian ban, and sustained growth in e-commerce.

title: Lloyds bank buys into cloud-native payments
summary: Lloyds Banking Group is investing in and collaborating with fintech firm Form3 to develop a cloud-native payments as a service (PaaS) platform. This initiative is part of a £300m project aimed at modernizing its IT infrastructure, improving payment processes, and accelerating the development of new products and services. The bank's broader digital transformation strategy also includes significant deals with Google Cloud and Microsoft to enhance technology access, software development, and employee productivity.

title: Gold Is Within Striking Distance of Its All-Time High. Here’s How to Play the Rally
summary: The article discusses gold's rally, nearing its all-time high, driven by the ongoing pandemic, global stimulus packages, and the overvaluation of tech stocks. Author Frank Holmes suggests that the precious metal is in a secular bull market and recommends a 10% portfolio weighting in gold and precious metals. He also highlights the strong performance of precious metal miners and royalty/streaming companies.

title: Equinix expands HK4 footprint in Hong Kong
summary: Equinix has completed the third phase expansion of its HK4 data center in Hong Kong, investing US$51 million to add 1,000 cabinets, bringing the facility's total to 1,500. This expansion is part of a multi-year plan, with another 3,000 cabinets scheduled for future phases. The move comes amid increased demand for interconnection, though also in the wake of a controversial new security law in Hong Kong, which has prompted some tech firms like Naver to relocate data.

title: Boyd Gaming unveils mobile gaming app with nostalgic brand
summary: Boyd Gaming Corp. has launched a new mobile gaming app called Stardust Social Casino, leveraging its vintage Las Vegas Stardust brand to stand out in the competitive mobile gaming market. The app offers virtual versions of slot titles found on Boyd Gaming casino floors, primarily for entertainment, and allows members of its B Connected loyalty program to earn points for in-app purchases. This move aims to connect with existing customers and attract new players familiar with the historic Stardust brand.

title: Banking on AI: RBC Builds a DGX-Powered Private Cloud
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) has built an NVIDIA DGX-powered private cloud to enhance its AI capabilities and transform client experiences, leveraging a strategic investment in AI through its research institute, Borealis AI. This new infrastructure allows RBC to run thousands of simulations and analyze millions of data points rapidly, enabling the development of smart applications and significant savings in total cost of ownership. The initiative showcases RBC's commitment to innovation and its early adoption of emerging technologies to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services industry.

title: Alibaba Cloud helps Chinese students, foreign schools scale Great Firewall
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd's cloud division is offering a service to foreign universities to help their mainland Chinese students bypass the Great Firewall, allowing access to online classes and materials. This initiative, which leverages Fortinet's licensed networking technology, aims to address the challenges students face due to China's internet controls, especially since many returned home during the coronavirus pandemic. Alibaba Cloud views this as a new growth opportunity, despite the sensitive political climate, and emphasizes its purely technological solution for educational continuity.

title: Next-generation search engines want to bring back our privacy
summary: CodeFuel's new private search engine, Privado, in partnership with Microsoft, aims to offer users true anonymity by encrypting keywords and hiding identities. This initiative comes as consumers, particularly younger generations, increasingly demand greater privacy from tech giants. Privado seeks to provide targeted advertising based only on current searches, without building user profiles, and plans to explore voice and image search in the future.

title: Photo Editing App Market to See Booming Growth | Adobe, Google LLC, Lens Distortions, LLC.
summary: The global Photo Editing App Market is projected for booming growth, driven by the increasing professional photography career paths, rising digital transformation, and demand for special effects in media. Key players analyzed in the market study include Adobe Inc., Google LLC, and Corel Corporation. The report provides an overview of market insights, trends, growth factors, and the impact of COVID-19 on the industry.

title: Google Taps Dr Pepper, Spills Cloud Services, Pushes Edge With Orange
summary: Google Cloud has unveiled new services, a multi-year deal with Keurig Dr Pepper, and a partnership with Orange aimed at strengthening its position against Microsoft Azure. The new services focus on cloud migration and security, while the deal with Keurig Dr Pepper involves migrating their data centers to Google Cloud. The partnership with Orange will focus on 5G, mobile edge computing, and AI to develop new business services in Europe.

title: Google Cloud Implements Multi-Year Digital Transformation Initiative with Keurig Dr Pepper
summary: Google Cloud has signed a multi-year agreement with Keurig Dr Pepper to migrate the beverage giant's entire data footprint to Google Cloud. This initiative involves retiring two data centers and moving over 1,000 physical servers to virtual machines, supporting Keurig Dr Pepper's digital transformation to an agile IT operations infrastructure. The company chose Google Cloud for its stability, flexibility, innovation, and security, utilizing services like Live Migration to ensure minimal disruption during the transition.

title: Google Cloud announces three new marquee customers
summary: Google Cloud has secured three significant new customers: Wipro Ltd., Keurig Dr Pepper Inc., and Orange SA. Wipro is migrating its core ERP system and adopting G Suite. Keurig Dr Pepper is moving its entire data footprint to Google Cloud and retiring two data centers. Orange is partnering with Google for data, AI, and cloud computing to build a next-generation analytics platform and offer 5G-based edge computing services in Europe.

title: Apple CEO Cook says his company is "uniquely American" with no "dominant market share"
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook will testify before the House Judiciary's Subcommittee on Antitrust, where he plans to argue that Apple is a "uniquely American company" that operates in a competitive marketplace without dominant market share. He will highlight the fierce competition in the smartphone market from companies like LG, Samsung, Huawei, and Google, and defend the App Store's model as beneficial for developers. Cook will assert that Apple has never increased its commissions and that its fees are comparable to or lower than those of competitors.

title: Google Cloud Implements Multi-Year Digital Transformation Initiative with Keurig Dr Pepper
summary: Google Cloud announced a multi-year agreement with Keurig Dr Pepper to host the beverage giant's data footprint, migrating over 1,000 physical servers from two data centers to virtual machines on Google Cloud. This digital transformation aims to enhance operational efficiencies and IT infrastructure scalability, leveraging Google Cloud's innovation and security. Keurig Dr Pepper utilized Google Cloud's Live Migration service for a seamless transition, highlighting the critical role of data in business transformation.

title: Apple tried to lure Amazon's video app by offering a lower 15% fee, email shows
summary: An email released by the House Antitrust Subcommittee revealed that Apple offered Amazon a reduced 15% revenue share for Amazon Prime Video subscriptions signed up through the app, a departure from Apple's standard 30% fee. This suggests that large companies may be able to negotiate more favorable business terms on the App Store, contradicting Apple's public statements about treating all developers equally. The revelation came during a Congressional hearing on Big Tech where Apple CEO Tim Cook testified.

title: HAPSMobile Successfully Completes Latest Test Flight of Its Unmanned Aircraft Designed for Stratospheric Telecommunications Platform Systems
summary: HAPSMobile Inc., a SoftBank Corp. subsidiary, announced the successful completion of its fourth test flight for the "Sunglider" solar-powered high-altitude platform system (HAPS) on July 23, 2020, at Spaceport America in New Mexico. This flight confirmed all basic aircraft tests for the UAS, enabling HAPSMobile to proceed with preparations for stratospheric test flights. The Sunglider reached higher altitudes for longer durations than previous flights and successfully passed all test points, demonstrating significant progress in its mission to bridge the digital divide.

title: Here’s what the CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook and Alphabet will say at Wednesday’s antitrust hearing
summary: The CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook, and Alphabet are scheduled to testify before a House antitrust panel on Wednesday. Their prepared statements indicate they will argue that competition exists and their companies strengthen America. The executives, including Jeff Bezos, Tim Cook, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sundar Pichai, will appear via videoconference.

title: Alphabet Inc’s Expenses Rise As Earnings Drop In Second Quarter
summary: Alphabet Inc. reported a 2% year-over-year revenue drop to $38.9 billion in Q2 2020, its first in company history, yet still managed to beat analyst estimates. The revenue decline was primarily due to decreasing net sales in Google Search, while operating costs increased significantly, leading to a substantial drop in operating income. Despite these challenges, YouTube ad and non-ad revenues, along with Google Cloud, showed growth, and Traffic Acquisition Costs decreased.

title: Apple smashes revenue estimates in record third quarter
summary: Apple significantly surpassed revenue expectations in its fiscal third quarter, reporting a record $59.7 billion, an 11% increase year-over-year. This surge was driven by increased demand for iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers as consumers adapted to working and learning from home during the pandemic. The company also announced a four-for-one stock split and confirmed a slight delay for the next iPhone launch.

title: Apple Announces 4-1 Stock Split After Shares Surge Toward $400
summary: Apple Inc. announced a 4-for-1 stock split following a significant surge in its share price over the past year. The company stated this move aims to make the stock more accessible to a broader base of investors, with post-split trading beginning on August 31. This marks Apple's fifth stock split since going public in 1980, contrasting with other large tech companies that typically avoid such actions.

title: Alphabet Inc (GOOG) (GOOGL) Q2 2020 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: This is a transcript of Alphabet Inc.'s Q2 2020 earnings call. CEO Sundar Pichai and CFO Ruth Porat discuss the company's performance during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting a decline in advertising revenue but strong growth in non-ad sectors like Cloud, Google Play, and YouTube subscriptions. They also cover strategic investments in AI, commerce initiatives, and efforts to support users and businesses during the global economic uncertainty.

title: How Google is making it easier to identify Black-owned businesses
summary: Google has rolled out a new feature allowing Black-owned businesses in the U.S. to identify themselves on Google Maps and Search with an orange-striped badge. This initiative, supported by the U.S. Black Chambers, Inc., aims to increase visibility and support for these businesses, following CEO Sundar Pichai's commitment to the Black community and a surge in searches for Black-owned businesses. The company previously introduced similar badges for women-owned and LGBTQ+-friendly businesses.

title: Looking to drive sales of Nest devices, Google invests $450M in security firm ADT
summary: Google is investing $450 million in security company ADT Inc. for a 6.6% stake, aiming to boost sales of its Nest devices. This strategic partnership will combine Google's Nest technology with ADT's extensive security solutions for homes and small businesses. The deal is expected to increase consumer awareness and customer base for Nest products, as ADT professionals will sell and install devices like Nest Cameras and Nest Hub Max.

title: BBVA USA announces collaboration with Google to offer digital bank accounts
summary: BBVA USA announced a collaboration with Google to offer co-branded, FDIC-insured digital bank accounts through Google Pay, expected to launch in 2021. This partnership aligns with BBVA's strategy to expand its digital offerings and enhance customers' financial health by leveraging its existing infrastructure and Google's user experience capabilities. Both companies believe this collaboration will benefit consumers by combining financial expertise with technology.

title: BBVA USA anuncia un acuerdo con Google para ofrecer cuentas digitales en EE. UU.
summary: BBVA USA, the U.S. subsidiary of BBVA, has announced a partnership with Google to offer digital bank accounts through Google Pay, scheduled for 2021. This collaboration aligns with BBVA's strategy to enhance digital offerings and leverage its innovation in finance to improve customers' financial health, with Google providing the client interface and user experience. The accounts will be FDIC-insured and leverage BBVA's existing technological infrastructure and 'open banking' initiative.

title: BMO signs deal to offer digital chequing accounts in U.S. through Google Pay
summary: Bank of Montreal (BMO) has partnered with Google to offer digital chequing accounts in the U.S. via Google Pay, joining an initiative launched by Google last November. This collaboration allows BMO to expand its customer reach through Google's platform, offering financial insights and budgeting tools to users, while Google benefits from banks' stability and access to financial data. This move highlights the banking industry's trend of collaborating with tech giants to counter digital disruption and leverage their vast user bases.

title: Google buys $450M stake in ADT to give Nest a new perch
summary: Google is investing $450 million for a nearly 7% stake in ADT Inc., aiming to expand the reach of its Nest cameras and voice assistant. As part of this partnership, ADT will integrate Nest's internet-connected cameras and Nest Home Hub into its security systems. This deal allows Google to further develop its home management product line and benefit from ADT's extensive customer base.

title: Tim Cook Says These 3 Words Guide Every Decision at Apple
summary: Tim Cook stated that "privacy, security, and quality" guide every decision at Apple, especially in its app review process. The article argues that these three words differentiate Apple from its competitors, particularly concerning data privacy and product experience. It emphasizes that these principles provide clarity for Apple's decisions and are foundational to its operations, serving as a lesson for other leaders.

title: Google parent Alphabet issued the largest corporate ESG bond
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet Inc., issued the largest corporate ESG bond to date, totaling USD $5.75 billion, to fund environmental and social initiatives. This bond was part of a larger USD $10 billion debt offering and achieved record-low yields. The issuance highlights a growing trend among companies to utilize ESG themes for bond differentiation and demonstrates that sustainable business practices are being rewarded by capital markets.

title: Google to buy stake in ADT in home security push for $450 million
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is acquiring a 6.6% stake in ADT Inc. for $450 million to boost its home security presence and drive sales of its Nest devices. This investment gives ADT a high-profile technology partner and access to new resources, while Google gains access to ADT's 6.5 million customers. The companies plan to integrate Google products with ADT's services and co-invest an additional $150 million each in co-marketing, product development, technology, and employee training.

title: Apple marketing chief Phil Schiller steps down from role
summary: Phil Schiller, Apple's long-serving marketing boss, is stepping down from his role but will remain with the company as an "Apple Fellow," continuing to oversee the App Store and company events. Greg Joswiak, one of Schiller's deputies, will take over as vice president of worldwide marketing. Schiller's transition marks another high-profile executive change at Apple, coming amidst increased scrutiny over the App Store's policies.

title: Google investment in ADT raises profile, competitive edge — plus data worries
summary: Google's $450 million investment in ADT Inc. will boost ADT's profile and allow it to sell and install Google's smart home devices, enhancing its competitive edge and customer experience. The partnership is expected to benefit ADT through Google's AI and data analytics expertise, although it also raises concerns about data privacy and market consolidation among tech giants.

title: Android Users Say Google Collects Data for Product Development
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Google LLC and Alphabet Inc., alleging that Google employees monitor and collect Android user data without consent for product development, specifically a potential TikTok competitor. The plaintiff, Robert McCoy, claims Google uses "Android Lockbox" technology to monitor interactions with non-Google apps and mischaracterizes the purpose of data collection, violating consumer privacy laws and breaching contracts. The lawsuit argues that Google obtains consent through vague language during device setup, not fully disclosing its extensive data collection practices for competitive advantage.

title: Gartner: IaaS Public Cloud Services Market Grew 37.3% In 2019
summary: The global infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) market for public cloud services saw a 37.3% growth in 2019, reaching $44.5 billion, with Amazon Web Services (AWS) maintaining its lead despite a slight market share decrease. Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud experienced significant growth, while Chinese providers Alibaba Cloud and Tencent also showed strong market expansion. Gartner plans to combine IaaS and PaaS into a new category called Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services (CIPS) for future reporting to better reflect market realities.

title: |【2020最新】知的好奇心を刺激するアート(芸術)系アプリのおすすめ5選
summary: This article introduces five recommended art-related apps from 2020 that stimulate intellectual curiosity. It highlights apps like "DailyArt" for daily art discovery, "Ukiyo-e Wallpaper" for Japanese art backgrounds, "Magic Poser" for 3D model drawing references, "Chirashi Museum" for event leaflets, and "Happy Color" for number-based coloring puzzles. The article details features and benefits of each app, catering to both art education and entertainment.

title: BUSINESS INSIDER GLOBAL TRENDS FESTIVAL explores the effects of Covid-19 on global business
summary: The BUSINESS INSIDER Global Trends Festival, scheduled for October 19-23, 2020, will be an exclusively online event focusing on the impact of Covid-19 on global business. It will feature prominent speakers like Reed Hastings and Nouriel Roubini, covering five main themes: Welcome to the Future, Shifting Societies, Sustainability, Technology, and Organization. The festival aims to provide a platform for discussing post-pandemic scenarios and new ways of working and interacting, with contributions from international teams across various Business Insider editions.

title: Banks and tech giants including JPMorgan and Amazon pledge to hire 100,000 minority and low-income New Yorkers
