title: PayPal Plans to Shift Core Applications to Google Cloud
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. is planning to migrate several core payment-processing applications to Google Cloud. This move is part of the company's broader strategy to host all its applications in the public cloud, responding to increased activity driven by evolving consumer spending habits. The migration will include PayPal's peer-to-peer payments, merchant checkout, bill-payment apps, and user account management.

title: DIU to Select Contractor for Secure Cloud Access Tech Soon; Zscaler’s Drew Schnabel Quoted
summary: The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) is close to selecting a secure cloud access management platform from prototypes developed by Zscaler, Google, and McAfee. This platform will facilitate collaboration between the Department of Defense and cloud service providers. Zscaler's vice president of federal, Drew Schnabel, highlighted the technology's ability to create secure connections and efficiently manage user traffic, building on Zscaler's previous engagement with DIU in June 2020 to develop a zero-trust framework.

title: Amdocs Acquires Sourced to Further Boost Communications Industry’s Move to the Cloud
summary: Amdocs has acquired Sourced Group, a leading global technology consultancy, to enhance its capabilities in helping the communications industry transition to the cloud. This acquisition expands Amdocs’ portfolio of cloud-native products and services, leveraging Sourced’s decade of experience in large-scale cloud transformations for high-end enterprises. The deal, valued at approximately $75 million in cash, is expected to be neutral to Amdocs' non-GAAP diluted earnings per share for fiscal year 2021.

title: Elasticsearch on AWS: Deploying Your First Managed Cluster
summary: This article explains how to deploy a managed Elasticsearch cluster on Amazon Web Services (AWS) using Amazon's managed Elasticsearch Service (Amazon ES). It covers the key features of Amazon ES, a step-by-step guide to creating a new domain, and methods for ingesting and searching data. Additionally, it addresses how Amazon ES manages various administrative tasks and its compatibility with open-source Elasticsearch APIs.

title: International Relocation Is Not the Only Type of Work Mobility Needed to Attract Great Talent
summary: This article discusses how workplace mobility has evolved beyond traditional international relocation, driven by technology and new work models. Belgin Ertam of GE MENAT highlights that successful companies like GE are creating diverse opportunities for employees regarding their work "place" to attract and retain talent. It suggests that a broader understanding of mobility, beyond just physical relocation, is crucial in the modern workforce.

title: Apple Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock fell 1.12% on Tuesday, closing at $124.85, amidst a broader market downturn with the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declining. This marked the stock's second consecutive day of losses, placing it $20.24 below its 52-week high. The article also notes Apple's performance compared to competitors like Microsoft, Alphabet, and IBM, all of which also experienced declines.

title: HPE bets on Europe’s Gaia-X cloud and data services initiative
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is launching its HPE Solution Framework for Gaia-X, aligning with Europe's initiative to create a unified, data-privacy-protected cloud and data services ecosystem. Gaia-X aims to reduce Europe's reliance on non-European cloud providers by fostering an interoperable data exchange governed by European laws. HPE's framework, built on the HPE Ezmeral Software Platform, will help companies participate in this decentralized environment, emphasizing secure data operations and allowing businesses to maintain ownership and control over their data.

title: Don't download this Microsoft Authenticator extension for Chrome: it is fake
summary: A fake "Microsoft Authenticator" extension has been found in the Chrome Web Store, deceptively named and offered by "Extensions" rather than Microsoft. The extension, which had over 400 users, redirects to a Polish webpage asking for sign-in or account creation. Users are advised to verify the developer and details of any extension before installation, as official Microsoft Authenticator is only available as a mobile or Microsoft Store application, not a browser extension.

title: Alphabet was the most widely held stock for the largest ESG funds. Here’s what else they own
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) was the most widely held stock among the 20 largest ESG equity funds in 2020, with an average weight of 1.9%. Technology companies, including Apple and Microsoft, dominated the portfolios of these funds, accounting for the largest allocation in most, leading to their outperformance in a year where tech rallied and energy declined. While tech firms like Alphabet were favored due to meeting ESG criteria, the study also revealed holdings in other sectors, including specific energy companies and utilities, with their carbon intensity evaluated on a stock-by-stock basis.

title: Lo que necesitas saber para empezar a vender por redes sociales
summary: This article from Bancolombia provides a comprehensive guide for businesses looking to start selling on social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. It outlines the benefits of having a digital presence, offers a 5-step process for establishing business accounts on Facebook and Instagram, and highlights the features of WhatsApp Business for growth. The guide emphasizes content creation, audience interaction, sales opportunities, and performance measurement using platform analytics.

title: Where and how to buy Alphabet (GOOGL) stock
summary: This guide provides a comprehensive overview for newcomers interested in buying Alphabet (GOOGL) stock. It covers essential steps such as choosing a trading platform, funding an account, deciding investment amounts, and differentiating between buying shares or ETFs. The article also explains various order types and the importance of monitoring GOOGL's performance.

title: Why Google, Procter & Gamble veteran will lead IRI
summary: Kirk Perry, a veteran of Google and Procter & Gamble, has been appointed President and CEO of IRI. The article highlights his experienced background from major companies, signaling a new leadership direction for IRI. No further details are provided in this snippet regarding the "why" of his appointment.

title: Morgan Stanley defies bank diversity trend
summary: Morgan Stanley recently announced significant leadership changes, positioning a slate of potential successors to CEO James Gorman that is predominantly white and male, contrasting with JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s recent moves to promote women to senior roles. This decision has sparked criticism regarding diversity in leadership, despite Morgan Stanley's spokesperson stating a commitment to diverse talent and the presence of qualified women and people of color on their operating committee. The article highlights that while some progress has been made across Wall Street, top jobs continue to be primarily held by white men, prompting calls from activists and former employees for more substantial change.

title: Fortinet SD-WAN gains Megaport middle-mile connectivity
summary: Fortinet has integrated its SD-WAN platform with Megaport Virtual Edge (MVE), becoming the second SD-WAN vendor after Cisco to support this network-as-a-service offering. MVE aims to simplify branch-to-cloud connectivity by providing an edge compute offering for virtual network functions and a middle-mile transport service that improves reliability over the open internet. This partnership addresses the increasing demand for optimized middle-mile connectivity, critical for enterprises returning to offices and seeking alternatives to costly MPLS circuits.

title: Should you buy Alphabet stock now? A total of 98% of analysts consider it a ‘buy’
summary: Alphabet Inc. (Google's parent company) continues to show strong performance, with first-quarter sales increasing by 34% despite its trillion-dollar valuation. The article, which is a quarterly review from MarketWatch, suggests that investors appreciate Alphabet's high-profit margins, rapid sales growth, and robust free cash flow. A significant 98% of analysts recommend buying Alphabet stock, making it a highly favored investment.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook faces sharp questioning from judge in Epic Games trial
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook faced sharp questioning from Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers regarding Apple's App Store business model during the Epic Games v. Apple trial. The judge pressed Cook on the lack of competition in in-app purchases and expressed skepticism about Apple's Small Business Program. Cook defended Apple's policies by citing fierce competition in the smartphone market and the need for security and privacy for users.

title: Oracle debuts its first Arm-based cloud instances
summary: Oracle has launched its first Arm-based cloud instances, OCI Ampere A1 Compute, offering customers more flexibility and high performance at lower costs for general-purpose and cloud-native workloads. This move signifies Oracle's increased investment in the Arm ecosystem, providing a compelling alternative to x86-based instances and competing with rival cloud providers by offering attractive pricing and scaling options. The company is also expanding developer resources and tools to encourage Arm-based application development on its cloud platform, including free tier offerings and a new development stack.

title: Microsoft teams up with Accenture and Goldman Sachs to create energy efficient software
summary: Microsoft, Accenture, and Goldman Sachs, along with other organizations, are forming the Green Software Foundation to develop and share methods for creating software that produces fewer carbon emissions in data centers. Data centers currently account for about 1% of global electricity demand, projected to rise significantly, prompting the need for "green software engineering" skills. The foundation aims to build tools, establish standards for measuring software's climate impact, and provide training for engineers.

title: App Store Arguments
summary: This article analyzes the legal, pragmatic, duopoly, moral, and anti-steering arguments surrounding Apple's App Store, particularly in light of the Epic Games v. Apple trial. The author suggests that while Apple has a strong legal standing based on Supreme Court precedents, there are valid counterarguments regarding competition, developer relationships, and the overall health of the iOS ecosystem. The piece concludes by suggesting Apple should consider conceding some ground to developers to foster a more open and innovative environment, especially given global regulatory scrutiny.

title: HCA Healthcare partners with Google Cloud to accelerate digital transformation
summary: HCA Healthcare and Google Cloud have announced a multi-year strategic partnership to accelerate HCA Healthcare's digital transformation. This collaboration aims to create a secure data analytics platform and develop next-generation operational models, leveraging data from HCA Healthcare's 32 million annual patient encounters. The partnership will focus on improving clinical care, empowering caregivers with mobile tools, and optimizing non-clinical support areas while ensuring patient privacy and data security.

title: Apple Faces Criticism Over Its Cooperation With China
summary: Apple is facing increasing criticism for its cooperation with Chinese laws, which involve sharing consumer data and censoring content, amid a wider technological and economic competition between the U.S. and China. The article also discusses the US Senate's "Endless Frontier Act" aimed at countering China's tech advancements, China's efforts to influence Latin American and African telecom markets, and its crackdown on cryptocurrency and its own tech giants.

title: 'They have clear double standards': T V Mohandas Pai slams large social media platforms
summary: T V Mohandas Pai, former CFO of Infosys, criticized large social media platforms like WhatsApp for having "double standards" regarding user privacy. He stated that the Indian government and laws, not private platforms, should define and protect citizens' privacy. Pai's comments came in response to WhatsApp's lawsuit challenging new Indian digital rules that require the company to provide access to encrypted messages, predicting the issue would reach the Supreme Court.

title: S&P 500 trading guide: constituents, market hours and h
summary: This guide provides an in-depth look at the S&P 500, a key benchmark for U.S. stock market performance. It covers the index's constituents, listing criteria, calculation methods, factors affecting its price, and average annual returns. The article also details various ways to trade the S&P 500, including CFDs, futures, options, and ETFs, and discusses strategies for shorting the index.

title: Women suing Google over gender bias win class-action status
summary: Four former female Google employees have won class-action status for their gender-pay disparity lawsuit against the tech giant, allowing them to represent nearly 11,000 other women. The lawsuit alleges Google pays women less than men for the same job and seeks over $600 million in damages for violations of California's Equal Pay Act. The women also claim Google's past policy of asking for prior salaries perpetuated lower pay for women.

title: Google Women Suing Over Gender Bias Win Class-Action Status
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Google failed to prevent a gender-pay disparity lawsuit from achieving class-action status. A San Francisco judge certified the class action, allowing four lead plaintiffs to represent almost 11,000 women seeking over $600 million in damages. The lawsuit alleges Google pays men more for the same job, violating California's Equal Pay Act.

title: Hundreds of Companies Unite to Oppose Voting Limits, but Others Abstain (Published 2021)
summary: Hundreds of major companies, including Amazon, Google, G.M., and Starbucks, signed a statement opposing "any discriminatory legislation" that makes it harder to vote. This initiative, organized by former American Express CEO Kenneth Chenault and Merck CEO Kenneth Frazier, marks the largest show of corporate solidarity against Republican-led efforts to enact new election rules nationwide. The move comes despite calls from senior Republicans for companies to avoid political issues.

title: AR’s role in shopping poised to swell in next 5 years, Publicis and Snap find
summary: A new study by Publicis Media, Snap, and Alter Agents indicates that augmented reality (AR) significantly influences consumer shopping habits, especially among Snapchat users who are 56% more likely to use branded AR lenses and increase their likelihood to purchase. The pandemic accelerated AR adoption in shopping, and three out of four respondents believe AR will play a larger role in retail over the next five years. Snap continues to expand its commerce capabilities, integrating AR into new features and partnerships to meet evolving consumer expectations and leverage AR's increasing utility in the shopping journey.

title: 10,800 women suing Google over gender pay disparity win class-action status
summary: A San Francisco state judge has granted class-action status to a lawsuit brought by nearly 11,000 women against Google, alleging gender pay disparity. The plaintiffs claim Google pays men more for the same job and are seeking over $600 million in damages for violations of California’s Equal Pay Act. This decision allows four lead plaintiffs to represent approximately 10,800 women in the case.

title: Yes, You Can Invest in a Tech-Less Nasdaq-100
summary: The article discusses the First Trust NASDAQ-100 Ex-Technology Sector Index Fund (QQXT), an ETF that allows investors to gain exposure to the Nasdaq-100 without the heavy technology sector allocation. This fund offers diversification away from tech and communication services while still providing growth potential and has historically outperformed the S&P 500 with less volatility. QQXT is presented as a compelling option for investors seeking growth outside of traditional tech-heavy portfolios.

title: China’s ‘Uber for Trucks’ Heads for Billion-Dollar-Plus U.S. IPO
summary: Full Truck Alliance Co., a Chinese startup providing an "Uber-like" service for the trucking industry, is planning a U.S. initial public offering. The company aims to raise at least $1 billion at a valuation between $20 billion and $30 billion, possibly raising up to $2 billion. Its prominent backers include SoftBank Group Corp.'s Vision Fund and Alphabet Inc.

title: Mountain View self-driving trucking company Aurora Innovation expanding in Dallas area
summary: Aurora Innovation, a self-driving trucking company backed by Amazon and Hyundai, is expanding its operations in the Dallas area to accommodate its growing workforce. This expansion comes less than a year after the company announced its intention to test its self-driving technology in Texas. Aurora Innovation's CEO, Chris Urmson, previously led Google's self-driving car unit.

title: NVIDIA Base Command Platform Provides Enterprises with Fast Path to Scale Production AI
summary: NVIDIA announced the Base Command Platform, a cloud-hosted development hub designed to help enterprises streamline AI projects from prototype to production. This platform, available through a monthly subscription with NetApp, offers access to NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD AI supercomputers and NetApp data management. Google Cloud plans to integrate the platform into its marketplace, promoting a hybrid AI experience.

title: KKR, CD&R Strike $5.3 Billion Deal to Buy Cloudera
summary: Private-equity firms KKR & Co. and Clayton Dubilier & Rice LLC have agreed to acquire software company Cloudera Inc. for approximately $5.3 billion, taking the company private. The deal values Cloudera at $16 per share, representing a 24% premium over its closing price on the preceding Friday. Cloudera, founded by engineers from major tech companies, struggled to adapt to the public cloud market, facing stiff competition from larger firms.

title: KKR, CD&R take data analytics firm Cloudera private for $4.7 bln
summary: Private equity firms Clayton Dubilier & Rice LLC (CD&R) and KKR & Co (KKR.N) are taking cloud-based data analytics company Cloudera Inc (CLDR.N) private for $4.7 billion. Cloudera's shares jumped 23.9% following the announcement, nearing the offer price of $16 per share. The move is intended to help Cloudera transition more smoothly into hybrid cloud solutions without the pressure of quarterly reporting.

title: Explainer: Tesla drops radar; is Autopilot system safe?
summary: Tesla has transitioned its Autopilot system to a camera-only approach, eliminating radar sensors, which raises concerns about safety and performance in various conditions. While Tesla CEO Elon Musk believes the vision-only system is safer due to less "noise" from radar, many in the industry and safety groups are skeptical, emphasizing the benefits of combining multiple sensor types, like cameras, radar, and lidar. Safety ratings bodies are re-evaluating their labels for newly configured Tesla vehicles.

title: Microsoft’s Irish subsidiary posted £220bn profit in single year | Tax havens
summary: Microsoft's Irish subsidiary, Microsoft Round Island One, recorded a profit of $315 billion (£222 billion) in a single year, which is nearly three-quarters of Ireland's GDP, despite having no employees other than directors. The company is resident for tax purposes in Bermuda, which has no corporation tax, allowing it to pay no tax on income. This news emerged as G7 finance ministers discussed global minimum corporate tax rates to combat multinational tax avoidance.

title: Whirlpool Corporation Migrates SAP Systems to Google Cloud for Sustainable Growth
summary: Whirlpool Corporation has expanded its strategic collaboration with Google Cloud by migrating its enterprise-wide SAP environment and applications to Google Cloud's secure, reliable, and sustainable infrastructure. This move aims to provide global teams with low-latency access to SAP systems and data, support future growth with elastic cloud infrastructure, and contribute to Whirlpool’s commitment to reaching net-zero emissions by 2030. The migration leverages Google Cloud's capabilities in AI, machine learning, and analytics, while ensuring business systems run on carbon-neutral infrastructure.

title: Apple is turning privacy into a business advantage, not just a marketing slogan
summary: Apple is increasingly integrating privacy measures into its products and services, differentiating itself from competitors. Recent announcements include features like email tracking prevention, IP address obfuscation, and burner emails, all under the umbrella of iCloud+. The company leverages its self-designed chips and on-device processing capabilities to enhance privacy and introduce new functionalities in areas like health and digital identity, reinforcing user trust and opening new market opportunities.

title: Apple's new 'private relay' feature will not be available in China
summary: Apple announced that its new "private relay" feature, designed to enhance user privacy by obscuring web browsing behavior, will not be available in China due to regulatory reasons. This decision represents another compromise by Apple in a country that is a significant market for the company, following previous adjustments like moving iCloud data keys to China. The feature, which routes web traffic through multiple servers to prevent tracking, will also be withheld in several other countries.

title: Google Moves to Dismiss Class-Action Lawsuit over Refusal to Redeem Gift Cards
summary: Google has filed a motion to dismiss a class-action lawsuit alleging that it refuses to redeem Google Play gift cards in violation of California law. The company argues that its terms of service include a forum selection clause requiring disputes to be resolved in Santa Clara County, California, and that the claims made by the plaintiffs are not viable under California's Gift Certificate Law. Google also suggests that individual class members should be verified.

title: NetApp Simplifies and Accelerates the Journey to Hybrid Cloud
summary: NetApp has released new ONTAP software and hybrid cloud portfolio enhancements designed to reduce costs, complexity, and unify data management across on-premises and public cloud environments. The updates provide flexible foundations for hybrid cloud, simplify data management, and offer cloud-like financial flexibility through services like the NetApp Keystone Flex Subscription at Equinix. These innovations aim to help enterprises modernize their IT, manage data, and accelerate their digital transformation journeys.

title: Cognizant forms new business group dedicated to Google cloud
summary: Cognizant has established a new Google Business Group (GBG) to accelerate clients' cloud modernization journeys, expanding its existing relationship with Google Cloud. This initiative aims to combine their service capabilities and solution development to meet evolving business needs, particularly in vertical markets like retail, life sciences, healthcare, and financial services. The GBG will leverage industry solutions, data analytics, AI, process automation, and application modernization.

title: NetApp brings ONTAP updates to simplify hybrid Cloud Data Management
summary: NetApp has updated its ONTAP data management software to enhance features and simplify hybrid cloud data administration. This move aligns with NetApp's "cloud-first" strategy, aiming to unify managing public and on-premises cloud environments for better data access. The updates are expected to simplify storage procedures, improve management ease for IT administrators, and enhance overall performance and data protection capabilities.

title: TCL 5-Series Roku TV (S535) review: A killer QLED TV value
summary: The TCL 5-Series Roku TV (S535) offers a strong 4K quantum-dot picture and built-in Roku smart features at a very competitive price, making it an excellent budget-friendly option. While it excels in color accuracy and gaming response time, its brightness and sound quality are moderate. This TV is highly recommended for those seeking a quality QLED experience without breaking the bank.

title: Waymo, J.B. Hunt test robo-trucks in Texas
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. and Waymo are partnering to test human-supervised, self-driving trucks for cargo delivery between Houston and Fort Worth, Texas. This initiative aims to gather data on the operation of automated trucks within J.B. Hunt's network, exploring the potential for increased efficiency and enhanced safety, while acknowledging the continued need for human drivers. The collaboration comes as the trucking industry faces driver shortages and investigates automated technology to address future operational needs.

title: On Sundar Pichai's Birthday, 5 Little-Known Facts About The Google CEO
summary: This article highlights five lesser-known facts about Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Google and Alphabet Inc., on his birthday. It covers his educational background with multiple degrees, his love for football and cricket, his career before Google at Applied Materials and McKinsey, his college love story with Anjali, and his consideration for the CEO position at Microsoft before Satya Nadella was chosen.

title: Zoom and Salesforce make quick $23 million profit after IPO of Israeli software vendor Monday.com
summary: Zoom and Salesforce each invested $75 million into Monday.com's IPO, quickly realizing a combined profit of $23 million as the stock jumped 15% on its debut day. This investment strategy is part of a larger trend for Salesforce Ventures, which has yielded significant gains from other IPOs like Snowflake, while Zoom is also beginning to use investments as a new business venture. Both companies are subject to a 180-day lock-up period before they can sell their shares.

title: Waymo Via Partners With J.B. Hunt to Run Robotically Driven Freight From Houston to Fort Worth
summary: Waymo Via is partnering with J.B. Hunt Transport Services to test robotically driven freight from Houston to Fort Worth using autonomous Class 8 trucking units. The test runs will cover a 262-mile haul with a human driver and technician present to monitor operations. This collaboration aims to gather data, improve efficiency, enhance safety, and explore the long-term integration of autonomous driving technology in trucking fleets.

title: J.B. Hunt, Waymo team up for self-driving deliveries in Texas
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. and Waymo, the self-driving unit of Google-parent Alphabet, announced a partnership for autonomous freight delivery in Texas. This collaboration involves using Waymo Via platform's Level 4 autonomous driving technology to haul freight between Houston and Fort Worth, supervised by specialists. The trial will help both companies gather data, define future collaborations, and explore how autonomous technology can enhance safety and efficiency in trucking.

title: How To Get HubSpot Reports Into Notion
summary: This article explains how to integrate HubSpot reports into Notion using Google Sheets as an intermediary. It details a four-step process involving Demand Sage to pull HubSpot data into Google Sheets, creating a report and chart in Sheets, and then embedding that chart into a Notion page. The method allows for dynamically updating data in Notion, overcoming the lack of native integration between HubSpot and Notion.

title: Korean firms split into new units for fair valuation amid uncertainty
summary: Major Korean companies are increasingly splitting their businesses into separate entities through spin-offs and split-offs to achieve fair valuation and secure additional funding. This trend, inspired by companies like Google's Alphabet restructuring, has seen a significant rise in the past year, with many firms experiencing stock price increases post-announcement. While beneficial for growth and attracting new talent, the process also raises concerns regarding shareholder dissatisfaction, especially with split-offs that do not distribute shares to existing shareholders, and potential discrepancies in compensation schemes.

title: LDC’s “Mastergold” Cooking Oil E-store Live on JD.com
summary: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) has launched its first-ever e-store on JD.com, a major Chinese B2C online retailer, to sell its Mastergold cooking oils to Chinese consumers. This strategic move aims to leverage China's booming e-commerce market, which presents significant growth opportunities for food brands. The online store will initially offer peanut and sunflower cooking oils, with plans to expand to a wider range including non-GMO soybean, corn flaxseed, rice bran, olive, and linseed oils.

title: Jessica Ashooh: The taming of Reddit and the National Security State Plant tabbed to do it
summary: The article discusses the controversial appointment of foreign policy hawk Jessica Ashooh as Reddit's Director of Policy in 2017. It highlights her background at the Atlantic Council and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, detailing her hawkish stances on Middle Eastern foreign policy, particularly regarding Syria. The author suggests her appointment is part of a broader trend of national security state influence over social media platforms, aiming to control content and narratives.

title: Federal data privacy legislation could benefit U.S. economy
summary: Experts argue that federal data privacy legislation is crucial for the U.S. economy, national security, and global competitiveness, especially when compared to countries like China. A unified federal law, rather than a patchwork of state laws, would strengthen relationships with foreign governments, protect against cyber threats, and facilitate international data exchange, which is vital for GDP growth and digital trade. Without a comprehensive federal approach, the U.S. risks being at a global disadvantage in the digital economy.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman On His Return-To-Work Plan: ‘If You Can Go To A Restaurant In New York City, You Can Come Into The Office’
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman has stated his firm stance on returning to the office, asserting that if employees can go to a restaurant in New York City, they can come into the office. This view aligns with other Wall Street bank CEOs like JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon and Goldman Sachs' David Solomon, who are pushing for a return to in-person work, especially for junior staff and to preserve company culture. In contrast, many tech companies are adopting more flexible hybrid work models.

title: New research shows social media has created a more
summary: New research from Sprout Social indicates that social media has intensified competition for brands, with 93% of marketers agreeing, but also serves as a critical tool for differentiation and staying ahead. The 2021 Sprout Social Index: Accelerate highlights that 90% of marketers rely on social data to gain a competitive edge, though few fully leverage this data for ROI measurement or business decisions. The study also reveals that while consumers expect strong customer service on social, marketers often deprioritize it, missing opportunities for engagement and bottom-line growth.

title: Airbnb and Booking targets of G7 push for higher taxes for multinationals and EU focus on restraining gatekeepers
summary: The article discusses how Airbnb and Booking.com are becoming targets for higher taxation and stricter regulation due to evolving international policies. The G7 summit's proposal for a 15% global minimum corporate tax and a push for multinationals to pay taxes where they sell services directly challenges current practices of these platforms, which often pay lower taxes in countries like Ireland. Additionally, the EU's Digital Services Act aims to regulate large digital platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com as "gatekeepers," potentially leading to increased complexity for hosts and greater data sharing with municipalities.

title: Google Cloud lands deal to host Johnson Controls’ resource planning platform
summary: Google Cloud has secured a deal to host Johnson Controls International plc's enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, expanding an existing partnership. Johnson Controls, a $22 billion hardware firm, will migrate its SAP SE’s ECC platform to Google Cloud, aiming for lower latency and improved sustainability. This move allows Johnson Controls to leverage Google’s global data center network and aligns with both companies' sustainability goals, with Johnson Controls also supplying cooling systems for Google's data centers.

title: Waymo announces another $2.5 billion in funding from latest investment round
summary: Waymo, the autonomous rideshare startup, has secured an additional $2.5 billion in funding, led by its parent company Alphabet Inc. This new investment aims to support staffing increases and further advance its self-driving technology, particularly as Waymo prepares for paid rides in San Francisco pending permit approvals. This funding round brings Waymo's total capital to nearly $6 billion, placing it in a competitive position against rivals like Cruise.

title: Transforming mobility with the confidence of world-class investors
summary: Waymo announced a significant investment round of $2.5 billion, backed by a diverse group of investors including Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and T. Rowe Price. This funding will be used to further advance the Waymo Driver technology and expand its team. The company emphasizes its progress in autonomous ride-hailing and freight delivery, highlighting its experience with millions of miles driven on public roads and billions in simulation.

title: Cloud-native backup benefits and use cases explained
summary: Cloud-native backup offers organizations fast, reliable, and scalable data protection for workloads on containers, VMs, and hyperscaler services. It leverages native cloud capabilities for cost-effective disaster recovery, compliance, and ransomware protection. Key benefits include automation, self-management, API-driven policy adjustments, and metadata enrichment for efficient storage and data discovery.

title: How fund managers are bracing for inflation
summary: This article explores how fund managers are adjusting their portfolios in response to rising inflation, which has surpassed central bank targets in both the UK and US. Fund managers are implementing strategies such as diversification, investing in cyclical stocks and commodities, seeking companies with strong pricing power, and utilizing real assets to protect investments against inflationary pressures. While some managers are making significant changes, others are maintaining their low-risk equity positions, acknowledging inflation as a risk but not necessarily requiring drastic portfolio overhauls.

title: IonQ quantum computing systems available through Google Cloud
summary: IonQ, a quantum computing startup, is making its 11-qubit and soon its 32-qubit quantum hardware accessible to customers via Google Cloud Marketplace. This partnership marks IonQ as the first quantum computer available on GCP, pre-dating Google's own hardware offerings, and expands the reach of quantum computing to a broader developer base. IonQ's systems are also available through AWS and Microsoft Azure, and the company recently announced a $2 billion merger to become the first publicly traded quantum computing firm.

title: New Austin Skyscraper Sold for $580 Million
summary: Kilroy Realty Corp. has acquired the newly completed Indeed Tower in downtown Austin for $580 million. The 36-story, 730,000 SF office building is currently 57% leased, with Indeed.com anchoring 42% of the space through 2034. Developed by Trammell Crow in partnership with Principal Real Estate Investors, the tower is considered a prime asset in the strengthening Austin office market.

title: Sustainable equity ETFs cut Tesla, Microsoft, and Netflix
summary: Two of Australia's largest sustainable international equity ETFs, BetaShares Global Sustainability Leaders (ETHI) and VanEck Vectors MSCI International Sustainable Equity (ESGI), have divested from Tesla, Microsoft, and Netflix due to failures in ESG screens. These divestments highlight the active decisions passive sustainable funds can make based on rigorous environmental, social, and governance criteria, contrasting with Vanguard's Ethically Conscious International Shares ETF (VESG) which continues to hold these companies. The article examines the different screening methodologies used by these funds and their impact on holdings, performance, and diversification.

title: Reducing noise and bias in investing
summary: This article examines how broad-based ETFs can effectively reduce noise and bias in investing, drawing insights from the book "Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment." It highlights that mechanical predictions are superior to human ones and that aggregating forecasts reduces noise. The author argues that diversified ETFs represent the aggregate forecasts of millions of market participants, offering a simple way to benefit from collective wisdom.

title: Google Executives See Cracks in Their Company’s Success (Published 2021)
summary: Despite record profits and a $1.6 trillion valuation, Google is reportedly facing internal criticism from executives who worry about its increasing size, bureaucracy, risk aversion, and leadership. Many current and former executives attribute these issues to CEO Sundar Pichai's leadership style, leading some to leave the company and publicly express their concerns about innovation challenges.

title: This is Grand Theft Auto as made by AI
summary: AI researchers have utilized Nvidia's GameGAN neural network to create "GAN Theft Auto," an entirely AI-generated version of Grand Theft Auto V. The playable demo showcases an AI-generated highway scene that, despite being pixelated, demonstrates impressive details like shadows and reflections, all without human-coded graphics. This project offers a glimpse into a future where entire games, or portions thereof, could be concocted by AI.

title: Mastercard Foundation Appoints Robin Washington to Board of Directors
summary: The Mastercard Foundation has appointed Robin L. Washington to its Board of Directors, while long-time member President Festus G. Mogae is retiring after 11 years of service. Washington brings extensive operational experience from her roles at companies like Alphabet, Honeywell, and as CFO of Gilead Sciences. The Foundation and its Chair, Zein M. Abdalla, expressed enthusiasm for Washington's contributions and gratitude for President Mogae's impactful service.

title: Where a cannabis company trades can have a big impact on liquidity, valuation
summary: The article discusses how the stock exchange where a cannabis company trades significantly impacts its liquidity and valuation. It highlights that U.S. plant-touching operators face lower liquidity due to restrictions on major exchanges like Nasdaq and TSX, forcing them onto smaller exchanges. Uplisting to higher-volume exchanges would substantially increase liquidity, leading to greater access to capital at a lower cost and, consequently, higher valuations.

title: What to expect from Microsoft's next version of Windows
summary: Microsoft is preparing to unveil a significant update to Windows, which a leaked build suggests will be called Windows 11. This new version is expected to feature design changes, including a centered taskbar and rounded window corners, along with modern features like enhanced window snapping and better multi-monitor support. Analysts are also watching for potential business model shifts, such as a "Windows-as-a-Service" offering or stronger M365 integration.

title: Wattpad & WEBTOON Merge Studio Divisions into Fan-Driven Entertainment Outfit
summary: Wattpad and WEBTOON have merged their studio divisions into Wattpad WEBTOON Studios, a new entity focused on creating fan and data-driven TV shows, films, and books. This new studio, backed by Naver with a $100 million commitment, leverages the combined audience of over 166 million people and aims to develop global hits from their extensive IP libraries. Aron Levitz will lead the new studio as President, bringing together the expertise of both Wattpad Studios and WEBTOON Studios.

title: Google delays Chrome's blocking of tracking cookies to late 2023
summary: Google has announced a delay in fully blocking tracking cookies in its Chrome web browser until late 2023, nearly two years later than initially planned. This decision comes amidst antitrust concerns from competitors and regulators, with Google citing the need for sufficient time for public discussion and for the advertising industry to adapt. The delay has positively impacted shares of companies reliant on cookies, while regulatory bodies like Britain's CMA and the EU's competition commission are actively involved in overseeing Google's changes.

title: Payoneer Is Set to Merge With FTOC, Future Looks Bright
summary: Payoneer is set to go public through a reverse merger with the SPAC FTAC Olympus Acquisition Corp. (FTOC), with common stock expected to trade under "PAYO" on Nasdaq starting June 28. The company, which provides payment services for major firms like Amazon and Google, shows strong financials with expected 2021 revenues of $432 million and a reasonable valuation, making it a potentially attractive investment. Payoneer's business was significantly boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic and the shift to online transactions, with impressive growth reported in Q1 2021, and the company has recently undergone a rebranding effort.

title: EXCLUSIVE Toyota-backed self-driving startup Pony.ai considers going public
summary: Pony.ai, a self-driving technology company backed by Toyota Motor Corp, is exploring the possibility of going public in the United States. This move would help fund its ambitious goal of commercializing driverless ride-hailing services, aiming to integrate its technology into tens of thousands of vehicles by 2024-2025. The company's CEO, James Peng, highlighted the significant funding required for long-term development in autonomous driving, especially with the recent appointment of Lawrence Steyn as CFO to accelerate growth and deployment.

title: How Western Union is fighting back against fintech startups
summary: Western Union, a long-standing player in cross-border payments, is actively combating competition from fintech startups by heavily investing in its digital operations. The company saw significant growth in digital money transfer revenues in 2020 due to the pandemic-driven acceleration towards digital services, and expects revenues to exceed $1 billion in 2021. Western Union is also expanding its offerings beyond payments, including launching a bank account, debit card, and multicurrency accounts in Europe, and modernizing its technology using cloud platforms and AI.

title: Breaking Down 'BLOK': Inside This ETF's Portfolio
summary: The Amplify Transformational Data Sharing ETF (BLOK) demonstrated its active management prowess by capitalizing on crypto market volatility in May, mitigating losses despite its high correlation to Bitcoin. BLOK strategically narrowed its holdings and increased exposure to digital platforms and exchanges, which typically thrive during periods of extreme market fluctuations. The ETF, with over $1 billion in AUM, focuses 80% of its portfolio on companies involved in blockchain technology but does not directly invest in cryptocurrencies.

title: How Salesforce, Amazon, Google measure climate impact
summary: This article discusses how companies like Salesforce, Amazon, and Google are measuring their climate impact and the challenges involved. It highlights the increasing pressure on companies to demonstrate sustainability efforts through trusted data and metrics, moving beyond just reporting to actively using data to drive decarbonization. The piece also emphasizes the importance of internal communication, incentives, and policymaker involvement in achieving climate goals.

title: Nvidia integrates Arm processors with its 5G edge infrastructure platform
summary: Nvidia has announced the integration of Arm processors into its Nvidia Aerial A100 AI-on-5G platform, expanding its capabilities for 5G applications at the network edge. This move provides more choice for users, as the platform previously supported only x86-based CPUs from Intel. Additionally, Nvidia is partnering with Google LLC to establish an AI-on-5G Innovation Lab, aiming to accelerate the adoption and development of solutions on this combined AI and 5G platform.

title: A lot of laid-off and furloughed workers launched startups last year, according to Salesforce
summary: A Salesforce survey revealed that a significant number of laid-off and furloughed workers launched startups in 2020, often out of necessity due to COVID-19 related job losses. These "pandemic entrepreneurs" frequently adopted digital-first methodologies, with many businesses being direct-to-consumer and operating with minimal initial capital. The trend contributed to a 24% increase in new small businesses created in 2020 compared to 2019.

title: Southeast Asia’s most valuable company has an edge in the battle of the super-apps: Its gaming business
summary: Sea Limited, Southeast Asia's most valuable company, leverages its highly profitable gaming division, Garena, to fund the rapid expansion of its e-commerce platform, Shopee, and digital financial services arm, SeaMoney. This strategy gives Sea a significant advantage over rivals like Grab and GoTo in the competitive super-app market, allowing it to offer aggressive incentives and capture market share even while operating at an overall loss. The article details Sea's history, its founder's vision for mobile-first services in emerging markets, and the challenges and opportunities facing the company as it seeks sustained profitability and dominance.

title: Rigetti looks to scale up quantum computing with modular processor architecture
summary: Rigetti Computing Inc. is addressing the challenge of scaling quantum computers with a new modular architecture that links smaller qubit collections to function as one processor. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of building larger, single quantum chips that are prone to failure and low manufacturing yields. The company expects to make an 80-qubit system available on its Quantum Cloud Services platform later this year, believing this modular strategy offers the fastest path to practical quantum applications.

title: Digital ad firm Taboola closes down 2% on first day of trading
summary: Digital ad company Taboola began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker "TBLA" after merging with ION Acquisition Corp. 1. The company, which specializes in content recommendation boxes on the "open web" outside of Google and Facebook, saw its shares close down 2% on its first day of trading. Taboola aims to be a leading recommendation engine, expanding beyond articles to e-commerce, videos, and other devices.

title: PayPal phishing attack uses legitimate services to bypass Google Workspace security
summary: A new PayPal phishing scam is effectively bypassing Google Workspace security by leveraging legitimate services like GoDaddy and Glitch. The attack uses social engineering and brand impersonation, exploiting PayPal integrations to trick victims into providing credentials on a fake login page. Experts recommend augmenting native email security with additional threat detection layers, and emphasize the importance of multifactor authentication and robust password management.

title: Euro Tax Flash from KPMG's EU Tax Centre
summary: KPMG's Euro Tax Flash reports on the historic agreement reached by 130 countries in the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS 2.0, aiming to reform international tax rules with a two-pillar approach. Pillar One reallocates taxing rights for large companies to market countries, while Pillar Two establishes a global minimum tax rate of at least 15%. The article also discusses potential EU implementation challenges and notes that some countries, like Ireland, have reservations about certain aspects of the agreement.

title: Google must face Voice Assistant privacy lawsuit -U.S. judge
summary: A federal judge ruled that Google must face much of a class-action lawsuit alleging illegal recording and dissemination of private conversations through its Voice Assistant. Plaintiffs claim Google uses "false accepts" of hot words for targeted advertising, violating privacy rights and contractual agreements. The judge allowed most claims to proceed, emphasizing that Google's privacy policy did not adequately disclose the use of recordings made without intentional activation.

title: 'Abuse of dominance': Was this what Congress originally intended for Section 2?
summary: The article discusses a potential shift in U.S. antitrust enforcement, moving toward stricter policing of single-firm dominance, akin to the European "abuse of dominance" standard. This change is influenced by Senator Amy Klobuchar's proposed legislation and President Biden's appointment of Lina M. Khan to the FTC, reflecting concerns about the market power of technology giants. The author argues that this renewed approach to antitrust law may align more closely with the original intent of the Sherman Act, which historically sought to prevent concentration of power.

title: Embrace Investing in Momentum With the ProShares QQQA ETF
summary: The ProShares Nasdaq-100 Dorsey Wright Momentum ETF (QQQA) is a new ETF that launched in mid-May, focusing on Nasdaq-100 stocks with the greatest potential to outperform. The fund utilizes a momentum-based investing philosophy, specifically Dorsey Wright's "Relative Strength" measure, and an equal-weight construction to identify top-performing companies. This Q&A with Simeon Hyman from ProShares explains the fund's unique approach and its benefits for investors seeking diversification and exposure to innovative companies.

title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter and Google over social media bans
summary: Former US President Donald Trump has filed class-action lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google, as well as their chief executives, aiming to overturn his social media bans and seek punitive damages. Trump argues that these tech giants, by banning him, are violating First Amendment rights and should be considered government actors due to their liability protections under Section 230. The lawsuits follow his permanent ban from Twitter and a two-year suspension from Facebook after the January 6 Capitol riot, reigniting debates about Section 230 and social media censorship of conservative viewpoints.

title: Trump sues tech firms for blocking him, and fund-raises off it. (Published 2021)
summary: Former President Donald J. Trump sued Facebook, Twitter, and Google, and their CEOs, after being banned or blocked from their platforms. He announced a class-action lawsuit, arguing wrongful censorship and calling it a "very beautiful development," while his political operation immediately began fundraising off the news. Legal experts expressed skepticism about the suit, particularly its arguments that tech firms are "state actors" and that Section 230 is unconstitutional.

title: SOC Prime Mentioned as a Detection Content Provider in the 2021 Gartner, SIEM Magic Quadrant
summary: SOC Prime, a leader in Detection as Code, has been recognized for the second consecutive year in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM). The company's platform helps organizations improve SIEM and EDR detection capabilities, supporting 9 SIEM vendors identified in the Gartner report. This recognition also highlights the growth of the Sigma project, a de-facto standard for threat detection queries.

title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter and Google, claiming censorship
summary: Former U.S. President Donald Trump has filed lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google, along with their chief executives, alleging unlawful censorship of conservative viewpoints. The lawsuits, seeking class action status, claim the social media companies violated First Amendment rights and also ask a judge to invalidate Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. These legal actions follow the companies' decisions to suspend Trump's accounts after the January 6th Capitol riot, citing violations of policies against glorifying violence.

title: News Corp. closes Knewz aggregator site
summary: News Corp. has shut down its news aggregation service, Knewz, just 18 months after its launch. The platform, which aimed to offer diverse news content as an alternative to Google and Facebook, cited a lack of profitability as the reason for its closure despite attracting millions of users. News Corp. stated that Knewz served as an important proving ground for technology that will continue to benefit its other businesses.

title: Reddit Upvotes The Land Down Under
summary: Reddit has officially launched its Australian operations with a new office in Sydney, recognizing Australia as its fourth-largest user base and a key part of its international growth strategy. The new team includes dedicated Community, Engineering, Sales staff, and Country Manager David Ray, aiming to build on strong organic user growth and establish local brand partnerships. Australian Reddit users are highly engaged, spending more time on the platform than on Instagram, Snapchat, Twitter, and Pinterest, and show popularity for local communities alongside global trends.

title: HCA AND THE FUTURE OF HEALTHCARE
summary: This article discusses HCA Healthcare's partnership with Google Cloud for digital transformation, its controversial past involving fraud and an insider trading scandal, and its subsequent comeback through strategic acquisitions and a return to public markets. It analyzes HCA's financial performance, growth strategies, and future prospects, especially concerning expanding into new healthcare markets like senior living and outpatient care. The author evaluates whether HCA stock is a good buy, considering its aggressive expansion, debt management, and potential long-term growth despite short-term revenue concerns.

title: Google is in the hottest antitrust seat, but Apple and the rest of Big Tech shouldn't breathe easy
summary: Google is currently facing its fifth government antitrust lawsuit in the U.S., specifically concerning Android and its app store, making it a primary target in global Big Tech investigations. Despite Google's prominent position, antitrust experts anticipate more inquiries into other major tech companies following President Joe Biden's recent executive order addressing competition in the tech industry. This indicates a broad governmental consensus that Big Tech poses a significant problem.

title: BIPOC and women employees ranked their CEOs: These were the top 10 for 2021
summary: A new Comparably survey reveals the top CEOs as ranked by their BIPOC and women employees in 2021, based on 10 million anonymous ratings. Eric Yuan of Zoom Video Communications topped the list for BIPOC employees, while Shantanu Narayen of Adobe ranked highest among women. The rankings also highlight a significant shift compared to previous years and note the limited presence of female CEOs at the very top.

title: ZoomInfo acquires Chorus.ai for $575M to expand its sales intelligence platform
summary: ZoomInfo Technologies Inc. has announced the acquisition of sales analytics startup Chorus.ai Inc. for $575 million. Chorus.ai uses AI to analyze sales conversations, providing insights to improve sales team productivity and detect market changes. This acquisition is part of ZoomInfo's strategy to expand its sales technology market presence and enhance its go-to-market platform.

title: Partial victory for Sonos and EIP against Google over consumer electronics
summary: Sonos has achieved a partial victory against Google in a patent dispute concerning consumer electronics control technology. The Munich Regional Court dismissed Google's infringement lawsuit against Sonos, while the Hamburg Higher Regional Court upheld a preliminary injunction filed by Sonos against Google. This marks an escalation in their ongoing global patent battle.

title: Spotify’s Top Lawyer Has Spent Years Making Apple the Bad Guy
summary: Horacio Gutierrez, Spotify’s chief legal officer, has been a key figure in the ongoing antitrust battle against Apple. Having previously defended Microsoft in an antitrust case, Gutierrez has now switched sides and led Spotify's campaign, aiming to portray Apple as an abusive monopolist. His efforts have contributed to a significant shift in public perception regarding Apple's business practices, making it a target for antitrust scrutiny alongside other tech giants.

title: A complete guide to Amazon stock
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Amazon stock, discussing its performance, market position, and how investors can trade it. It highlights Amazon's primary revenue streams (retail, subscriptions, and AWS), the company's valuation, and key factors investors should consider before trading AMZN shares, such as its growth-over-profit strategy and the importance of AWS.

title: Why is Tesla incorporated in Delaware?
summary: This article explains why a disproportionate number of companies, including Tesla, Amazon, and Google, are incorporated in Delaware despite not being headquartered there. Key reasons include flexible corporate law, the efficient Court of Chancery, favorable tax treatment for out-of-state income, and a long-standing state focus on business formation. The article also touches on the challenges this presents for regional data and business coverage.

title: Bell Canada taps Google Cloud to support its 5G network
summary: Bell Canada has partnered with Google Cloud to accelerate its digital transformation and enhance its 5G network infrastructure. The multiyear collaboration will leverage Google's expertise in multicloud, data analytics, and AI to improve operational efficiencies, deliver consistent customer experiences, and support Bell's goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2025. This partnership highlights Google Cloud's continued success in securing major enterprise clients.

title: Microsoft says Israeli group sold tools to hack Windows
summary: Microsoft and Citizen Lab reported that an Israeli company called Candiru sold software tools to hack Microsoft Windows and other widely used software platforms like Google Chrome. These tools were allegedly used to target civil society organizations, including a Saudi dissident group and an Indonesian news outlet, in countries like Iran, Lebanon, Spain, and the UK. Both Microsoft and Google have since patched the vulnerabilities exploited by Candiru's tools.

title: Beware of the Sugar Rush: Thoughts on the Google Chrome 3rd Party Cookie Announcement
summary: Google's decision to delay the sunsetting of third-party cookies in Chrome should not lead to complacency for marketers and media owners. Instead, this extra time should be utilized to develop robust first-party data strategies and enhance contextual targeting solutions. The article emphasizes that a cookieless future is inevitable and acting now will create a more sustainable and trustworthy online ecosystem.

title: It's ‘very dangerous’ to invest in stocks and bitcoin right now, long-time bear David Tice warns
summary: Long-time bear David Tice, known for his bearish bets, warns that investing in stocks and bitcoin is "very dangerous" due to an overvalued market, rising debt, and strange treasury market behavior. He suggests investors avoid pursuing small gains that risk a significant pullback, especially in Big Tech and FAANG stocks. Tice, who turned bearish on bitcoin, now advocates for investing in gold and silver mining companies, believing they offer protection against fiat money and significant growth opportunities.

title: Zoom to buy cloud-based call center operator Five9 in $15 bln deal
summary: Zoom Video Communications announced its largest-ever acquisition, an all-stock deal to buy cloud-based call center operator Five9 Inc for $14.7 billion. This strategic move aims to expand Zoom's offerings beyond video conferencing into the $24 billion contact center market, enhancing its presence with enterprise customers. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2022, with Five9 becoming an operating unit of Zoom.

title: Raleigh tech firm Bandwidth is betting millions on a full return to the office
summary: Raleigh tech firm Bandwidth is committing millions to an in-person, five-day-a-week office model, a contrast to the prevailing hybrid work trend in the tech industry. CEO David Morken believes this is crucial for preserving company culture, backing this conviction with a new headquarters featuring a Montessori school for employees' children, and stating that productivity increased with remote work, but the company prioritizes "presence". The company is not mandating COVID-19 vaccines but is encouraging vaccination and will continue to hire over 1,000 workers.

title: EU and China Announce Greenhouse Gas Reduction Plans
summary: The EU and China have announced significant plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The EU's plan involves cutting reliance on fossil fuels, imposing taxes on imports from high-emitting countries, and increasing renewable energy goals. China launched a domestic cap-and-trade style emissions market, doubling the global emissions covered under such a program.

title: Honda Ditches Go-It-Alone Strategy to Make Safer Move Toward EVs
summary: Honda Motor Co. is changing its long-standing strategy of avoiding major strategic alliances as it moves toward electric vehicles. CEO Toshihiro Mibe stated that going it alone would be too risky and forming alliances is crucial for mass production and cost reduction, especially in software development for EVs. This shift follows Honda's commitment to phase out gasoline-powered vehicles by 2040 and comes after previous collaborations with General Motors Co.'s Cruise LLC.

title: 4 best practices for big data security in cloud computing
summary: Securing big data in the cloud is crucial due to the vast amounts of sensitive information involved. This article outlines four best practices for big data security in cloud computing, including architectural design, least privilege tactics, data encryption, and continuous monitoring. These strategies help businesses protect data integrity, prevent theft, and ensure regulatory compliance in cloud environments.

title: Joker Joking in Google Play
summary: Zscaler's ThreatLabz team detected a new variants of the Joker malware family targeting Android devices. This spyware, known for stealing SMS, contacts, and subscribing victims to premium services, continues to bypass Google Play's vetting process by changing its code and retrieving techniques. The team identified 11 unique samples across various app categories, collaborating with Google to remove them while warning users against third-party app stores.

title: Kotak Global Innovation Fund of Fund Review
summary: The Kotak Global Innovation Fund of Fund, which invests in the Wellington Global Innovation Fund, is reviewed in this article. The author advises investors to avoid this fund despite its recent outperformance due to high expense ratios and the fund's short history, suggesting alternatives like the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund for international market exposure. The fund invests in global companies driving innovation and structural growth trends.

title: Microsoft acquires security start-up CloudKnox
summary: Microsoft announced its acquisition of CloudKnox, a security start-up that develops software to help companies manage and reduce access permissions to their cloud resources. This acquisition is part of Microsoft's broader strategy to expand its security business, which has seen over $10 billion in revenue in the prior 12 months. CloudKnox's software functions across Microsoft Azure, Amazon, and Google public clouds, identifying and removing unused permissions and flagging unusual activity to prevent security breaches.

title: The Home Depot and Google Cloud Expand Partnership to Enhance the Interconnected Shopping Experience
summary: The Home Depot and Google Cloud have extended their multi-year partnership to enhance the retailer's digital transformation and improve customer shopping experiences in physical and digital environments. Building on Google Cloud's expertise since 2015, The Home Depot leverages AI, ML, and data analytics for features like "Rent Online, Pick Up In Store," predictive inventory management, and voice search. The collaboration aims to provide scalability and personalized experiences for customers and associates.

title: Palo Alto Networks, Google Cloud Announce Intrusion Detection System
summary: Palo Alto Networks and Google Cloud have introduced Cloud IDS, a new network threat detection service built on Palo Alto Networks' Threat Prevention security service. Cloud IDS is designed to provide granular application-level visibility of traffic within a virtual private cloud (VPC) and detect various network-based threats. This service supports industry-specific security compliance and can be integrated with existing security solutions for automated responses.

title: Home Depot Extends Google Cloud Deal
summary: Home Depot Inc. has announced it is extending its multiyear cloud-services deal with Google Cloud. This decision comes after a period of explosive online sales during the pandemic, with the home-improvement chain attributing the cloud's capabilities to helping it respond quickly to changing market trends. The partnership aims to expand the digital tools that supported rocketing demand from DIY customers and professional contractors.

title: Rackspace Layoffs, Offshore Strategy Buried in 'Growth' Announcement -
summary: Rackspace Technology announced plans to invest up to $75 million in growth, while simultaneously conducting layoffs affecting 10% of its workforce and shifting job responsibilities offshore. The company's press release focused on growth and financial guidance, but an SEC filing revealed the "termination" of employees and the backfilling of roles in offshore service centers. This led to criticism of Rackspace's "overly ambitious PR spin" for obscuring the job cuts despite increasing financial forecasts.

title: Facebook, Google and Snap stocks rocket to records as online ad market heats up
summary: Facebook, Google, and Snap Inc. stocks reached record highs Friday due to a surge in digital ad sales. This surge was signaled by better-than-expected earnings reports from Snap and Twitter, indicating a strong recovery in the online advertising market. Snap was a particular standout, exceeding revenue expectations significantly and seeing its shares jump 23.9%.

title: Young Indian investors warming up to clean energy ETFs: Report
summary: A report by Globalise indicates that young Indian investors are increasingly interested in clean energy ETFs, alongside growth-oriented technology funds. The ARK Innovation ETF, Renaissance IPO ETF, Small Cap Growth Vanguard ETF, Invesco WilderHill Clean Energy ETF, and Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 were among the top ETFs in demand. Young investors, particularly from states like Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Delhi, and Karnataka, are seeking to diversify their portfolios through global investing platforms.

title: ACO Tech to add Spotify app to Proton GKUI soon?
summary: ACO Tech, the company behind Proton's GKUI infotainment system, hinted at new entertainment app additions, with strong speculation pointing to Spotify. While Google and Waze apps are unlikely due to Google's collaboration policies, ACO Tech teased an upcoming app starting with 'S' and stated they are "working with other entertainment applications." The company also suggested its own system is moving beyond mobile phone ecosystems like Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for future entertainment and lifestyle experiences.

title: FTC changes course on prior approval for reattempted mergers
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has voted to rescind a 1995 policy statement, allowing them to routinely require prior approval for reattempted mergers and prior notice for mergers below the Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) threshold. This move, initiated by FTC Chairman Lina Khan and following President Biden's executive order, aims to bolster protections against unlawful mergers and acquisitions by removing the need for new, time-consuming investigations into deals previously deemed anticompetitive. While supported by a 3-2 vote, Commissioner Noah Phillips expressed concerns that ignoring market changes could hinder normal market operations.

title: FTC votes 5-0 to examine privacy practices of internet service providers and mobile broadband providers
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has unanimously voted to examine the privacy practices of internet service providers (ISPs) and mobile broadband providers in the United States. They have issued letters to major providers, including AT&T, Comcast, Google Fiber, T-Mobile, and Verizon, demanding special reports within 45 days. The FTC seeks to understand how these companies collect, store, and share user data, and whether deceptive practices are impacting consumer privacy, particularly concerning differentiated service levels based on data collection consent.

title: The Energizer Bunny Taps SAP Software to Power Finance Transformation
summary: Energizer Holdings Inc. announced its adoption of RISE with SAP, implementing SAP S/4HANA for central finance on Google Cloud to streamline finance transformation, manage future mergers and acquisitions, and bolster product strategy. This move is expected to automate essential business processes, improve customer service, and fuel innovation, strengthening Energizer's global leadership.

title: As global demand for microchips surges, tech giants go all-in on Israel
summary: Amid a global surge in microchip demand and a component shortage, major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Intel, and Nvidia are establishing or expanding chip design operations in Israel. The country is benefiting from its strong R&D capabilities and skilled workforce in semiconductor design. This trend is attracting increased venture capital investment, despite challenges like a shortage of engineers and rising salaries.

title: Apple's iPhone expected to drive sales, but App Store faces regulatory risk
summary: Apple is projected to see significant growth driven by 5G iPhone sales and its services, particularly the App Store and Apple Music. However, the company faces substantial regulatory risks and lawsuits concerning its App Store practices, including potential legislation to reduce commissions and scrutiny over search engine payments. Analysts anticipate high iPhone sales for the fiscal third quarter, which currently overshadow these regulatory concerns, though the services sector's growth has contributed to Apple's higher valuation.

title: Check Point CloudGuard Improves Google Cloud Security with Exciting New Capabilities for Managed Instance ...
summary: Check Point CloudGuard has introduced significant enhancements for Google Cloud security, focusing on automation and ease-of-use with Managed Instance Groups (MIGs). The updates allow CloudGuard to seamlessly integrate with dynamic MIG functionalities for inbound, outbound, and East-West traffic, including auto-scaling and automatic health check responses. A key improvement is the adoption of Google Cloud's symmetric hashing, which eliminates the need for Source NAT (SNAT) in East-West traffic inspection, thereby improving performance and preserving the true source IP for applications.

title: Element bolsters decentralized team messaging with $30M raise
summary: Element, a company behind an end-to-end encrypted team messaging platform powered by the Matrix protocol, has raised $30 million in Series B funding. This funding comes from notable backers including Skype cofounder Jaan Tallinn's Metaplanet, Automattic, Protocol Labs, and Notion. The investment highlights the growing importance of decentralized, open-source communication solutions amidst major acquisitions like Salesforce's Slack takeover and increasing concerns over data sovereignty and privacy.

title: HP To Acquire Teradici: ‘Huge Asset’ In Remote Computing Push
summary: HP Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Teradici, a high-performance remote computing software firm, to bolster its offerings in virtual computing technologies for the hybrid work market. Teradici's technology enables secure and high-fidelity remote access to computing, including for graphics-intensive workloads, and is platform-agnostic. This acquisition aims to complement HP's PC business with software and services, integrating well with solutions like Microsoft's Windows 365, and expanding opportunities for HP's channel partners.

title: On the Move with Growth Stocks: 'QQQA' Rides Large Cap Momentum
summary: The ProShares Nasdaq-100 Dorsey Wright Momentum ETF (QQQA) is presented as a smart beta ETF that uses a momentum strategy to select top-performing, equal-weighted companies from the Nasdaq-100 Index. Despite holding only 21 securities, QQQA is considered more diversified than the broader Nasdaq-100 and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), particularly in its allocation to FANMAG companies and across various sectors, including a recent increase in healthcare exposure. The article highlights QQQA's unique approach to portfolio construction through momentum investing and equal-weighting to achieve diversification within a growth-focused universe.

title: YouTube is a proven juggernaut that rivals Netflix in the streaming wars
summary: YouTube is emerging as a significant contender in the streaming wars, with its ad revenue growing at a much faster rate than Netflix's overall revenue. Despite the focus on subscription services, YouTube's substantial growth in ad revenue and increasing viewership on television sets position it as a key rival to traditional paid streaming platforms. The platform also shows potential for further expansion, with its short-form video service, YouTube Shorts, gaining traction and a large portion of the population still on traditional TV, offering ample room for all streamers to grow.

title: Vittorio Cretella left school at 17 to join the Italian Army. Now he’s CIO at Procter & Gamble.
summary: Vittorio Cretella, CIO of Procter & Gamble, discusses his unconventional career path from the Italian Army to leading digital transformation at the $300+ billion CPG company. He emphasizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in hiring, along with the pervasive role of digital transformation, machine learning, and cloud adoption in P&G's strategy. Cretella also highlights his work with NPower, a non-profit helping veterans and underserved youth find careers in tech, and P&G's neurodiversity hiring program.

title: Google founders have sold $1 billion in stock since May, the most since 2017
summary: Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin have sold over $1 billion worth of stock combined since May 2021, marking their first sales since 2017. Their stock sales, totaling more than $1.07 billion, occurred after the company's share price nearly tripled and Alphabet reported strong second-quarter earnings. Despite stepping down from executive roles in 2019, Page and Brin remain board members and control a majority of Alphabet's voting shares.

title: How SAP and Deutsche Boerse Are Paving the Way to the Public Cloud for the Finance Industry
summary: SAP and Deutsche Boerse have collaborated to create a framework for secure and compliant hosting of sensitive financial data in the public cloud, addressing the strict regulatory requirements of the financial sector. This solution, based on SAP Data Custodian, allows financial service providers like Deutsche Boerse to maintain full control over their data, ensure data sovereignty, and protect sensitive information while leveraging the scalability and agility of cloud technology. The initiative aims to enable more financial institutions to move critical operations to the cloud, overcoming concerns about security and compliance.

title: Zoom Agrees To Settle A Privacy Lawsuit For $85 Million
summary: Zoom has agreed to an $85 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit alleging privacy violations, including sharing user data and issues with "Zoombombing." The telecommunications company denies wrongdoing but will increase security measures and offer refunds or payments to affected users, pending judicial approval. This settlement follows a significant increase in Zoom's user base during the pandemic, which brought increased scrutiny to its platform's security and privacy.

title: Google’s upcoming plans for Israel: a server farm and fiber optics network
summary: Google is significantly expanding its operations in Israel following being awarded a government tender for cloud computing. This expansion includes establishing a server farm in the Sharon region and rolling out an ultra-high-speed fiber optics network, complementing its existing subsea cables. These investments aim to ensure maximum availability of Google's services, improve local internet infrastructure, and enhance Google's presence as a global telecommunications provider.

title: Twitter partners with AP, Reuters to battle misinformation on its site
summary: Twitter has announced partnerships with The Associated Press and Reuters to combat misinformation on its platform. This collaboration aims to provide credible information more quickly, especially during breaking news events, by adding accurate context to tweets. This initiative marks the first time Twitter has formally partnered with news organizations to elevate accurate information on its site.

title: Baxter extends Amazon Web Services collaboration to support new digital health, data management projects
summary: Baxter is expanding its long-term partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to focus on new digital health tools, supply chain efficiency, and deeper insights from business operations. This collaboration aims to enhance its DoseEdge software, improve supply chain responsiveness through AWS analytics, and further develop remote patient management systems like its AWS-powered Sharesource platform. The move is part of Baxter's ongoing "digital transformation" and builds on its recent sales growth.

title: How to Use Snowflake to Connect Your Systems and Centralize Your Data to Prevent Customer Churn
summary: This article explains how to use Snowflake as a data hub to centralize data from various systems, such as AS400 and Salesforce, to prevent customer churn. It details the steps for connecting AWS S3 data to Snowflake using Snowpipes and integrating Salesforce data, demonstrating how a Senior Data Architect would implement this solution. The integration aims to provide a holistic view of customer information, enabling proactive measures against churn.

title: Integrating Threat Detection with XDR in Google Cloud
