summary: The article discusses the integration of Google Cloud IDS, a new intrusion detection service built with Palo Alto Networks technology, with Cortex XDR. This integration allows for enhanced threat detection at the network level within Google Cloud environments and provides a comprehensive solution for investigating and responding to security incidents by correlating logs and enabling immediate response actions. The piece also includes a step-by-step guide on how to configure this integration by setting up Pub/Sub topics, service accounts, and data collection in Cortex XDR.

title: AES, Google moonshot factory, to partner on grid virtualization platform
summary: AES is partnering with X, Google's R&D arm, to develop electric grid virtualization tools. This collaboration aims to simulate and virtualize AES' distribution grids in Indiana and Ohio, providing real-time grid insights and supporting long-range planning, especially for the integration of renewable energy and distributed energy resources. The initiative seeks to improve grid reliability and efficiency while incorporating new technologies.

title: Kroger partners with Kitchen United for ghost kitchens in its grocery stores
summary: Kroger and ghost kitchen startup Kitchen United are partnering to open ghost kitchens inside Kroger grocery stores. This collaboration aims to meet customer demand for freshly prepared meals while supporting Kitchen United's expansion. The first location is set to open in a Ralphs store in Los Angeles, featuring multiple restaurant brands for pickup or delivery.

title: NVIDIA maintains dominant position in 2020 market for AI processors for cloud and data center
summary: NVIDIA maintained its dominant position in the 2020 global market for AI processors used in cloud and data centers, holding an 80.6% share of global revenue. The company generated $3.2 billion in cloud and data center AI processor revenue, up from $1.8 billion in 2019, primarily due to its leadership in GPU-derived chips. Omdia predicts that alternative suppliers will gain significant market share in the coming years despite NVIDIA's current advantage.

title: Verily, Colgate-Palmolive to conduct study on link between oral health and diabetes, cardiovascular disease
summary: Verily, Alphabet's life science subsidiary, is partnering with Colgate-Palmolive to research the connection between oral health and overall health, specifically focusing on diabetes and cardiovascular disease. The study will be integrated into Verily's Baseline Health Study and will examine the impact of intensive non-surgical periodontal therapy and home dental hygiene. Participants must be at least 18 years old and have prediabetes, Type 2 diabetes, and/or cardiovascular disease.

title: Austria’s Nuki wants to replace physical keys with smartphones; raises €20M and plans to hire 100+ people
summary: Nuki, an Austrian company specializing in smart home access solutions, has raised €20M in a new funding round with new investor Cipio Partners and existing investors. The company aims to replace physical keys with smartphone-controlled access and plans to hire over 100 new employees. Funds will be used to develop new products and technologies, including the "Smart Door" for direct integration in new buildings, and to expand its market leadership in Europe.

title: YouTube sets TV data deals with Comscore, Parrot Analytics
summary: YouTube, YouTube TV, and Google TV have announced new data deals with Comscore and Parrot Analytics. Comscore will integrate YouTube and YouTube TV measurement into its cross-platform service to provide marketers with better audience consumption data, including co-viewing. Concurrently, YouTube and Google TV will leverage Parrot Analytics' global audience demand data to inform programming decisions for their ad-supported streaming services and connected TV platforms.

title: comScore, inc (SCOR) Q2 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: comScore (SCOR) reported its Q2 2021 earnings, highlighting the completion of its recapitalization transaction as a turning point for growth and product investment. Despite lingering pandemic effects on some products, the company saw increased total contract value year-over-year and significant growth in its Activation business (up 65%). Key announcements included an expanded integration with Google Ad Data Hub for cross-platform advertising measurement, and new partnerships for cookie-free targeting and global audience measurement, with expectations for revenue growth in the second half of 2021.

title: Global Quantum Computing Market to Reach $411.4 Million by 2026
summary: The global quantum computing market is projected to grow significantly, reaching $411.4 million by 2026 from $112.6 million in 2020, driven by increased funding, rising cybercrime, and adoption in emerging technologies like AI and machine learning. The report highlights critical applications in material simulation, optimization, and end-use sectors such as space and defense, with the U.S. and China leading market growth. This expansion is supported by government initiatives and investments in infrastructure across major geographies.

title: Unity buys remote desktop streaming app Parsec for $320M, its biggest acquisition yet
summary: Unity Software Inc. is acquiring remote desktop provider Parsec Cloud Inc. for $320 million, marking its largest acquisition to date. This move underscores Unity's ambition to expand beyond video game development and attract more creators to its platform, leveraging Parsec's remote desktop streamlining capabilities for real-time 3D experiences. The acquisition coincides with Unity reporting strong second-quarter financial results, beating Wall Street's expectations with a 48% increase in revenue year-over-year.

title: Workday selects Google Cloud as a preferred cloud partner
summary: Workday Inc., a provider of financial and human capital management software, has chosen Google Cloud as a preferred cloud partner. This partnership will allow Workday customers in various industries to deploy Workday applications directly on Google's cloud infrastructure, giving them more deployment choices. The agreement follows recent reports of scalability issues for Workday's software with large customers like Amazon Web Services and the State of Maine.

title: Oracle targets data warehouse rivals with automated features for HeatWave MySQL service
summary: Oracle has enhanced its HeatWave MySQL service with new machine learning-based automation features, dubbed MySQL Autopilot, to improve performance and target rival analytical engines from Amazon, Google, and Snowflake. The company claims these features make queries significantly faster and more cost-effective. Additionally, Oracle introduced MySQL Scale-out Data Management and increased HeatWave cluster size, aiming to monetize its widely used MySQL engine through a managed service offering.

title: HP Delivers Ultimate Chrome OS Experiences for Life and Work in Today's Hybrid World
summary: HP Inc. has expanded its Chrome OS ecosystem with the introduction of the HP Chromebook x2 11 and the HP Chromebase 21.5 inch All-in-One Desktop, along with the HP M24fd USB-C Monitor. These new devices are designed to offer versatility and mobility for hybrid work and family use, featuring innovations like the first Chromebook detachable powered by Snapdragon 7c and the first Chromebase All-in-One with a rotating display. The company emphasizes sustainable design in its new lineup, reflecting a focus on environmental responsibility.

title: Antisemitism Watchdog Gives Corporate Giants Failing Grades in Handling of Antisemitism
summary: Stop Antisemitism released a report grading major U.S. corporations on their handling of antisemitism, giving "F" grades to Google, Unilever, and Cigna for various shortcomings. The report criticized Google for not firing an employee with a problematic past statement and omitting antisemitism from diversity standards, Unilever for Ben & Jerry's stance on "Occupied Palestinian Territory" and lack of Jewish representation in diversity policies, and Cigna for similar omissions. Only L'Oreal and American Eagle Outfitters received "A" grades for proactive measures against antisemitism and fostering Jewish employee groups, respectively, highlighting a general failure of corporations to protect Jewish employees and address rising antisemitism.

title: What's Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services
summary: This article analyzes the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services (CIPS), highlighting key movements and strategies of the seven leading providers: Alibaba Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, and Tencent Cloud. AWS maintains its dominant leadership, with Microsoft and Google also holding strong positions in the Leaders quadrant by focusing on operational databases, big data, and edge computing, respectively. The report details the evolving strategies of Visionary and Niche Players, including Alibaba's expansion beyond Asia, Oracle's commitment to its cloud infrastructure, IBM's restructuring to focus on hybrid/edge computing, and Tencent's investment in network capabilities for gaming.

title: U.S. lawmakers introduce bill to rein in Apple, Google app stores
summary: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators has introduced a bill aiming to curb the market control of app stores operated by Apple and Google. The proposed legislation would prevent these companies from forcing app developers to use their payment systems or penalizing those offering different prices elsewhere. This move comes amidst ongoing scrutiny and legal challenges regarding the practices and commission fees of Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store.

title: Gusto goes with $175m series E round
summary: Gusto, a US-based human resources technology provider backed by Alphabet and Salesforce, has completed a $175 million Series E funding round, valuing the company at $9.5 billion. The round was led by T Rowe Price Associates and included participation from new and returning investors such as Fidelity Management and Research Company. Gusto provides a platform for small businesses to manage HR, payroll, tax, and employee benefits, having previously secured significant funding rounds from various corporate and financial investors.

title: Shopify Names New Legal Leadership, Adds Government Affairs Head
summary: Shopify Inc. has appointed Erin Zipes and Vivek Narayanadas as vice presidents of legal to lead its legal team after the departure of its former chief legal officer. The company also hired Maryam Mujica, a former executive at Google and Twitter, as vice president of global government affairs. These new leadership roles come as Shopify's market capitalization reached $200 billion in July.

title: Pony.ai Reportedly Seeks Funds at $8 Billion Value Amid Listing Halt
summary: Pony.ai is reportedly seeking a new funding round to raise $500 million to $1 billion, potentially valuing the self-driving startup at $8 billion, after pausing its U.S. listing plans. The decision to halt the listing comes amid Beijing's crackdown on technology companies and overseas listings. Pony.ai, with Chinese origins, aims to strengthen its financial position to compete with rivals like GM's Cruise and Alphabet's Waymo in the self-driving technology sector.

title: Allbirds is One of the Latest Brands Facing a Lawsuit Over its Sustainability-Centric Advertising
summary: Allbirds is facing a class-action lawsuit alleging its sustainability-centric advertising is "false, deceptive and misleading." The lawsuit claims the footwear brand misrepresents its carbon footprint assessment, animal welfare practices, and transparency, leading consumers to pay more for products based on inaccurate "eco-friendly" claims. This case is part of a growing trend of lawsuits challenging corporate sustainability claims, signaling a shift in legal accountability for such marketing.

title: Kroger kicks off pickup partnership with Google
summary: Kroger has partnered with Google to integrate pickup service functionality into Google Maps for 96 stores across Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana, with plans for further expansion. This allows shoppers to manage their orders, receive reminders, and notify stores of their arrival directly through the app. The initiative aims to enhance convenience, attract new shoppers, and capitalize on the surge in online grocery demand driven by the pandemic and the spread of the delta variant.

title: Samsung Has Its Own AI-Designed Chip. Soon, Others Will Too
summary: Samsung is utilizing AI-designed chips developed with Synopsys's new software, DSO.ai, for its Exynos processors, marking a significant step in the semiconductor industry. This innovative approach, also being explored by companies like Google, Nvidia, and IBM, leverages reinforcement learning to automate and accelerate the complex chip design process, potentially leading to novel designs and improved performance. While AI-driven design is currently expensive, experts anticipate it will become a standard tool in the future.

title: Tales of a human CAPTCHA solver
summary: The author, Dan Woods, describes his experience working as a human CAPTCHA solver for a Russian company called 2Captcha to understand how cybercriminals bypass these security measures. He explains that CAPTCHAs, once effective, are now merely a "speed bump" for advanced bots and human click farms, frustrating legitimate users more than adversaries. The article highlights the surprisingly legitimate business structure of these services, their low pay for solvers, and the need for more effective fraud prevention methods beyond CAPTCHAs.

title: Google Infringed on Patents Owned by Sonos, a Trade Judge Says
summary: A U.S. International Trade Commission judge issued a preliminary finding that Google infringed on speaker-technology patents held by Sonos, potentially leading to an import ban on several Google products made in China. Sonos, which sued Google in 2020, is seeking to block imports of products like Google Home smart speakers and Pixel phones. Google disputes the ruling, while Sonos's chief legal officer stated that Google has infringed on over 150 of its patents.

title: Scared of flying commercial? Private flights and short-range jets are skyrocketing during the pandemic
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a significant surge in private flights and short-range jet travel, as individuals seek alternatives to crowded commercial airports. Affluent travelers are increasingly using membership carriers, luxury charters, and fractional ownership programs for more personalized and health-conscious journeys. This trend is also fueling growth in regional airports across California, with plans for expansion and new routes, and some companies envisioning a future of greener, more affordable short-haul air travel powered by new technologies.

title: Google infringed five Sonos patents
summary: A U.S. trade judge has ruled that Google infringed five patents belonging to Sonos, related to smart speakers and associated technology. This preliminary decision by the U.S. International Trade Commission could potentially lead to a ban on imports of Google's smart speakers and Pixel phones. Sonos expressed satisfaction with the ruling, which they see as validation of their claims of patent infringement by Google.

title: Music distribution startup Distrokid hits unicorn status with Insight Partners funding
summary: Distrokid, an online music distribution startup, has achieved unicorn status after receiving new funding from Insight Partners, valuing the company at $1.3 billion. Founded in 2003, Distrokid allows musicians to upload unlimited music to various online stores and streaming services for a flat annual fee, while retaining 100% of their earnings. The company claims to distribute over a third of all new music globally.

title: Wipro's former COO Bhanumurthy Ballapuram joins Google Cloud
summary: Bhanumurthy Ballapuram, former President and COO of Wipro Ltd., has joined Google Cloud as Vice President for the Japan and Asia Pacific region. This appointment is part of Google Cloud's strategy to intensify its competition with rivals Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services in the cloud-computing market, amidst its ongoing expansion and executive hiring. Ballapuram will work with regional leadership to further Google Cloud's enterprise momentum and customer success.

title: Arch Capital appoint high flyers to board
summary: Bermuda-based Arch Capital Group Ltd has appointed Francis Ebong and Eileen Mallesch to its board of directors. Mr. Ebong brings extensive technology and innovation experience from Alphabet's X and Facebook, while Ms. Mallesch offers over 30 years of finance and risk expertise including senior leadership roles at Nationwide and other significant board positions. These appointments aim to enhance the board's capabilities in fintech transformation and broaden its talent and outlook for future growth.

title: Arch makes double director appointment
summary: Arch Capital Group has appointed Francis Ebong and Eileen Mallesch as directors to its board, effective immediately. Ebong brings expertise from Alphabet and Facebook in program management and global operations, while Mallesch has a 30-year career in finance and risk, including CFO roles and board memberships. The additions are expected to enhance the board's capabilities in areas like fintech transformation and to broaden its talent and outlook for future growth.

title: DC and Webtoon partner to bring DC superheroes to 75 million mobile users
summary: DC and Webtoon Entertainment, Inc. are collaborating to create several standalone webcomic series featuring DC superheroes, specifically formatted for mobile viewing. This partnership aims to reach Webtoon's 72 million global users and introduce DC characters to a new generation of fans, without requiring prior knowledge of existing DC continuity.

title: MicroSectors™ Launches FANG & Innovation ETNs, 'BULZ' & 'BERZ'
summary: REX Shares, LLC announced the launch of two new MicroSectors Exchange Traded Notes (ETNs), BULZ and BERZ, issued by the Bank of Montreal. These ETNs are linked to the Solactive FANG Innovation Index, which tracks major U.S.-listed tech and internet/media companies. The products aim to offer sophisticated investors leveraged and inverse leveraged exposure to prominent technology and innovation stocks.

title: Step into Mary Berg’s Kitchen! New Original Culinary Series, MARY MAKES IT EASY Premieres Sept. 6 on CTV Life Channel
summary: CTV Life Channel is launching a new culinary series, "MARY MAKES IT EASY," hosted by two-time Canadian Screen Award-winner Mary Berg, premiering on September 6th. The series aims to simplify cooking with practical recipes and tips to solve common kitchen dilemmas, with accompanying exclusive content available online. Stonemill Bakehouse is joining as a series partner, featuring their breads in several recipes and related promotional content.

title: GDS Q2 results: Company acquires data center campus in Beijing, developing in Macau
summary: GDS Holdings reported increased revenues and losses in Q2, with revenues up 38.9 percent to RMB1.86 billion ($288.7 million) and net loss at RMB298.5 million ($46.2 million). The Chinese data center company expanded significantly, bringing six new data centers online, starting construction on five more, and acquiring facilities in Beijing and Shenzhen. GDS is also extending its reach into Hong Kong and Macau, with a new 20MW data center planned for Macau and a 7,200 sqm facility in Hong Kong.

title: Apple’s Proposed Protections Against Child Predators — a Challenge to Privacy?
summary: Apple announced a new system to identify child predatory content in its photo cloud, sparking varied reactions from law enforcement, child protection groups, and privacy defenders. The system involves on-device scanning of iCloud Photos using an algorithm to detect known child abuse images, raising concerns among critics about potential privacy invasions and governmental pressure to expand surveillance capabilities. The article discusses the technical implementation, immediate reactions, and the broader implications for Apple's long-standing commitment to user privacy amidst new challenges.

title: Big Tech Is in a Perilous Moment. The Stocks Are Unstoppable.
summary: Despite significant regulatory scrutiny, major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Facebook have demonstrated unstoppable stock performance. During the April to June quarter, these five giants collectively generated $332 billion in revenue, a 36% increase year over year, with all reporting better-than-expected profits. Interestingly, most of their stocks sold off slightly after the positive earnings announcements.

title: With Amazon MemoryDB, AWS takes aim at Redis in the cloud
summary: AWS has launched Amazon MemoryDB for Redis, a new managed Redis-compatible in-memory database service. This service aims to compete with existing offerings from Redis, Google, and Microsoft by providing high performance and low latency for Redis users within the AWS cloud. While Redis acknowledges the competition, it emphasizes its differentiated enterprise functionality and multi-cloud deployment options.

title: Youtube says it has paid out more than $30 billion to online creators
summary: YouTube announced it has paid out over $30 billion to content creators in the past three years through ads, merchandising, and other features. This move comes as competition for online content and creators intensifies from rivals like Facebook, TikTok, and Spotify. YouTube maintains its 45% ad revenue share, emphasizing growing the overall pie for creators.

title: China’s politics in command economy
summary: The Chinese government has been increasingly cracking down on its domestic tech monopolies, including blocking Ant Financial's IPO, banning Didi from app stores, and restricting the for-profit education market. These actions, which have significantly impacted stock values and economic growth, are seen as a deliberate strategy by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to tighten political control. The CCP aims to balance economic growth with maintaining its power, shifting towards greater state control and self-sufficiency in strategic industries, potentially at the cost of innovation from private enterprises.

title: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud: Which Will Pay You the Most?
summary: A Stack Overflow Developer Survey reveals that among major cloud platforms, Amazon Web Services (AWS) specialists earn the highest median salaries, followed by Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. The article highlights that professionals focusing on IBM or Oracle clouds might be at a disadvantage regarding pay, likely due to lower demand for these platforms. It emphasizes the importance of continuous learning and skill development in the evolving cloud computing landscape.

title: Like the QQQ ETF? Don't Forget About 'QQQM'
summary: This article highlights QQQM as an alternative to the popular QQQ ETF, particularly for buy-and-hold investors. QQQM tracks the NASDAQ-100 Index, similar to QQQ, but is designed to be more accessible due to a lower expense ratio and a lower share price. It emphasizes the strong performance of growth stocks, especially those in the Nasdaq 100, over the past decade.

title: Insight: A secret weapon for self-driving car startups: Humans
summary: Self-driving car startups like Cruise and Pony.ai are using human safety operators in their driverless vehicles in California, highlighting the ongoing challenges in achieving fully autonomous driving. Major players such as Waymo and even Tesla acknowledge the need for human oversight, either through in-car operators, remote monitoring, or roadside assistance, to ensure safety and build public trust. The continued reliance on human involvement suggests a scaling down of initial full autonomy ambitions to generate revenue sooner, a shift from the previous "dirty little secret" of human assistance.

title: South Korea set to curb Google, Apple commission dominance
summary: South Korea is poised to pass legislation, dubbed the "Anti-Google law," that would prevent Google and Apple from mandating their proprietary payment systems for in-app purchases, effectively stopping them from levying commissions. This move would make South Korea the first major economy to impose such restrictions on the tech giants, who currently charge up to 30% commission. The legislation has drawn criticism from Apple and industry groups representing U.S. tech companies, who argue it could risk users' privacy, reduce trust in app store purchases, and potentially violate trade commitments.

title: Elastic acquisition spree continues as it acquires security startup CMD
summary: Elastic has announced its acquisition of Vancouver-based security vendor CMD, marking its second security-related acquisition in a short period. CMD's technology provides runtime security for cloud infrastructure using open-source eBPF, and its team, including co-founders Santosh Krishan and Jake King, will join Elastic to integrate their technology into the Elastic Stack platform. This acquisition aims to enhance Elastic's security capabilities, particularly for cloud and Kubernetes environments, following its previous acquisition of build.security.

title: Alphabet’s Wing Nears 100,000th Package Delivery
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Wing subsidiary is close to delivering its 100,000th package, demonstrating rapid growth in the drone-delivery sector. The company is bullish on the long-term efficiency and profitability of drone delivery, with plans to expand operations in the U.S. and Finland. Wing anticipates that this automated delivery method will eventually be more cost-effective than traditional ground delivery.

title: Synopsys' AI-Assisted EDA Tools Aim To Cut GPU Design Costs in Half
summary: Synopsys' new AI-assisted Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools promise to significantly reduce the cost and time required for chip design, particularly for GPUs. The DSO.ai platform can optimize various aspects of chip design, potentially cutting development time from 24 months to 24 weeks and reducing costs by as much as 50%. Companies like Samsung, Google, and Nvidia are already adopting this technology, which could also democratize chip development for smaller firms.

title: Who will dominate the tech arms race?
summary: The article explores the competitive landscape of quantum computing, focusing on the race between tech giants like Google and

title: Keysight Joins Google Cloud Partner Initiative to Support Agile Orchestration of Innovative 5G Services at Network Edge
summary: Keysight Technologies (NYSE: KEYS) has partnered with Google Cloud to facilitate the agile orchestration of innovative 5G services at the network edge. This collaboration aims to help service providers transition to cloud and edge computing, enabling advanced applications like streaming media, gaming, and connected vehicles. Keysight's end-to-end solutions, built on common hardware and software platforms, will support the deployment of multi-access edge computing (MEC), network function virtualization (NFV), and AI technology within a cloud-centric 5G ecosystem.

title: Keysight Becomes a Part of Google Cloud Partner Initiative
summary: Keysight Technologies has joined Google Cloud's partner initiative to advance cloud-centric 5G ecosystems, enabling agile orchestration of 5G services at the network edge. This partnership aims to assist service providers in transitioning to cloud and edge computing for delivering advanced applications and use cases. Keysight's solutions will support the deployment of cloud-native 5G quickly and cost-effectively, catering to the increasing demand for low-latency cloud capabilities at the network edge.

title: Amazon acquisitions: What does Amazon own?
summary: This article details Amazon's extensive acquisition history, highlighting how the company expanded from an online bookstore to one of the world's most valuable companies by acquiring over 100 businesses across various sectors. It lists Amazon's largest acquisitions, such as Whole Foods and MGM, and also touches upon Jeff Bezos's other ventures outside of Amazon, like The Washington Post and Blue Origin. The article emphasizes Amazon's "need-to-win mentality" in driving its acquisition strategy.

title: World's Biggest Stock Indices | Index Fundamentals
summary: This article explains the key factors that influence the prices of major global stock indices, including the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, FTSE 100, and DAX. It highlights how economic growth, dominant sectors, index weighting methodologies, and currency strength play significant roles in their performance. The piece offers a foundational understanding for traders looking to grasp index movements.

title: How Google and Yelp handle fake reviews and policy violations
summary: This article provides a side-by-side analysis of how Google and Yelp detect and address fake reviews and policy violations. It delves into their respective automated systems, human moderation processes, and the consequences for businesses that violate their content policies, including the insights from local search marketing experts. The piece highlights Google's machine learning-first approach for prevention at scale versus Yelp's focus on review integrity with more robust punitive measures.

title: Cybersecurity giant Check Point acquires Israeli startup to protect cloud emails
summary: Cybersecurity firm Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. announced its acquisition of Israeli startup Avanan, a cloud email security provider, for an estimated $270-$280 million in cash and stocks. Avanan, founded in 2015, protects cloud collaboration solutions like Microsoft Office 365, G-Suite, and Slack from cyberattacks, with over 5,000 global clients and 2.5 million inboxes protected. This acquisition aims to integrate Avanan's technology with Check Point's existing threat prevention software to enhance cloud email security, especially in the context of increased remote work and phishing attacks.

title: Check Point buys Israeli email security co Avanan for $280m
summary: Israeli cybersecurity firm Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. has acquired email security company Avanan for an estimated $270-280 million in cash and shares. Avanan, founded in 2015, specializes in AI-based technology to detect and block malicious email links in cloud environments and has seen its valuation nearly triple since its last funding round in 2018. This acquisition aims to enhance Check Point's email protection capabilities by integrating Avanan's technology into Check Point Infinity, addressing the growing threat of cyberattacks via email and collaboration tools.

title: Arlo Offers Comprehensive Third-Party Compatibility With Amazon, Apple, Google, Samsung, And Others For Seamless Smart Home Security Experience
summary: Arlo Technologies announced enhanced compatibility for its smart home security systems with major platforms like Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Google Home Assistant, IFTTT, and Samsung SmartThings. These integrations provide users with seamless control over their Arlo devices through voice commands, notifications, and live video feeds on various smart home devices, reflecting Arlo's commitment to a robust and integrated security experience. The updates aim to offer peace of mind regardless of the user's preferred smart home ecosystem.

title: Cleaning house: how Google and Yelp handle fake reviews; Tuesday’s daily brief
summary: This article discusses how Google and Yelp combat fake reviews, highlighting their differing approaches in automated systems, human moderation, and punitive measures. It also covers the shift in Google's title creation for SERPs and the tools SEOs can use to track these changes, as well as Google's substantial payments to Apple to remain the default search engine on Safari. Additionally, the piece touches on the persistent issue of gender stereotypes in advertising despite societal progress.

title: Google, Apple forced to open app store pay systems in South Korea
summary: South Korea has become the first country to mandate that Apple and Google open their app stores to alternative payment systems, thus preventing them from forcing developers to use their proprietary online payment methods. This new legislation, known as the Telecommunications Business Act, allows users a free choice of app payment providers and could set a global precedent for how tech giants monetize their app marketplaces. The move comes as Google had planned to introduce a 30% commission fee in South Korea, reversing a long-standing exemption.

title: C3 AI Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2022 Results
summary: C3 AI (NYSE: AI) announced strong results for its fiscal first quarter ended July 31, 2021, with revenue up 29% year over year to $52.4 million and gross profit up 31% to $39.4 million. The company expanded its market-partner ecosystem, notably entering a strategic alliance with Google Cloud, and saw significant growth in its enterprise AI customer count and production application footprint across various industries. C3 AI also provided financial guidance for the second quarter and full fiscal year 2022, anticipating continued revenue growth.

title: Google Cloud & C3 AI: Enterprise AI Alliance
summary: C3 AI and Google Cloud announced a new partnership to accelerate the application of AI solutions across various industries. This collaboration involves co-selling C3 AI's enterprise AI applications on Google Cloud's infrastructure and leveraging Google Cloud's ML and data analytics capabilities. The partnership aims to address real-world challenges in sectors like manufacturing, supply chain, financial services, healthcare, and telecommunications.

title: Now Patched Vulnerability in WhatsApp could have led to data exposure of users
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) uncovered a theoretical Out-Of-Bounds read-write vulnerability in WhatsApp related to its image filter functionality. This flaw, patched in version 2.21.1.13, could have allowed an attacker to read sensitive information from WhatsApp's memory following complex user interactions, though WhatsApp found no evidence of its exploitation. The vulnerability stemmed from insufficient checks on image format and size during filter application, leading to out-of-bounds memory access with maliciously crafted image files.

title: Remember When Expedia Wanted to Reduce Its Reliance on Google? Big 180-Degree Shift Now
summary: Expedia Group, which previously aimed to lessen its dependence on Google, has now significantly increased its spending on Google paid search. A Bernstein report indicates that in the first quarter of 2021, Expedia attracted three times more traffic from paid search on U.S. desktops compared to Booking.com, Airbnb, and Tripadvisor combined, with Expedia.com exceeding its pre-pandemic paid search traffic from March 2019. The company is actively pursuing this strategy to gain market share.

title: CPR finds patched vulnerability in whatsapp could have led to data exposure of users
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) discovered a security vulnerability in WhatsApp's image filter function that could have allowed an attacker to read sensitive information from WhatsApp memory. The vulnerability, rooted in how filters were applied to specially crafted images, was reported to WhatsApp on November 10, 2020, and subsequently fixed in version 2.21.2.13. WhatsApp acknowledged the bug, designated as CVE-2020-1910, and stated that while the flaw was complex to exploit, such research helps improve user security.

title: Interview: Expanding Global Access to the DELFI Environment
summary: This interview details Schlumberger's collaboration with IBM and Red Hat to expand global access to the DELFI cognitive E&P environment. The primary goal is to provide a hybrid cloud deployment option, overcoming restrictions in regions with data sovereignty requirements or problematic connectivity issues that prevent the use of global public clouds. This partnership aims to enable more oil and gas companies, suppliers, and partners to leverage DELFI's capabilities, fostering collaboration and workflow optimization through the Red Hat OpenShift container platform.

title: Alphabet, Tesla and Amazon are among the most favourite stocks held by US-focused mutual funds. Here are top 10 stocks
summary: This article identifies Alphabet, Tesla, and Amazon as top stock holdings among U.S.-focused mutual funds available to Indian investors. It details 10 such mutual funds, highlighting their investment strategies, underlying assets, and historical performance. The funds provide Indian investors exposure to leading US companies and geographical diversification.

title: Lennox announces new integration of its iComfort thermostat
summary: Lennox has expanded the compatibility of its iComfort thermostats to integrate with various smart home automation platforms, including premium systems like Control4 and popular virtual assistants such as Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Google Assistant, and IFTTT. This integration allows users to manage their Lennox heating and cooling systems through a wider range of smart home devices, offering enhanced convenience and control over their indoor environment. Control4 customers with Lennox HVAC systems and iComfort S30, E30, or M30 thermostats can request integration through their dealer, enabling centralized control from their smart home system.

title: Qualcomm Says It Will Supply Chip For New Renault Electric Vehicle
summary: Qualcomm Inc. announced it will supply a key computing chip for the digital dashboard in Renault SA's new Megane E-TECH Electric vehicle. The chip will power the vehicle's infotainment system, utilizing software from Alphabet Inc.'s Google. This move represents Qualcomm's continued expansion into the automotive sector, following a previous deal with General Motors Co.

title: Cisco Webex Cloud Calling
summary: Webex by Cisco has achieved a record 8 billion monthly calls, supporting over 39 million cloud calling users globally, making it the leading cloud calling provider. The company has expanded its Cisco Calling Plans to include the UK, now covering over 65 countries, and introduced new innovations that offer greater flexibility and speed for enterprises migrating to cloud calling solutions. These advancements aim to unify communications for hybrid work environments, ensuring reliable and secure calling experiences embedded in daily business operations.

title: Google-backed Edtech firm bets on free math courses to add users
summary: Cuemath, an online math-course provider backed by CapitalG (Alphabet Inc.), is offering much of its content for free for a year to attract new users and compete in India's edtech market. This strategy aims to boost elementary math skills globally, especially after learning disruptions caused by Covid-19, and increase its revenue to $100 million. The company, founded by Manan Khurma, emphasizes creating learning outcomes amidst the rapid growth and significant funding rounds in the edtech industry.

title: China says no to K-pop fan culture, from bulk-buying to ‘effeminate’ boy bands
summary: China has implemented strict new entertainment regulations impacting K-pop, including bans on bulk-buying albums, paid voting on TV shows, and "effeminate" boy bands. These measures, aimed at improving fan culture and eliminating "immoral entertainers," are expected to significantly affect the revenue of Korean entertainment agencies, with stock prices already seeing declines. The full monetary impact on K-pop album sales, particularly from China which is a major market, is being assessed by securities firms.

title: Chevron to sell test batch of sustainable aviation fuel to Delta Air
summary: Chevron Corp plans to produce and sell a test batch of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) to Delta Air Lines at Los Angeles International Airport. This initiative is part of a partnership with Google to track SAF emissions data using cloud-based technology. Delta aims to replace 10% of its jet fuel with SAF by 2030, and the companies hope to create a transparent model for analyzing greenhouse gas emission reductions.

title: Amazon EKS Anywhere launches into general availability
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. has announced the general availability of Amazon EKS Anywhere, an extension of its Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service. This new service allows customers to run Kubernetes clusters on-premises using VMware vSphere, providing an installable software package and automation tools for cluster lifecycle support. EKS Anywhere, similar to Google's Anthos and Microsoft's Azure Arc, is intended to simplify Kubernetes management across both cloud and on-premises environments, addressing the need for consistent management and deployment mechanisms for hybrid cloud operations.

title: Prevent Container Risks With Advanced Container Image Sandboxing
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced new capabilities in Prisma Cloud's Cloud Workload Protection to enhance container security, particularly through advanced machine learning for pre-deployment image sandboxing. This allows developers and DevOps teams to analyze third-party container images for dynamic threats in an isolated environment before deployment. The update also expands host security for VMs on Azure and Google Cloud, improves web application and API security, and includes Red Hat certification for its vulnerability scanner.

title: Find Lost Items at Home with Alexa, Google, Xfinity, and Siri
summary: This article provides guidance on how to locate lost items within a home using various smart assistants such as Alexa, Google, Xfinity, and Siri. It covers different methods and tips for leveraging these technologies to find misplaced belongings.

title: Native Rust support on Cloudflare Workers
summary: Cloudflare Workers now officially supports writing Workers in 100% Rust, eliminating the need for JavaScript interaction. This is made possible through the new `worker` crate, which simplifies development by providing Rustacean-friendly APIs and removing boilerplate code. This development aims to simplify the developer experience on Cloudflare Workers, leveraging Rust's strengths in WebAssembly and its growing ecosystem.

title: Apple can’t force developers to use its in-app payment system, federal judge rules
summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple Inc. can no longer compel developers to use its in-app payment system, allowing them to bypass commission fees of 15% to 30%. This decision, stemming from the Epic Games Inc. case, could significantly alter how apps are distributed by dominant online platforms like Apple, Alphabet Inc. (Google), and Amazon.com Inc. However, the ruling stopped short of declaring Apple an antitrust monopolist.

title: Apple, Google, Amazon spying on you, lawsuits claim
summary: Lawsuits allege that Apple, Google, and Amazon are spying on users through their voice assistants, recording private conversations and sharing them with advertisers. A class-action lawsuit against Apple's Siri has been greenlit by a federal judge, with similar claims made against Google and Amazon. The companies deny these allegations, stating that recordings are only kept with user consent or to improve service, and offer options for users to manage their privacy settings.

title: How Navi's FoF on Vanguard US Total Stock Market ETF could add value to your portfolio
summary: Navi Mutual Fund has filed for a new Fund of Fund (FoF) that will invest in the Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund ETF (VTI), a passively managed US-based ETF with a very low expense ratio. This FoF will allow Indian investors to access the broad US equity market, including companies typically unavailable in India, potentially adding value due to low correlation with the Indian market. However, investors should be aware of debt fund taxation rules for international funds.

title: Wells Fargo picks Microsoft, Google as cloud service providers
summary: Wells Fargo & Co has selected Microsoft Corp's Azure as its primary cloud provider and Google Cloud for additional business-critical services, adopting a multi-cloud strategy. This move aligns with the bank's new digital infrastructure strategy, which involves transitioning to third-party data centers and relying more on public cloud services in the long term. Wells Fargo is the latest major bank to adopt such an approach, which offers flexibility and helps reduce the significant costs associated with operating proprietary data centers.

title: Goldman just created an equity ETF targeting future tech leaders
summary: Goldman Sachs has launched a new actively managed Equity ETF, GTEK, aimed at investing in next-generation technology companies with market values under $100 billion, primarily outside of the US megacap tech giants. The ETF seeks to help investors diversify away from the dominant FAANG stocks, identifying opportunities in global innovation, digital transformation, fintech, and semiconductors. Fund managers believe the tech landscape will shift significantly, with new leaders emerging from various sectors and geographies.

title: Microsoft (MSFT) Board Approves $60B Share Repurchase Program
summary: Microsoft's board has approved a new $60 billion share repurchase program and increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to 62 cents per share. This move follows a series of similar buyback programs initiated by the company over the past decade, with the latest coming as a previous $40 billion program is nearing its completion. The announcement is particularly noteworthy given recent efforts by Democrats to impose a tax on corporate stock buybacks, a practice that critics argue can artificially inflate stock prices and EPS.

title: Tencent Opens WeChat to Rivals’ Links as China App Walls Crumble
summary: Tencent has begun allowing WeChat users to link to rival services like Alibaba's Taobao and ByteDance's Douyin in one-on-one chats, a move aimed at complying with Beijing's directive to dismantle "walled gardens" among online giants. This is a significant step towards interoperability but is currently limited in scope, with broader sharing features still under development. The government's push seeks to curb monopolies and protect consumers by ending practices that impair the flow of commerce and control user data.

title: Delta’s Extra $200 Insurance Fee Shows Vaccine Dilemma for Employers (Published 2021)
summary: Delta Air Lines has implemented a policy requiring unvaccinated employees to pay an additional $200 per month for health insurance, starting November 1. This move, which comes after one vaccine received full federal approval, represents a distinct approach compared to companies mandating vaccines. Delta states this is to increase vaccination rates and noted that recent COVID-19 hospitalizations among its employees were all unvaccinated, costing the company approximately $50,000 per stay.

title: NC Fought Hard for Gilead’s New Site, Adding to Exploding Biotech Presence
summary: North Carolina aggressively vied with Atlanta to secure Gilead's new business services center, offering significant incentives like a nearly $10 million reimbursement. The new facility in the Research Triangle will create 275 high-paying HR, finance, and IT jobs, boosting the state's economy by an estimated $1.11 billion through tax revenue. This win further solidifies North Carolina's growing status as a major life sciences and tech hub, attracting other giants like Eli Lilly and Apple.

title: Salesforce values and culture driven innovation
summary: This article explores how Salesforce has evolved from a CRM company to a leading cloud and productivity organization, driven by its core values and culture. Field CTO Adam Spearing discusses how the company's focus has shifted towards digital transformation, accelerated by the pandemic, and highlights key acquisitions like Tableau and Slack. The piece emphasizes the importance of culture, customer-centric innovation, and collaborative ecosystems in Salesforce's strategy for future growth.

title: S&P 500 falls Friday, notches second straight week of losses in September slump
summary: Stocks, including the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite, experienced declines on Friday, marking the second consecutive week of losses for the S&P 500. This downturn is attributed to investor caution regarding the resurgent Covid virus, an upcoming Federal Reserve meeting, and September's historical tendency for market weakness. The market is also anticipating increased volatility due to seasonal patterns, continued virus uncertainty, and upcoming monetary and fiscal policy announcements from September to October.

title: Wells Fargo cloud plans revealed amid sweeping IT overhaul
summary: Wells Fargo has unveiled a new multi-cloud infrastructure strategy, selecting Azure as its primary public cloud provider and Google Cloud for AI solutions, alongside existing HPE GreenLake contracts. This move is part of a sweeping IT overhaul aimed at driving technological speed, agility, and scalability, as well as addressing risk and compliance issues following a major scandal. The bank plans a hybrid approach, initially utilizing third-party data centers while aspiring to predominantly rely on public cloud offerings.

title: U.S. committee is reviewing Zoom's $14.7 billion deal for Five9 on national-security grounds
summary: A U.S. government committee is reviewing Zoom's proposed $14.7 billion acquisition of cloud contact center software company Five9 due to national security concerns related to "foreign participation." The committee, formerly known as Team Telecom, highlighted Five9's operations in Russia and Zoom's R&D staff in China as potential risks. Despite the review, Zoom anticipates the acquisition will close in the first half of 2022.

title: Propel raises $20M funding for its product lifecycle management platform
summary: Propel, a product lifecycle management (PML) startup, secured $20 million in Series C funding led by Salesforce Ventures, bringing its total raised to $48 million. The funding will support product development and sales for its Product 360 platform, which integrates quality management, PLM, and commercialization tools on Salesforce. The platform aims to help companies launch products faster, simplify compliance, and improve supply chain resiliency, with customers like Vizio and GoPro reporting significant improvements.

title: Google to Spend $2.1 Billion on Manhattan Office Building (Published 2021)
summary: Google announced its intention to purchase the St. John's Terminal building in Manhattan for $2.1 billion, marking one of the largest office building acquisitions in the U.S. in recent years. This move signals Google's continued confidence in New York City's vitality and its plans to expand its workforce there, despite the broader challenges in the city's office market due to remote work. The company already has a significant presence in New York and aims to hire an additional 2,000 employees in the coming years.

title: Parus files another patent infringement case on Apple
summary: Parus Holdings has filed a second patent infringement lawsuit against Apple, accusing the tech giant of infringing on its voice-browsing and device control technologies. Parus seeks damages, treble damages, and attorneys' costs, alleging willful infringement. This follows previous lawsuits against Apple, Samsung, and Google, and a recent victory for Parus at the US Patent and Trademark Office.

title: How cloud-native tech will impact 5G mobile networks
summary: Yaniv Hoffman of Radware discusses how cloud-native technology is transforming 5G mobile networks for Communication Service Providers (CSPs) in the Asia Pacific region. While offering benefits like reduced capital and operating expenditures and enabling new services, this shift introduces significant security challenges due to the distributed, microservices-based architecture of 5G. CSPs must adopt automated, scalable security solutions to protect against diverse threats arising from network slicing, edge computing, and increased exposure.

title: SiriusXM Launches New Free Channel and Premium Podcast Subscription with Marvel Entertainment on Apple Podcasts
summary: SiriusXM and Marvel Entertainment have partnered to launch Marvel Podcasts Unlimited, a premium audio subscription available exclusively on Apple Podcasts. This service offers subscribers early and exclusive access to new scripted and unscripted Marvel podcast series, including "Marvel's Wastelanders" and the Spanish-language adaptation of "Marvel's Wolverine: The Long Night." Additionally, a free Marvel channel on Apple Podcasts will feature popular existing series.

title: AI carbon footprint: Helping and hurting the environment
summary: This article examines the dual impact of artificial intelligence on the environment, highlighting both its potential for reducing carbon footprints and its own significant energy consumption. It discusses how AI can be utilized to prevent forest fires, optimize logistics, and reduce industrial waste, while also detailing the substantial carbon emissions associated with training large AI models. The piece emphasizes the importance of measuring and reducing AI's environmental impact through factors like algorithm efficiency, processor choice, data center energy efficiency, and renewable energy sources.

title: Thousands of Netgear routers can be hacked — here's what to do
summary: A serious security flaw in Netgear Nighthawk routers, stemming from the Disney-designed Circle parental-control feature, leaves thousands of devices vulnerable to hacking. Eleven different Nighthawk models are affected, and users are urged to update their router firmware immediately to patch the vulnerability. The flaw allows remote attackers with network access to gain control of the router due to unencrypted Circle update files.

title: Inside Wells Fargo’s multicloud strategy
summary: Wells Fargo is implementing a decade-long multicloud strategy, partnering with Microsoft and Google to modernize its technology infrastructure for public cloud operations. This approach, while different from some competitors, aims for portability, resilience, and avoids vendor lock-in, addressing the challenges of migrating highly regulated data and upskilling its workforce. The financial institution plans to progressively move existing applications to the public cloud, prioritizing impact over speed, with the ultimate goal of moving away from traditional data centers.

title: Google to Purchase US$2 Billion Business Center in New York
summary: Google plans to purchase the St. John's Terminal business center in New York City for over $2 billion, deepening its commitment to New York and establishing its new Hudson Square campus anchor. The company will also invest over $250 million this year into its New York campus presence and intends to hire 2,000 more employees, adding to its current 12,000 New York workforce. The St. John's Terminal, currently rented by Google, is expected to open in mid-2023 after renovations.

title: Cisco Named a Leader in 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for WAN Edge Infrastructure
summary: Cisco has announced its recognition as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for WAN Edge Infrastructure, highlighting its SD-WAN solutions. These solutions focus on enabling secure, predictable digital experiences for hybrid workforces, building dynamic workspaces, and securing multi-cloud environments, accelerating the transition to a SASE-enabled architecture. Cisco emphasizes its comprehensive capabilities in seamless multicloud access, integrated security, and optimized insights through ThousandEyes integration.

title: The Financial Services Data Revolution at Wells Fargo & JP Morgan
summary: Banks and financial services companies are rapidly adopting cloud-based data management solutions to modernize their operations and enhance customer experiences. Wells Fargo has partnered with Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud for its digital infrastructure, while JP Morgan Chase is leveraging AWS for a large-scale modernization effort. Snowflake has also introduced a Financial Services Data Cloud, highlighting a trend towards industry-specific cloud platforms.

title: Papa Johns Opening Headquarters in Atlanta
summary: Papa John's International is relocating its headquarters for commercial, communications, development, operations, people operations, and Diversity, Equity and Inclusion teams to Atlanta. The Louisville-based pizza company will occupy the top two floors of Three Ballpark Center at The Battery, totaling 60,000 square feet, and expects to house 190 employees in the new location. This move follows Papa John's announcement last September about establishing a corporate office in Atlanta, joining other major companies in the area.

title: Starbucks pushes back against US workers’ cafe-by-cafe union vote
summary: Starbucks is opposing unionization efforts by workers in Buffalo, New York, arguing that any union vote should encompass all 20 of its Buffalo-area locations rather than individual cafes. The company's stance challenges a labor board precedent that typically favors smaller bargaining units, with a hearing officer noting that single-location units are "presumptively appropriate." This move by Starbucks aligns with employer preferences for larger units to make unionization more difficult, amidst a broader wave of labor activism at nonunion companies.

title: BlackBerry ditches Classic, adding to smartphone future doubts
summary: BlackBerry Ltd announced it will stop producing its Classic smartphone model, a move that contributed to a more than 4% drop in stock and intensified doubts about the future of its handset business. The decision reinforces the company's shift towards software, as the Classic and other BlackBerry 10 devices struggled to compete with the iPhone and Android-powered phones. Additionally, an internal U.S. Senate memo revealed that major carriers were informed that all BlackBerry 10 devices had been discontinued.

title: Match to sidestep Apple and Google Pay with imminent updates to Korean apps
summary: Match Group plans to update its Korean dating apps by the end of October to allow alternative payment systems, bypassing Apple and Google's in-app purchase fees. This move follows a new South Korean law targeting these fees and represents an initial test of the legislation. Match Group, which expects to pay $500 million in such fees globally this year, is preparing for potential resistance from Apple and Google.

title: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment sells $270M worth of Tesla stake
summary: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment Management sold over 340,000 shares of Tesla, worth nearly $270 million, across three of its exchange-traded funds. This move comes as a bond selloff impacted rate-sensitive technology stocks, leading to outflows from Ark's growth-focused funds. Despite the sale, Tesla remains Ark's largest holding, with Wood predicting its shares will reach $3,000.

title: Baidu search engine review
summary: This article reviews Baidu, highlighting it as China's leading search engine and comparing it to Google. It emphasizes Baidu's utility for brands targeting a Chinese market, detailing its various products, advertising platform, and the necessity of searching in Chinese for optimal results. The review also touches on privacy features and user experience, particularly concerning translation challenges for English speakers.

title: General Motors’ new software platform Ultifi is coming to vehicles starting in 2023
summary: General Motors is launching Ultifi, a new end-to-end software platform, in vehicles starting in 2023. This platform will enable advanced capabilities such as in-car subscriptions, over-the-air updates for new apps and services, and greater control over vehicle functions. Built on top of GM's VIP hardware architecture and integrated with Android Automotive, Ultifi aims to centralize vehicle modules for faster updates and eventually allow third-party developers to create in-car applications.

title: Real-Time Communications at Scale
summary: Cloudflare is introducing its Real-Time Communications platform, a new suite of products designed to help build next-generation interactive applications. This platform, leveraging Cloudflare’s global edge network, aims to improve connectivity for WebRTC-based video and audio applications, addressing challenges like latency, packet loss, jitter, and scaling to thousands of participants. The initiative recognizes the surge in demand for real-time communication, accelerated by recent global changes, and seeks to simplify the development and scaling of such applications.

title: Friday’s analyst upgrades and downgrades
summary: This article details various analyst upgrades and downgrades on October 1, 2021, covering companies in the fertilizer, real estate, energy infrastructure, gaming, and renewable royalties sectors. Analysts from Citi, JP Morgan, TD Securities, Credit Suisse, RBC Dominion Securities, Raymond James, National Bank Financial, CIBC World Markets, Scotia Capital, and Piper Sandler provided updated ratings, price targets, and rationales for their investment recommendations. Key companies discussed include Nutrien Ltd., various Canadian REITs, Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd., Enthusiast Gaming Holdings Inc., Altius Renewable Royalties Corp., and several large-cap internet stocks.

title: Tesla is ordered to pay former worker $137 million for racism at plant
summary: A federal jury in San Francisco has ordered Tesla to pay a Black former elevator operator $137 million in damages. The worker, Owen Diaz, endured racial taunts and offensive graffiti at Tesla's Northern California plant, which the company allegedly ignored. The verdict includes $6.9 million for emotional distress and $130 million in punitive damages, sending a strong message to Tesla regarding its treatment of employees.

title: VMware Helps Customers Move to the Cloud With Flexibility and Speed
summary: VMware has announced new advancements for its VMware Cloud platform, designed to help customers modernize applications, increase business agility, and reduce costs. These innovations include a new portfolio of managed Kubernetes services, capabilities to enhance security and simplify running enterprise applications, and an initiative supporting sovereign clouds. The company also showcased future tech previews like Project Arctic and Project Capitola at VMworld 2021.

title: Departing Hulu Chief Kelly Campbell in talks to join NBCUniversal
summary: Kelly Campbell, president of Hulu, has resigned from her position and is currently in negotiations to take a senior role at Comcast Corp.’s NBCUniversal. Campbell's departure comes after over four years at Hulu, with the last 21 months as president, and follows frustrations over restructurings that reduced her oversight in certain areas, including content. Her potential move to NBCUniversal suggests a significant shift in the streaming and media landscape.

title: Korea's first-generation platforms collapse, ringing in new e-commerce era
summary: First-generation South Korean e-commerce platforms like Danawa and Interpark are being sold off as they struggle to compete with newer, more innovative companies. Despite the e-commerce boom, these pioneers are succumbing to new players like Naver and Coupang, who leverage AI recommendations and fast delivery. This shift signifies a new era in the highly competitive e-commerce market in Korea.

title: The Beam (Gen 2) delivers in price, features and ease of use - WiFiHiFi
summary: The Sonos Beam (Gen 2) soundbar offers excellent 3D sound with Dolby Atmos support at an affordable price, but fully utilizing its advanced audio features requires a newer TV with HDMI eARC and premium streaming music subscriptions. The review highlights improvements over the original Beam, such as a more powerful processor, redesigned speaker grouping, and eco-friendly packaging. It concludes that while the Beam (Gen 2) is a strong entry point into the Sonos ecosystem, the larger Sonos Arc still provides a more immersive experience.

title: PGE partnering with Google on Nest Renew, a service to help customers prioritize clean energy
summary: Portland General Electric (PGE) is partnering with Google on Nest Renew, a service designed to help customers prioritize clean energy. This collaboration offers options like Nest Renew Basic, which shifts electricity usage to cleaner energy times, and Nest Renew Premium, which matches estimated fossil fuel electricity usage with renewable energy credits. The initiative aims to provide customers with innovative ways to save energy, reduce their carbon footprint, and support renewable energy.

title: GM aims to build Netflix-sized subscription business by 2030
summary: General Motors announced its ambitious goal to generate $25 billion in annual revenue from in-car subscription services by 2030, putting it in the same league as Netflix. The automaker expects nearly $2 billion in revenue from these services this year, driven by its current base of 4.2 million subscribed vehicles and the upcoming Ultifi software platform. GM plans to monetize features like OnStar, Maps+, and fleet management solutions, projecting a serviceable addressable market of $80 billion by 2030.

title: Quantum computer maker Rigetti to go public via $1.5 bln SPAC deal
summary: Quantum computer maker Rigetti & Co Inc announced its plan to go public through a merger with a blank-check firm, Supernova Partners Acquisition Company II Ltd, in a deal valued potentially at $1.5 billion. This move makes Rigetti the second quantum computer hardware maker to list publicly this year via a SPAC. The merger is expected to provide Rigetti with approximately $458 million in proceeds, including significant investments from major financial firms and strategic partners like Palantir Technologies Inc.

title: Shaping the Future of Delivery, Robot Serve Doesn’t Need a Delivery Man to Bring You Food
summary: Serve Robotics, spun off from Uber-acquired Postmates, has developed a semi-autonomous delivery robot aimed at sustainable and accessible deliveries. These all-electric robots navigate sidewalks using cameras and Lidar sensors, with a human remote override for complex situations. The article highlights Serve's features, such as its 50 lb storage capacity and 3 mph top speed, and discusses its potential impact on delivery costs, traffic, and local restaurant sales.

title: Oracle picks Joburg for its first data centre in Africa
summary: Oracle has chosen Johannesburg as the site for its first data center in Africa, aiming to meet customer needs and provide cloud services within the region. This move is part of Oracle's global strategy to expand its data center footprint and support its clients in running critical workloads in the cloud. The South African market for data centers is not considered saturated, and this investment is expected to increase competition, boost cloud adoption, and foster skills development in the region.

title: Las acciones argentinas escalaron hasta 11%, mientras Wall Street cedió nuevamente
summary: Argentine ADRs saw significant gains, rising up to 11% for companies like Central Puerto, Pampa Energía, and Edenor, despite Wall Street experiencing negative variations. The local market was closed due to a holiday. Meanwhile, US indices like the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all declined, primarily due to rising oil prices and investor concerns over inflation and slowing US growth.

title: Finding randomly installed apps on your phone? Blame it on ads
summary: Users are reporting that certain advertisements sourced from Digital Turbine's demand-side platform can install apps on Android smartphones without user consent. This occurs when Digital Turbine's system-level software, often pre-loaded by carriers as DT Ignite, is present on the device, allowing the ad to bypass the Google Play Store's permission system. Digital Turbine states that user interaction should be required for app installation and that distributed applications are verified, but this loophole raises significant security and ethical concerns regarding unauthorized installations.

title: Democratizing Access to Care with Digital Health
summary: This article discusses the increasing need for digital health solutions to address healthcare inequities and the challenges posed by an aging global population with rising chronic conditions. It highlights how digital health can bridge gaps in information, treatment adherence, and access for marginalized communities, using a hypothetical patient example and real-world cases. The piece also mentions Boston Scientific's "Connected Patient Challenge," which awarded Kalia Health and General Prognostics for their innovative digital health ideas.

title: Google cloud customers can now track their carbon emissions
summary: Google Cloud has introduced new tools, including "Carbon Footprint" and updates to Active Assist Recommender, to help its customers track and reduce their carbon emissions. The Carbon Footprint tool allows companies to monitor emissions by project, product, or region and integrates with Salesforce's Sustainability Cloud. Additionally, Google is promoting the use of cleaner cloud regions and expanding access to Google Earth Engine for environmental insights.

title: Google expands Cloud Spanner database with PostgreSQL
summary: Google has expanded its Cloud Spanner database by introducing a new PostgreSQL interface, alongside the general availability of its BigQuery Omni multi-cloud data platform. This move aims to cater to developers by allowing them to use existing PostgreSQL skills and tools within Cloud Spanner, which is a fully managed relational database known for its scalability. Google now offers Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for easier migrations and Cloud Spanner with its new PostgreSQL interface for demanding, high-availability workloads.

title: Emerging trends in IoT gateway and edge application management in a cloud native paradigm
summary: This article discusses the emerging trends in IoT gateway and edge application management within a cloud-native paradigm. It highlights the shift towards remote, cloud-based management due to digital transformation, especially post-pandemic, and addresses the security and architectural challenges this presents. The author outlines six critical pillars for cloud-native IoT management in hybrid and multi-cloud environments, such as compute scalability and robust data processing, and introduces Cisco's IoT Operations Dashboard as a solution.

title: Groove closes $45M round to make enterprise sales teams more productive
summary: Groove Labs Inc., a sales software startup, has secured $45 million in funding led by Viking Global Investors to expand its customer base among large enterprises and grow international operations. The company's cloud-based platform, built on Salesforce, aims to boost sales team productivity by automating repetitive tasks and streamlining data management for major clients like Google, Atlassian, and Capital One. Groove emphasizes its platform's ability to enhance security and compliance by direct integration with Salesforce, minimizing data movement and reducing error risks.

title: Google Cloud, Hologic use AI tools to fight cervical cancer
summary: Google Cloud and medical technology vendor Hologic are collaborating to combat cervical cancer using AI and machine learning. Their partnership integrates Google Cloud's AI with Hologic's Genius Digital Diagnostic system to improve cervical cancer screening, aiming to make diagnostic technology widely accessible globally. This initiative seeks to enhance detection accuracy and provide a solution in areas with limited healthcare infrastructure.

title: Medtronic pledges R&D boost, brand refresh, amid rising Big Tech rivalry
summary: Medtronic is rebranding and increasing its R&D spending by 10% to adapt to the growing influence of consumers and tech giants in healthcare. CEO Geoff Martha emphasized moving "beyond devices" by investing in AI, data analytics, and robotics, acknowledging the company needs to build its direct-to-consumer presence. This strategic shift aims to speed up market entry and address chronic diseases, following a major reorganization implemented in October of the previous year.

title: S.Korea targets Apple over new app store regulation
summary: South Korea is moving to investigate Apple Inc. after the company indicated it would not change its app store policy, despite a new law requiring app developers to be able to use alternative payment systems. This law, amended in August, aims to curb the market dominance of major app store operators like Apple and Google by preventing them from mandating their own payment systems and charging commissions. Google, however, has stated its intention to comply with the new regulation.

title: GTLB Stock Price and Chart — NASDAQ:GTLB
summary: This article provides a detailed financial overview and stock performance of GitLab Inc. (GTLB) on the NASDAQ market. It includes current stock price, historical performance data, key statistics, upcoming earnings information, company background, and analyst ratings, alongside various trading ideas and technical analyses from the TradingView community. The content highlights the company's valuation, recent market fluctuations, and future growth expectations, including details on its financial statements and employee count.

The article discusses the growing trend of enormous special stock awards for startup founders, often far exceeding compensation for CEOs of established companies. It highlights examples like Archer Aviation, Palantir Technologies, and GoodRx Holdings, whose founders received nine-figure packages even before their companies were profitable or generated revenue. This practice contrasts with earlier Silicon Valley norms where founders like Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos relied on the appreciation of their initial equity, and it raises concerns about shareholder dilution and corporate governance.

title: Crawler Hints Update: Cloudflare Supports IndexNow and Announces General Availability
summary: Cloudflare announced two major updates for its Crawler Hints service: support for IndexNow, a new protocol allowing websites to notify search engines of content changes, and general availability of Crawler Hints for all Cloudflare customers for free. This initiative aims to improve the efficiency of web crawling by reducing wasted traffic, benefiting search engine operators with real-time updates and Cloudflare customers with fresher content in search results and reduced origin traffic.

title: Devin Nunes officially resigns from Congress, clearing way to helm Trump's social media company
summary: Devin Nunes officially resigned from Congress to become CEO of former President Trump's media and technology company, Truth Social. Nunes, a staunch ally of Trump, will lead the new platform which aims to be an alternative to mainstream social media. His move signifies his continued loyalty to Trump and his transition from a congressional career focused initially on local issues to national security and defense of the former president.

title: Smart Water for a Smarter Home: Moen Leads the Way with Industry's First Whole-Home Connected Water Product Suite
summary: Moen introduces the industry's first whole-home smart water ecosystem, the Moen Smart Water Network, which allows consumers to control, monitor, and conserve water throughout their homes using a single smartphone app. The network includes new and expanded smart products like the Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff, Smart Leak Detector, Smart Sump Pump Monitor, Smart Faucet with Motion Control, and Smart Shower, all designed to provide peace of mind, security, and personalized water experiences. These innovations offer automated water security, water usage education, personalized settings, and voice activation capabilities for a truly connected home water system.

title: Apple becomes first company to hit $3 trillion market value, then slips
summary: Apple Inc. briefly touched a $3 trillion stock market valuation on January 3, 2022, becoming the first company to reach this milestone, fueled by investor confidence in its product pipeline and expansion into new markets like automated cars and virtual reality. Although its market capitalization slipped just below $3 trillion by day's end, the achievement highlights the company's strong fundamentals and consumer loyalty for its iPhones, MacBooks, and services. The stock has seen significant growth since the first iPhone launch in 2007, and under CEO Tim Cook, Apple has successfully diversified its revenue streams beyond the iPhone.

title: Investor Michael Seibel Explains Google’s Search Quality Decline And How It’s Creating Opportunities
summary: Investor Michael Seibel, a partner and CEO at Y Combinator, has voiced concerns about the declining quality of Google Search results, particularly in categories like health, product reviews, and recipes, attributing the problem to Google's focus on short-term ad revenue. He believes this opens opportunities for disruptive startups, despite Google's dominant market share. Seibel highlighted that while DuckDuckGo offers an alternative, the fundamental issue lies in Google prioritizing monetization over user search experience.

title: 3 BYOD security risks and how to prevent them
summary: The increasing adoption of Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policies introduces significant security challenges for organizations, despite offering cost savings and flexibility. Key risks include data theft stemming from personal logins and cloud synchronization, unclear security protocols leading to shadow IT and employee-driven breaches, and the prevalence of mobile malware. Effective prevention requires robust mobile device management policies, including encryption, application blacklisting, regular data backups, and thorough employee security training.

title: Qualcomm inks car chip deals with Volvo, Honda and Renault
summary: Qualcomm announced deals to supply chips to automakers Volvo Group, Honda Motor Co Ltd, and Renault SA, accelerating its push into the automotive sector. The company will provide its "Snapdragon Cockpit" chips for digital dashboards and infotainment systems, aiming to help car manufacturers transform vehicles into rolling computers capable of over-the-air updates and generating recurring revenue. Qualcomm also unveiled a new chip and system, "Snapdragon Ride Vision System," for computer vision and safety features, utilizing technology from its recent acquisition of Arriver.

title: $20 Billion In 2022: Google Pays Apple For Not Launching Its Own Search Engine?
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Apple and Google, alleging an illegal agreement where Google pays Apple billions annually to remain the default search engine on Apple devices and prevents Apple from developing its own search engine. The lawsuit claims this arrangement violates US antitrust law, stifles competition, and inflates advertising rates.
