title: Brookfield agrees to buy Hibernia REIT for $1.2 billion
summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. has reached an agreement to acquire Hibernia REIT Plc for approximately 1.09 billion euros ($1.2 billion) in cash, causing Hibernia's shares to surge to a record high. The deal, which offers a 33.9% premium over Hibernia's average share price, sees Brookfield expanding its real estate portfolio in Dublin, a market where tech giants are rapidly growing. Brookfield is actively investing in European office landlords, capitalizing on market uncertainty and discounts to asset values.

title: Amazon Stock Rally Erases Losses for the Year
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares rallied, becoming the first megacap tech stock to recover its losses for the year,

title: Toyota, Aurora Test-Drive Autonomous Ride-Hailing Fleet In Texas
summary: Toyota and Aurora Innovation Inc. have begun testing an autonomous ride-hailing fleet in Texas using Toyota's Sienna minivans equipped with Aurora's self-driving system. The tests, conducted with two safety operators and no passengers, will cover highways and suburban streets in the Dallas-Fort-Worth area, including routes to the airport. This initiative aims to generate revenue from significant engineering investments in autonomous vehicle technology and prepares for a commercial launch on ride-hailing networks like Uber.

title: CEO interview: Silicon Labs’ Matt Johnson on balancing breadth and focus
summary: Matt Johnson, CEO of Silicon Labs, discusses the company's strategic shift to focus entirely on the IoT market after divesting its infrastructure and automotive businesses. He highlights the importance of offering complete, application- and software-led solutions for diverse wireless technologies in IoT, emphasizing security and continuous integration for cost, performance, and power reduction. Johnson also touches on the company's approach to manufacturing and capital deployment, including M&A and share repurchases.

title: KKR Values Behavioral-Health Startup Brightline at $705 Million
summary: Behavioral-health startup Brightline announced a valuation of $705 million after securing $105 million in a funding round led by KKR & Co. Existing investors, including Alphabet Inc.'s venture arm GV and Optum Ventures, also participated in the funding. Brightline provides virtual behavioral-health services to children and their families.

title: Best Global Company Culture 2022
summary: Comparably’s annual Best Global Company Culture list for 2022 ranks the top large companies (over 500 employees) with international operations based on anonymous employee feedback collected over the past year. The list highlights companies with strong cultures across nearly 20 categories, including compensation, leadership, and work-life balance, making it a relevant resource for job seekers worldwide. Microsoft, IBM, and Google took the top three spots, respectively, among the 50 recognized global companies.

title: Google Play Store App practices: France slaps $2 mn penalty on Google
summary: The Paris Commercial Court has fined Google 2 million euros ($2.2 million) for abusive practices against developers on its Play Store. Google is also required to amend seven clauses from its contracts from 2015 and 2016, which included a 30% commission on developer revenues. The French Ministry of Finance initiated the legal action in 2018, citing a significant imbalance in rights and obligations for app developers.

title: IonQ Named As One Of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies
summary: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), a leader in trapped-ion quantum computing, has been recognized on TIME’s annual TIME100 Most Influential Companies list for its leadership in commercializing quantum computing. The company was included in the "New Frontiers" category, acknowledging its extraordinary impact and recent achievements, including the introduction of IonQ Aria, the world's most powerful quantum computer. This recognition follows a year of significant business momentum and technical breakthroughs for IonQ.

title: GameStop Soars on Plans to Extend Rebound With Stock Split
summary: GameStop (GME) shares soared by as much as 22% in extended trading following the announcement of plans to propose a stock split to shareholders in the form of a dividend. The company intends to ask for approval to increase its Class A shares from 300 million to 1 billion at its upcoming annual meeting. This move led to a significant jump in the stock price, reaching $203.98 after closing at $166.58.

title: Nova Labs surges to $200m series D
summary: Helium, rebranded as Nova Labs, secured $200 million in Series D funding, leading to a $1.2 billion valuation. The funding round saw participation from corporate investors like Alphabet, Goodyear, Liberty Global, and Deutsche Telekom, alongside lead investors Tiger Global Management and Andreessen Horowitz and others. Nova Labs develops a blockchain-backed decentralized peer-to-peer wireless internet-of-things network.

title: Why Big Companies Like Tesla and Amazon Are Splitting Stocks
summary: This article explains what a stock split is and why major companies like Tesla, Amazon, and Alphabet execute them. It delves into the financial and psychological reasons behind stock splits, such as making shares more accessible to a wider range of investors and signaling positive future performance, despite the total market capitalization remaining unchanged. The piece also discusses the impact of stock splits on retail investors and highlights the strong post-split performance of such stocks.

title: Expedia Hires Google Travel Advertising Director Rob Torres
summary: Expedia Group announced the hiring of Rob Torres, Google's former managing director of advertising and marketing, as senior vice president of Media Solutions. Torres previously worked for Expedia from 1999 to 2006. This move comes as Expedia aims to reduce its reliance on Google for customer acquisition, a goal that was temporarily set aside during the pandemic.

title: Livestream game platforms in fierce competition
summary: The Vietnamese game livestream market is experiencing fierce competition, with global technology giants backing popular platforms like Facebook Gaming, YouTube Gaming, Nimo TV, and Booyah. Local platforms such as VNG's TalkTV have struggled to compete with the financial power and lucrative offers from these international players, leading to their eventual closure. The market is primarily driven by ad revenue, and platforms are investing in streamer training and unique content strategies to attract and retain users and content creators.

title: Startup Warp raises $23M to reinvent the venerable command-line terminal
summary: Warp, a developer productivity startup, has successfully raised $23 million in funding, including a $6 million seed round and a $17 million Series A round. The company aims to modernize the command-line terminal, which it believes is an outdated tool despite being used daily by developers. Warp's new terminal is built with the Rust programming language, offers a modern interface, and includes features for improved collaboration and intelligent command suggestions, moving the terminal experience into the modern era for developers.

title: Alphabet’s Pichai Freed From Questioning in Google ‘Incognito’ Privacy Suit
summary: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has been excused from questioning in a consumer privacy lawsuit against Google. The lawsuit alleges that Google collects user data through its Chrome browser even when users are in "Incognito" mode. A California judge ruled against deposing Pichai regarding the Chrome feature, though Google's marketing chief will still face queries.

title: Boeing and Google Cloud Partnership Takes Flight, Aims to Transform Aerospace Industry
summary: Google Cloud and Boeing have announced a partnership to migrate hundreds of Boeing's applications to Google Cloud, enhancing scalability, flexibility, and leveraging advanced data analytics and AI/ML tools. This collaboration aims to modernize Boeing's IT infrastructure, accelerate software development, and improve manufacturing efficiencies while supporting Boeing's commitment to net-zero carbon emissions by utilizing Google Cloud's renewable energy-matched infrastructure.

title: Dreams of green data
summary: This article discusses the efforts by companies like Apple, Google, and Equinix, alongside Santa Clara officials, to make data centers more environmentally friendly. The primary focus is on reducing energy consumption and shifting towards carbon emission-free power sources for these energy-intensive technological backbones. The article highlights the increasing importance of cleaner power sources and less electricity use for data centers.

title: Evolution of GIS: How Maps Have Progressed from a Mapping Pancake to a Soufflé
summary: The article discusses the evolution of Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) from rudimentary mapping to sophisticated platforms integral to daily life and various industries. It highlights how digital maps and smartphone integration have transformed navigation and planning, expanding GIS applications beyond traditional uses to include military, agriculture, retail, and logistics. The piece also addresses challenges in real-time data and information authenticity while forecasting future trends, including AI integration, disaster management, and smart city applications.

title: HP Buys Poly (Formerly Plantronics)
summary: HP Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Poly (formerly Plantronics), a Santa Cruz-based workplace collaboration solutions provider, for $40 per share, totaling $3.3 billion including net debt. This acquisition aims to capitalize on the growing hybrid work trend, strengthening HP's portfolio in peripherals and workforce solutions. The transaction is expected to generate $500 million in revenue synergies by 2025 and improve Poly's operating margins.

title: These Black Women Launched An AI-Powered Beauty Tech And Secured Backing From Serena Ventures
summary: Parfait, an AI and facial recognition-powered beauty technology, has successfully closed a $5 million Seed funding round led by Upfront Ventures and Serena Ventures. Founded by four Black women with extensive tech backgrounds, Parfait aims to revolutionize the wig market by applying AI to solve problems like AI biases and the fragmented wig buying process for women of color. The funds will be used to enhance production and automate supply chain capabilities to provide personalized experiences for customers in the rapidly growing wig industry.

title: Pay-as-you-go MongoDB Atlas now available on Google Cloud
summary: MongoDB Atlas has launched a new pay-as-you-go offering on Google Cloud, simplifying subscription for developers by charging only for resources used without upfront commitments. This initiative aims to align with modern application development and follows significant revenue growth for MongoDB Atlas, partly attributed to its partnerships with cloud providers. The move also integrates MongoDB Atlas more tightly with Google Cloud services, making data analysis and application development more efficient.

title: MU professor says Google v. Oracle case leaves fair use ‘muddy’
summary: A University of Missouri law professor, Gary Myers, argues that the 2021 Supreme Court ruling in Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc. has left the concept of "fair use" in copyright law "muddy" for software development. The ruling, which stated Google did not violate copyright by using Java code in Android, failed to clarify what aspects of computer code are protected and could introduce uncertainty for future software innovation. Myers highlights specific areas like intent, market impact, harm to the public, and transformative use that require further clarification from the courts.

title: UK gamers prepare for ‘post-console’ future, finds Amdocs
summary: Amdocs research indicates that UK gamers are increasingly ready for a "post-console" future, driven by cloud gaming and 5G connectivity. The study found high enthusiasm for cloud gaming and the metaverse, with many gamers willing to pay more for these services and forgo new hardware purchases. Key priorities for gamers include content quality and the ability to stream from any device, while concerns about the metaverse mainly revolve around its early stage, hardware costs, and internet connection capabilities.

title: How technology is transforming the future of performance marketing
summary: Technology is becoming increasingly vital in performance marketing, offering benefits like omnichannel mapping, real-time data, mobile-first strategies, powerful AI-driven ad stacks, and robust fraud protection tools. These advancements help brands connect with audiences more effectively, optimize ad spend, and maintain ROI in an evolving digital landscape. The article highlights how ad-tech ensures campaigns are impactful and efficient.

title: The Top Funded Quantum Security Companies and Who’s Backing Them
summary: This article lists the top-funded quantum security companies, detailing their services, funding, and key backers. It highlights eight companies including Arqit, IDQuantique, ISARA, Quantinuum, Quantum XChange, Quintessence Labs, PQShield, and Sandbox AQ, with a focus on their various approaches to quantum-safe encryption and cybersecurity. The piece emphasizes the growing landscape of quantum security and the significant investments flowing into these innovative firms.

title: Federal antitrust lawsuit filed against Google over Maps monopoly and Waze deal
summary: A federal class action antitrust lawsuit has been filed against Google, alleging it leveraged its dominance in the GPS navigation mapping market through Google Maps and Waze, improperly locking app developers into its ecosystem. The lawsuit, filed by Dream Big Media, Inc. and Getify Solutions, Inc., claims Google engaged in anticompetitive practices, including imposing restrictive terms, acquiring monopolies through acquisitions like Waze, and using data from its services to disadvantage rivals, violating federal antitrust laws and California state law.

title: FCC Mapping Data Open, Google-Waze Challenged in Court, Florida Co-op and Conexon Connect Team Up
summary: The FCC has opened preliminary serviceable location fabric data to fixed wireless providers, enabling them to align their availability data before the full fabric rollout on June 30, 2022. Concurrently, Google faces a class-action antitrust lawsuit over its alleged dominance in the GPS service market through Waze and Google Maps, while Florida's Tri-County Electric Co-op partners with Conexon Connect to deploy a 2,400-mile fiber-to-the-home network to serve rural areas.

title: LinkedIn was the most exploited brand in phishing attacks last quarter
summary: LinkedIn became the most exploited brand in phishing attacks during Q1 2022, accounting for 52% of all analyzed attempts, a significant jump from 8% in the previous quarter. Cyber threat intelligence provider Check Point Research reported this surge, noting that phishers are increasingly leveraging social networks. The article details examples of these attacks, including spoofed LinkedIn and Maersk emails, and offers tips to avoid falling victim to phishing.

title: Apple Spends Record High on Lobbying Amid Pressure from Congress
summary: Apple Inc. spent a record $2.5 million on lobbying in the first quarter of 2022, marking a 34% increase from the previous quarter. This significant expenditure comes as the company faces growing pressure from the U.S. Congress regarding antitrust concerns. Other major tech companies like Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft are also heavily investing in lobbying efforts as Congress considers antitrust legislation that could impact the technology sector.

title: Cloud Architect: The Tech Skill Everyone Wants to Learn?
summary: Cloud architecture is rapidly becoming the most sought-after tech skill, with a 285% jump in class participation on Udemy. This demand is driven by the widespread adoption of cloud infrastructure by organizations, leading to a significant skills shortage. Cloud architects command a median annual salary of $131,513 and require expertise in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and continuous learning of diverse technical and soft skills.

title: What is fintech and why does it matter?
summary: Fintech, a combination of “financial” and “technology,” refers to software that makes financial processes more accessible and automates traditional financial services. Kirsty Rutter, Fintech Investment Director at Lloyds Banking Group, explains how fintech is transforming banking by improving customer experiences through technologies like AI and machine learning. Lloyds Banking Group is actively investing in and collaborating with fintech companies to enhance its services and maintain a competitive edge.

title: Tax Breaks Cushion Tesla’s Texas Landing
summary: Tesla received approximately $64 million in state and local tax breaks to build its Giga Texas factory in Austin, sparking debate over the efficacy of such incentives in generating promised economic benefits and jobs. The article highlights concerns that communities often give up more than they gain from these deals, drawing parallels to Tesla's Buffalo factory where job creation targets were not met. Community groups and local residents have raised issues regarding the deal's lack of oversight, potential for wage theft and unsafe conditions, and the challenge of local hiring due to language barriers, leading some local lawmakers to question the wisdom of future incentive deals.

title: WPP merges Essence with MediaCom to form EssenceMediacom
summary: WPP's GroupM is merging Essence with MediaCom to create EssenceMediacom, aiming to combine Essence's digital and data-driven expertise with MediaCom's multichannel planning for client growth. Nick Lawson, formerly global CEO of MediaCom, will lead EssenceMediacom as global CEO, while Kyoko Matsushita, global CEO of Essence, will become WPP Japan CEO to focus on high-growth markets. This merger is part of broader WPP initiatives to enhance integrated services and leverage technology for outcomes-driven marketing, including the integration of Mindshare with Neo and the formation of GroupM Nexus.

title: Does a Musk-owned Twitter dim Tesla’s star?
summary: Elon Musk's bid to buy Twitter has raised concerns about its potential impact on Tesla's reputation and future. Observers question whether this acquisition distracts Musk from Tesla's core mission and if the controversies surrounding Twitter could negatively affect the automaker's brand and stock performance. While some see potential for new alliances and free speech advocacy, others worry about conflicts of interest and potential harm to customer perception and privacy.

title: Award-Winning Actor Michael Greyeyes Joins Directing Team for CTV Comedy Channel’s Original Series, ACTING GOOD
summary: Award-winning actor, director, and choreographer Michael Greyeyes is set to direct five episodes of CTV Comedy Channel's new original series, *ACTING GOOD*. The half-hour scripted comedy, loosely based on the life of Anishinaabe stand-up comedian Paul Rabliauskas, is currently in production in Winnipeg and surrounding areas. Darlene Naponse, Amber-Sekowan Daniels, and Eric Toth will also direct episodes for the debut season.

title: Why AWS, Microsoft, Google, Visa Are Setting Base In Kenya
summary: Major tech companies like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, and Visa are establishing operations in Kenya due to its growing economy and increasing client demand for cloud computing services. Kenya's strategic location as East Africa's largest economy and a hub for Fortune 500 companies makes it an attractive market for expansion. This move is driven by the need to meet local data residency requirements and capitalize on the burgeoning African cloud computing industry.

title: China Grants First Driverless Taxi Permits to Baidu, Pony.ai
summary: China has issued the first permits for driverless ride-hailing services to Baidu and Pony.ai in Beijing, marking a significant step in the country's pursuit of autonomous driving technology. These permits allow the companies to offer rides to the public without a safety driver behind the wheel, though a safety supervisor is still required in the front passenger seat. Baidu commenced its driverless services in a 23-square-mile suburban Beijing area on April 28.

title: MOTO & MRAD Rise on Tech Stock Rally
summary: U.S. stocks, particularly technology stocks, climbed on Thursday, with Apple and Amazon's earnings calls anticipated. Meta Platforms' strong first-quarter earnings report, showing an increase in users beyond expectations, boosted the Nasdaq Composite Index and the S&P 500 technology sector. The SmartETFs Advertising & Marketing Technology ETF (MRAD C) and the SmartETFs Smart Transportation & Technology ETF (MOTO) offer exposure to different segments of the technology sector, with MRAD focusing on advertising and marketing technology and MOTO investing in smart transportation and related tech.

title: The Cybersecurity Threats Self-Storage Operators Face Today and How to Defend Against Attacks
summary: This article discusses the increasing cybersecurity threats faced by self-storage operators, who are often targeted due to fewer resources compared to larger companies. It outlines common attack types such as ransomware, spearfishing, cryptomining malware, cloud vulnerabilities, and endpoint attacks. The piece also provides actionable defense strategies including staff training, two-factor authentication, secure wireless networks, fortified endpoints, data backups, and selecting reputable service providers.

title: Nasdaq 100 Index: Tech Stocks Lose $1.8 Trillion in a Month Thanks to Fed
summary: Tech investors have experienced the worst start to the year in two decades, with the Nasdaq 100 Index losing over $1.8 trillion in value in April alone. This decline is attributed to a tumultuous earnings season, fears of an economic slowdown, and aggressive expectations regarding the Federal Reserve's rate-hike trajectory, with another hike anticipated next week. Investors are bracing for continued volatility in the market.

title: Amazon’s biggest drop since 2006 caps dismal month for tech
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares experienced their largest one-day drop since 2006, sinking 14% and erasing $206.2 billion from its market value, following a disappointing outlook. This slump contributed to a dismal April for major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Tesla, which collectively lost a trillion dollars in market value due to tumultuous earnings, rising costs, and concerns over Federal Reserve policy. The Nasdaq 100 Index also saw its biggest one-month decline since October 2008.

title: China grants driverless taxi permits to Baidu, Pony.ai
summary: China has granted Baidu and Pony.ai permits to operate driverless ride-hailing services to the public in Beijing, marking a significant step in the nation's driverless technology ambitions. These permits allow the companies to offer rides without a safety driver behind the wheel, though a safety supervisor is still required in the front passenger seat. Baidu has already started offering these services in a 60km2 area in suburban Beijing, continuing its heavy investment in autonomous driving and AI technology.

title: Ford finds $130m road to Cavnue
summary: Ford Motor Company co-led a $130 million Series A funding round for Cavnue, a US-based road technology startup. Cavnue, formed by Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners, is developing technologies to integrate roads with advanced automotive features like autonomous vehicles and is exploring its first automated vehicle corridor in Michigan. Alongside Ford, other strategic partners including Globalvia and Landstar also invested, contributing their expertise in digital road technology and freight delivery improvement.

title: Sonos is now part of the Matter smart home alliance, joining Amazon, Apple and Google
summary: Sonos has joined the Connectivity Standards Alliance (CSA), the group behind the Matter smart home standard, which aims to create a unified protocol for interoperability between smart home devices from various manufacturers. While Sonos has a history of protecting its intellectual property, the company stated its commitment to ensuring its products integrate seamlessly with other smart home solutions. Although its involvement is in early stages, this move signals Sonos's interest in the growing smart home ecosystem, potentially influencing future product developments.

title: Top 10 Growth Stocks by Market Capitalization
summary: This article defines growth stocks and explains how they differ from other investment types, highlighting their potential for capital appreciation and typical reinvestment strategies. It then presents a list of the top 10 large-cap growth stocks as of April 2022, detailing their market capitalization, forward P/E ratio, dividend status, and specific growth drivers for each company. The article also touches on general market performance of growth stocks and factors influencing their volatility.

title: Crypto Logs: Crypto Goes from Meme to Mainstream
summary: This article discusses the increasing correlation between Bitcoin and broader equity markets, particularly tech stocks, despite a weaker start to 2022 for crypto and blockchain equities. It highlights growing institutional interest in cryptocurrencies, exemplified by Silvergate Capital's customer growth and Fidelity's announcement to offer Bitcoin investments in 401(k) plans, suggesting a move from "meme to mainstream" for crypto. The author posits that increased institutional participation could lead to more efficient trading and research, ultimately benefiting Bitcoin and related equities.

title: Two Chinese driverless robotaxi services approved in Beijing
summary: Beijing has approved autonomous rideshare companies Pony.ai and Baidu's Apollo Go to operate SAE Level 4 driverless robotaxis on public roads within a designated 60 square kilometer area. While no operator is required behind the wheel, a safety supervisor must still be present in the vehicle. This marks a significant step for China's driverless future, with both companies planning to expand their robotaxi fleets after passing rigorous safety tests.

title: Global Payments Partners with Bakkt, Offering Crypto and Loyalty Programmes
summary: Global Payments Inc. has partnered with Bakkt Holdings, Inc. to expand its cryptocurrency offerings, allowing its customers to pay using digital assets and integrate crypto into various payment solutions. This collaboration will also enable Global Payments to broaden its banking-as-a-service bankcard offerings to include customer access to cryptocurrencies. The partnership is part of Bakkt's ongoing efforts to boost crypto adoption within the payment ecosystem, following similar collaborations with American Bank, Wyndham Hotel, Google, and MasterCard.

title: With interest rates rising, it's time to focus on MANG stocks instead of FAANG, according to Jefferies
summary: Jefferies analysts recommend focusing on "MANG" stocks (Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, and Alphabet) over "FAANG + Microsoft" as interest rates rise and the Federal Reserve tightens monetary policy. This shift is presented as a safer investment strategy during an environment of increasing rates. The article highlights the rationale behind prioritizing this particular group of tech giants.

title: Stock Splits Lead to Split Results in Trading
summary: This article analyzes the impact of stock splits on market structure, liquidity, retail investor participation, notional exposure, trade size, odd lots, and volatility in both equities and options markets. Using data from 61 stock splits since 2020, including a case study on Apple (AAPL), the Cboe team found that stock splits do not necessarily increase liquidity proportionally to the split ratio and can lead to a decrease in overall investor capital exposure, though they do increase retail investor participation. The study suggests while splits enhance accessibility, they may not always benefit existing shareholders.

title: Google Cloud and SAP Expand Partnership to Enable Native Integration Between Google Workspace and SAP S/4HANA® Cloud
summary: Google Cloud and SAP have announced an expanded partnership that will integrate Google Workspace, specifically Google Docs and Google Sheets, directly with SAP S/4HANA® Cloud. This integration aims to enhance collaboration and efficiency for businesses by allowing users to collaboratively edit documents with SAP data, ensuring data integrity and version control. The initial features are expected to be included as a standard functionality in SAP S/4HANA Cloud later this year, built on SAP Business Technology Platform.

title: DevOps: Why it is now the only way to develop software
summary: DevOps is presented as a cultural shift essential for modern software development, moving beyond traditional "silos" and "waterfall" approaches. It emphasizes collaboration between development and operations teams and leverages automation to achieve frequent, seamless updates, meeting high end-user expectations set by major tech companies. The article argues that without DevOps, it's impossible for applications to remain relevant in today's fast-paced digital environment.

title: 2022 Selloff Has Left the U.S. Stock Market Undervalued
summary: The 2022 stock market selloff has pushed the broad U.S. equity market into undervalued territory, trading at a 12% discount to fair value according to Morningstar's equity research. While value stocks remain attractive, growth stocks, particularly small-caps, now offer significant discounts after substantial declines. The article highlights undervalued opportunities in the Communications, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, and Technology sectors, despite ongoing headwinds like slowing economic growth, Federal Reserve tightening, rising interest rates, and inflation.

title: Stock Price Trading Dynamics and Splits
summary: This article examines the impact of stock price on market quality features and the decision to split a stock, focusing on the recent trend of large corporations splitting their high-priced stocks. It analyzes various market features like consolidated quoted spreads, quoted size coverage, and quote volatility across different stock price and volume categories. The analysis suggests that targeting stock prices in the $50-$100 range for liquid securities offers the best market quality results, although the evidence for splitting less liquid stocks is less convincing.

title: ICON Announces Tom vonReichbauer as Chief Financial Officer
summary: ICON has announced that Tom vonReichbauer, a veteran leader from companies like Tesla, Nest, Google, and Sunrun, will join as its Chief Financial Officer on June 1, 2022. vonReichbauer brings extensive experience in disruptive technologies and financial leadership, aligning with ICON's mission to transform construction through large-scale 3D printing. His appointment is expected to help ICON scale its solutions for housing challenges and continue its work in providing resilient, dignified housing and developing off-world construction systems.

title: Tech sell-off pushes Nasdaq to steepest drop since June 2020
summary: A tech sell-off on Thursday, May 5, 2022 pushed the Nasdaq Composite to its steepest drop since June 2020, wiping out hundreds of billions in market value. This downturn was driven by disappointing earnings reports from cloud and e-commerce companies like Shopify, Amazon, and Meta, coupled with investor concerns following the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike to combat inflation. The rotation out of tech began in late 2021 due to inflation fears and escalated with events like Russia's invasion of Ukraine, leading to significant year-to-date losses for many "Covid winner" stocks.

title: Vodafone, Cardinality.io and Google Cloud build smarter European network performance platform
summary: Vodafone, Cardinality.io, and Google Cloud have partnered to develop a smarter, pan-European cloud-native network performance platform. This platform will enable Vodafone to manage and enhance its mobile network across eleven European countries more efficiently, using AI to analyze billions of network data points daily. The collaboration aims to accelerate network automation, improve customer experience, and optimize network investments.

title: Google Cloud: Unifying Manufacturer Data
summary: Google Cloud has launched new solutions, Manufacturing Data Engine and Manufacturing Connect, to help manufacturers unify data from disparate assets and improve visibility. These solutions enable AI- and analytics-based use cases such as manufacturing analytics, predictive maintenance, and machine-level anomaly detection. Early customers like Ford, Kyocera, and Phononic are using these tools to enhance data transparency and optimize production.

title: 7 Charts for Making Sense of These Markets
summary: This article analyzes current market volatility through seven charts, highlighting the Federal Reserve's aggressive interest rate hikes as a primary driver. It discusses the impact on both stock and bond markets, the underperformance of growth stocks versus value stocks, and offers insights on potential opportunities for investors amidst the market adjustments.

title: Class Action Complaint Claims Apple, Google, Snap Liable for Facilitating 'Sexual Grooming' of Minors
summary: Apple, Google, and Snap Inc. are facing a class action lawsuit in California Southern District Court for allegedly enabling the sexual grooming of minors. The suit stems from a criminal case where Snapchat was used to coerce a minor into pornographic acts. The plaintiffs seek to compel the defendants to enforce policies to prevent such criminal conduct and comply with child abuse laws.

title: Korean Webtoon Companies that are giving the Audience Addictive Content
summary: The Korean webtoon industry is experiencing significant global growth, driven by the success of K-culture, despite challenges like increased competition and a decline in artists' average income in 2023. Key players like Lezhin Comics, Naver's Webtoon and Line Manga, KakaoPage, Ridi Corp's Manta, Toomics, and Tappytoon are expanding internationally, leveraging diverse genres, free-reading models, and innovative technologies like AI and NFTs. These companies are not only captivating worldwide audiences but also transforming the global entertainment landscape through partnerships and strategic investments.

title: Meta is opening its first store as VR headsets inch closer to mainstream reality
summary: Meta Platforms is opening its first physical store to sell VR headsets like the Oculus Quest 2, despite its Reality Labs division facing significant losses. The company is betting heavily on the metaverse, viewing it as the solution to boost virtual reality adoption beyond the current low engagement among teens. Experts suggest that widespread VR adoption could be triggered by one or two "killer applications" and that Meta's strategy is to build the foundational platform for this new computing paradigm, even if profitability remains years away.

title: Walmart, J.B. Hunt Take Lead in Driverless Technology
summary: Walmart Inc. and J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. are leading the adoption of driverless truck technology to enhance supply chain efficiency. Walmart has partnered with Gatik for "middle-mile" deliveries, achieving 200,000 accident-free miles, while J.B. Hunt is collaborating with Waymo on long-haul routes in Texas, delivering 862,000 pounds of freight without incident. These initiatives aim to address increasing consumer demand, driver shortages, and the overall safety and efficiency of freight movement.

title: Concentrix Announces Acquisition of ServiceSource, a Global B2B Digital Sales Company
summary: Concentrix Corporation announced its definitive agreement to acquire ServiceSource International, Inc., a global leader in B2B digital sales, for approximately $131 million. This acquisition aims to expand Concentrix's B2B sales capabilities, enhance its client portfolio, and is expected to be accretive to growth and profitability through significant revenue and cost synergies. The transaction is projected to close in the second half of fiscal year 2022, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

title: 15 Top Cities for Machine Learning Engineer Salaries
summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. cities offering the highest salaries for Machine Learning Engineers, based on data from Blind. It highlights that major tech hubs like Silicon Valley and Seattle lead due to high demand from companies like Meta and Apple. The piece also notes the increasing importance and compensation for AI and machine learning skills across industries.

title: Tinder owner Match sues Google in 'last resort' to avoid app-store booting
summary: Match Group Inc., owner of dating apps like Tinder, has sued Alphabet Inc.'s Google, describing it as a "last resort" to prevent its apps from being removed from the Google Play store. Match is contesting Google's policy of demanding up to 30% of sales from apps and threatening to block downloads unless Match uses Google's payment system exclusively. The lawsuit accuses Google of violating antitrust laws and seeks to protect Match from potentially hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue payments to Google.

title: Tinder's parent company Match is suing Google over in-app billing
summary: Match Group, the parent company of Tinder and other popular dating apps, is suing Google over its in-app billing policies on the Android platform. Match Group alleges that Google's requirement for apps to use Google Play Billing for all in-app transactions, along with Google taking up to a 30% commission, constitutes antitrust and unfair competition. Google defends its policies, stating that its fees cover platform development, security, and distribution services, and that Match Group is trying to unfairly leverage Google's investments.

title: Online dating giant Match Group sues Google over app store
summary: Match Group, the company behind popular dating apps like Tinder and OkCupid, has sued Google, alleging an illegal monopoly in the Google Play Store and anticompetitive in-app payment policies. Match Group claims Google's 30% cut of in-app purchases and its mandate to use Google's payment technology are harmful, especially as Google threatened to remove Match apps from the Play Store if they don't comply with new rules. Google, in response, argues Match Group is trying to avoid paying for services and that the majority of apps on its platform do not pay fees.

title: Qualcomm Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 1.40% on Tuesday, closing at $136.81, despite a mixed trading session for the broader market. This gain, however, meant the stock underperformed some competitors like Alphabet Inc. and NVIDIA Corp., and remained significantly below its 52-week high.

title: Rackspace is looking to sell itself and exit the public markets, again
summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. is exploring a sale of all or part of its business to return to private ownership, less than two years after re-entering the public market. The company believes a sum-of-the-parts valuation could exceed its current enterprise value, driven by attractive growth in its public cloud sector. This move follows tepid first-quarter financial results, with a net loss of $64 million and modest revenue growth, prompting concerns about its growth trajectory in comparison to the broader cloud market.

title: Google Cloud launches AlloyDB, a PostgreSQL-compatible database for mission-critical workloads
summary: Google Cloud has introduced AlloyDB, a new fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible relational database service designed for mission-critical workloads. Unveiled at Google I/O, AlloyDB is built on open-source PostgreSQL and Google Cloud's infrastructure, aiming to offer superior performance, scalability, and reliability compared to standard PostgreSQL and AWS Aurora. It emphasizes transparent pricing without I/O charges and includes AI/ML capabilities for management and analytical acceleration, positioning it as a strong competitor to Oracle and AWS in the database market.

title: Rackspace for sale, looking for privatization
summary: Rackspace Technology, which went public less than two years ago, is seeking privatization due to its market capitalization not reflecting the company's true value. The company, which helps businesses manage cloud environments, needs to make strategic changes to better compete in the growing multicloud market. Although profitable, Rackspace's growth isn't fast enough to satisfy stock market analysts, making privatization an attractive option to allow for necessary repositioning in the market.

title: How Sonos’ new voice assistant could take on Alexa and Google Assistant
summary: Sonos is launching its own voice assistant on June 1, focusing specifically on audio playback, which will support multiple music services. Unlike general-purpose assistants, Sonos Voice Control processes commands on-device for improved privacy and responsiveness. The company believes this specialized approach, combined with new hardware like the Sonos Ray soundbar, can carve out a significant niche in the voice assistant market, especially as adoption for broader smart speakers shows signs of slowing.

title: Improving PPA With AI
summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are increasingly being used in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools to enhance chip design by improving Power, Performance, and Area (PPA), reducing design errors, and accelerating time to market. It highlights that while AI can't replace the need for human designers to make critical decisions, it significantly streamlines tedious processes and optimizes designs that would be too complex for humans alone. The integration of AI promises greater efficiency, cost reduction, and the ability to design highly complex chips, as demonstrated by examples from leading technology companies.

title: Google’s New Wallet Digitizes Payment Cards Plus Drivers’ Licenses And Other Credentials
summary: Google has launched a new Google Wallet, aiming to digitize not only payment cards but also various other credentials like driver's licenses, vaccine cards, transit passes, hotel keys, and office badges. The new wallet is a core part of the Android mobile operating system and integrates with Wear OS, with plans to expand its capabilities and availability. Key features include ease of access, rich customer experiences, and enhanced security through biometric authentication or PINs.

title: 100k Club: Digital news subscriptions top 30m across largest publishers
summary: Research from Press Gazette indicates that the largest English-language news publishers collectively boast over 30 million digital subscriptions. The New York Times, Wall Street Journal, and Washington Post lead this group with more than 14 million subscriptions combined. Additionally, six other companies, including Gannett, The Athletic, The Weather Channel, Substack, The Guardian, and the Financial Times, each have surpassed one million digital subscriptions.

title: WD Targets Cloud Challenges
summary: Western Digital (WD) is launching new SSDs and HDDs to address the exponential data growth and performance demands in cloud environments, particularly for hyperscale customers. The company's new 22TB and 26TB UltraSMR HDDs leverage OptiNAND and enhanced SMR technology, while their Ultrastar NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSDs target disaggregated storage in public clouds to improve utilization and density. WD also notes a strong demand for client SSDs driven by remote work and gaming, reinforcing the critical role of storage innovation across the board.

title: Domino’s grants ‘Stranger Things’ fans ‘mind-ordering’ powers through new app
summary: Domino's has launched a "mind-ordering" app in promotion of season four of Netflix's "Stranger Things," allowing users to order pizza using facial recognition and eye-tracking technology. The app lets fans role-play as characters from the show and explore a virtual Hawkins National Laboratory. While Domino's says no personally identifiable facial data is stored, the initiative aims to experiment with nascent tech while engaging "Stranger Things" fans and boosting sales amid recent declines and inflationary pressures.

title: Eikon Therapeutics Announces the Election of Robin L. Washington to Its Board of Directors
summary: Eikon Therapeutics has announced the appointment of Robin L. Washington, former Chief Financial Officer at Gilead, Inc., as an independent director to its Board of Directors, effective May 12, 2022. Ms. Washington brings extensive experience from the biopharmaceutical and technology industries, including board roles at Alphabet Inc., Honeywell International, Inc., and Salesforce.com. Her election is expected to provide Eikon Therapeutics with valuable guidance as the company pursues future expansion and drug discovery initiatives.

title: A Look Into Public Clouds From the Ransomware Actor's Perspective
summary: This article examines the potential evolution of ransomware attacks in public cloud environments, proposing that while traditional ransomware is largely ineffective, threat actors could adapt their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to be cloud-native. It discusses how attackers might gain initial access, execute attacks through control and data plane APIs, and achieve privilege escalation using IAM misconfigurations. The article concludes that public clouds are inherently more resilient to ransomware than on-premises systems, but emphasizes the need for organizations to proactively secure identities and adopt best practices to mitigate theoretical cloud-based ransomware threats.

title: Uber Eats set to pilot autonomous delivery with robots, cars
summary: Uber Eats is launching pilot programs in Los Angeles for autonomous food delivery using robots and self-driving cars, aiming to reduce delivery costs and environmental impact. Alongside this, the company is introducing voice ordering through Google Assistant and allowing in-app food ordering at selected sports stadiums. These initiatives were announced during Uber Eats' second annual Go/Get product showcase.

title: QVC in the digital age: Tech giants like YouTube embrace livestream shopping
summary: Tech giants like YouTube are embracing livestream shopping, reimagining the QVC model from the 1990s. YouTube aims to streamline the existing organic behavior of users seeking product reviews on its platform by integrating live video shopping experiences with influencers. This move comes as livestream shopping has become a multi-billion dollar industry, particularly significant in China, and presents a win-win opportunity for creators and viewers by making the process easier and more interactive.

title: SK Telecom's latest virtual assistant is more than just a voice
summary: SK Telecom has launched "A.", a new virtual assistant app that differentiates itself from others like Siri and Bixby by featuring a customizable character. This app aims to be a personalized daily companion for users, offering content curation, schedule management, and conversational capabilities, while integrating various services and utilizing the GPT-3 language model.

title: DevSecOps: Why Security can no longer be an afterthought
summary: This article argues that security can no longer be treated as an afterthought in software development, especially with the shift to cloud environments and the expanding attack surface. It advocates for DevSecOps, a methodology that integrates security into every stage of the development pipeline, emphasizing shared responsibility and secure coding practices. The author highlights the increasing sophistication of cyber threats and the limitations of traditional perimeter security, proposing Zero-Trust as a necessary framework.

title: How to Send Money: The 9 Best Ways to Transfer Money
summary: This article details nine of the best ways to send money, catering to various needs from instant peer-to-peer transfers to large international sums. It compares options like Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, wire transfers, and money orders, highlighting their fees, transfer limits, and transfer times. The guide aims to help users choose the most suitable method for their specific financial transactions.

title: With multi-device FIDO credentials, you can now go all-in on passwordless | CXO Revolutionaries
summary: Apple, Google, and Microsoft's expanded support for multi-device FIDO credentials is set to revolutionize passwordless logins, addressing previous limitations of FIDO authentication like device-locked cryptographic keys and complex re-enrollment processes. This development, coupled with the Federal Zero Trust Strategy requiring phishing-resistant authentication, positions FIDO to become a prevalent, high-assurance authentication method for both consumers and federal use cases. The update promises seamless and secure access to FIDO credentials across multiple devices, even after device replacement.

title: Google 'private browsing' mode not really private, Texas lawsuit says
summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has amended a privacy lawsuit against Google, claiming the search engine collects user data even when users are in "private browsing" or Incognito mode, which implies anonymity. Paxton argues that Google deceptively tracks personal data, including sensitive information, while Google counters that the claims are inaccurate and outdated, asserting its strong privacy controls. This amendment is part of broader lawsuits filed by several states regarding Google's alleged deceptive location-tracking practices.

title: International Business Machines Corp. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: International Business Machines Corp. (IBM) stock fell 0.91% to $128.48 on Friday, May 20, 2022, underperforming the broader stock market, which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rise slightly. This marked the third consecutive day of losses for IBM, leaving its stock $17.51 below its 52-week high. While IBM declined, some competitors showed mixed performance, with Apple Inc. (AAPL) rising and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. Cl A (GOOGL) falling.

title: Music festivals are a UX nightmare. Here’s how Snap and Live Nation are fixing them
summary: Snap and Live Nation are partnering to use augmented reality (AR) to enhance the music festival experience. New Snapchat lenses will debut at the Electric Daisy Carnival, offering features like 3D maps, set lists, directions, and a "FriendFind AR" tool to locate friends in the crowd. This collaboration aims to transform how attendees navigate and interact with large-scale events, going beyond mere selfies to provide practical utility and new engagement opportunities.

title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter, Google for ‘censorship’, launches his own social media platform
summary: Former President Donald Trump filed class-action lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google for alleged "censorship" after his accounts were restricted or suspended following the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol attack. The lawsuits claim these platforms, by coordinating with government entities, act as "state actors" and thus violate his First Amendment rights, though legal experts and court rulings have largely dismissed these arguments. Concurrently, Trump launched his own social media platform, "Truth Social," designed to be a "Big Tent" alternative to mainstream platforms.

title: Interxion pauses plans for $300 million expansion in Dublin
summary: Interxion has paused a $300 million expansion plan in Dublin due to a de facto moratorium placed on new data center developments in the greater Dublin area by EirGrid, Ireland's national grid operator. This moratorium, which could last until 2028, has led to calls for a nationwide ban and has prompted criticism from various industry bodies, despite local council efforts to prevent further data center construction. The situation highlights the growing pressure on Ireland's energy resources from data centers, which now consume 11 percent of the country's total grid-generated electricity.

title: Gartner: Marketing Budgets Increase To 9.5% Of Overall Company Revenue 05/24/2022
summary: Gartner's 2022 CMO Spend and Strategy Survey indicates a significant rebound in marketing budgets, which have increased to 9.5% of overall company revenue from 6.4% in 2021. Despite global economic challenges, 70% of CMOs reported budget increases, with digital accounting for 56% of the spend. Financial services recorded the highest budget at 10.4%, while consumer goods marketing spend slightly decreased.

title: Our Ultimate Stock-Pickers' Top 10 High-Conviction Purchases
summary: The article highlights the top 10 high-conviction purchases by Morningstar's Ultimate Stock-Pickers, focusing on significant additions to portfolios. Despite market volatility and inflation in early 2022, managers found value across various sectors, with Sherwin-Williams, T-Mobile, and Home Depot being particularly notable. Many of these high-conviction and new-money purchases received positive economic moat ratings from Morningstar analysts.

title: L’OFFICIEL Makes Its Arrival in the Metaverse with Virtual Land on The Sandbox
summary: Fashion magazine L’OFFICIEL has launched its presence in the metaverse with virtual land on The Sandbox, inspired by sci-fi films like Dune and Total Recall. This "L’OFFICIEL Land" is designed as an open-air exhibition and digital theatre to showcase the magazine's 100-year content history and future editorial focused on Web3 fashion. The initiative, led by Benjamin Eymère, CEO of L’OFFICIEL and Chief Metaverse Officer of AMTD group, marks a significant move into immersive digital experiences for the brand.

title: Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles revoked in California
summary: The California Department of Motor Vehicles has revoked Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles with safety drivers due to the company's failure to monitor the driving records of its safety drivers. The DMV found numerous violations on the driving records of active Pony.ai safety drivers, emphasizing the critical role of clean driving records for safety drivers. Pony.ai, while stating pride in its safety record of over 6.8 million accident-free autonomous miles, had previously lost a permit for driverless testing after a collision and subsequently recalled vehicles due to software issues.

title: How Chatbots are Revolutionizing Customer Experience
summary: Modern AI-powered chatbots are transforming customer experience by handling various tasks from ordering taxis to booking appointments, driven by advancements in AI, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Unlike traditional rule-based bots, NLP allows chatbots to understand complex conversations, retain context, and interpret human sentiment by integrating with external knowledge sources. Conversational AI, built on neural networks, enables chatbots to learn and improve continuously, process vast amounts of unstructured data to predict user behavior, and perform repetitive tasks, making them indispensable for businesses and freeing up human employees for more complex issues.

title: Global Data Annotation Tools Market Size, Share Forecast to 2033
summary: The global data annotation tools market was valued at USD 2.87 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 23.82 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 26.50%. Key growth drivers include the rapid penetration of AI in healthcare and massive data generation via advanced technologies, while the inaccuracy of some tools remains a restraint. Asia Pacific is expected to dominate the market, with North America also showing significant growth.

title: iRobot Unveils iRobot OS - The Most Thoughtfully Intelligent Operating System for the Home
summary: iRobot has launched iRobot OS, a new operating system that enhances the intelligence of its home robots. This OS integrates advanced computer vision and machine learning to offer features like improved pet-centric cleaning, object avoidance, and enhanced voice command capabilities for Roomba j7 and j7+ robot vacuums. iRobot OS is designed to make robot cleaning more effective and adapt to user preferences and home environments.

title: Apple Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: Apple Inc.'s stock (AAPL) fell 0.53% to $148.84 on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market as the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the end of a three-day winning streak for Apple, and the stock closed $34.10 below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed results, with Microsoft (MSFT) and IBM (IBM) also falling, while Alphabet (GOOGL) saw a gain.

title: To Promote 'Stranger Things,' These Businesses Developed an App That Lets You Order a Pizza With Your Mind
summary: To promote the fourth season of Netflix's "Stranger Things," Domino's partnered with WorkInProgress and Unit9 to launch a new "mind-ordering" app. This app allows users to order pizza using head movements, mimicking the telekinetic powers of the character Eleven. It also features a "Just for Fun" mode to explore the show's world and discover Easter eggs, building on Domino's history of innovative ordering methods.

title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology, focusing on value, quality, and momentum, can enhance core equity exposure for large-cap stock portfolios. It highlights research from FlexShares suggesting that this approach can deliver superior risk-adjusted returns compared to the broad large-cap market. The FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) is presented as an example of an ETF that utilizes these factors.

title: Ottawa should reject the Murdoch plan
summary: This article argues that Canada should reject Rupert Murdoch's plan to force tech companies like Google and Meta to pay news publishers for content, as successfully implemented in Australia. The author contends that the plan is a self-serving cash grab by large newspaper chains, particularly Postmedia, which is largely American-owned. The piece highlights Murdoch's history of media manipulation and questions the premise that Google and Meta are "stealing" content, while suggesting that Canada adopting this plan would create a domino effect for the UK to follow.

title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology can improve risk-adjusted returns for large-cap equity portfolios. It highlights factors such as value, quality, and momentum, and introduces the FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) which integrates these factors. The fund aims to provide benefits of these factor exposures while maintaining a similar risk profile to the broader large-cap market.

title: What Does Amazon's Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Amazon is executing a 20-1 stock split, its first in over two decades, effective June 3. The split will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate for Amazon to $192 per share from $3,850, but senior analyst Dan Romanoff's long-term view remains unchanged, anticipating continued growth in e-commerce, AWS, and advertising. Other major tech companies like Alphabet and Tesla are also planning stock splits.

title: KeyBank CIO: ‘Improving CX Is Our Endgame’
summary: KeyBank CIO Amy Brady discusses the bank's extensive cloud transformation to Google Cloud, aiming to move most products and services by 2025. She emphasizes that improving client experiences is the ultimate goal, and highlights the importance of managing cultural and talent challenges alongside technological changes.

title: Nvidia TAO Toolkit update aims to simplify deep learning model development
summary: Nvidia has updated its TAO Toolkit platform to simplify and accelerate deep learning model creation for enterprise applications, making AI development more accessible and less time-consuming. The toolkit now includes new capabilities like "bring your own model weights" and integration with TensorBoard for better visualization, along with the option to deploy as-a-service with REST APIs. While other companies have also worked on simplifying AI pipelines, analysts note that Nvidia's TAO Toolkit, with its low-code nature and pre-trained models, aims to speed up time-to-market for AI models and reduce the need for extensive data science expertise.

title: Facebook completes rebrand to Meta, changes Nasdaq listing ticker
summary: Facebook Inc. has completed its rebrand to Meta Platforms Inc., changing its Nasdaq stock ticker from 'FB' to 'META' effective June 9. This move signifies the company's strong commitment to building the metaverse, despite significant losses in its Reality Labs division. Meta is also integrating NFTs into Instagram and has plans for its own digital token.

title: Google Cloud Partnership to Bolster XPO’s Advanced Capabilities
summary: XPO announced a multiyear partnership with Google Cloud to enhance its supply chain capabilities through advanced AI, machine learning, and data analytics. This collaboration aims to improve visibility, optimize logistics in both truck brokerage and less-than-truckload (LTL) services, and support XPO's upcoming spin-off of its brokered services business. The partnership also emphasizes sustainability by reducing XPO's carbon footprint through more efficient transportation technologies.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Gains as Stock Split Lowers Price Tag for Retail Buyers
summary: Amazon's stock surged after a 20-for-1 split, making shares more accessible to retail investors. This marks the company's first split in over two decades, leading to increased trading volume and outperforming the Nasdaq 100 Index. The move is expected to attract greater retail interest, potentially acting as a sentiment catalyst.

title: Didi set to resume app downloads, new user registrations as probe nears end
summary: Chinese ride-hailing giant Didi Chuxing is expected to have its ban on app downloads and new user registrations lifted soon, signaling the near completion of a cybersecurity investigation by Beijing. This development, reported by The Wall Street Journal, suggests Didi's apps could be reinstated as early as this week. The move follows Didi's agreement to delist from the New York Stock Exchange to satisfy Beijing's demands.

title: Lawyer David Boies bills $1,950 hourly in Google case, court filing shows
summary: Veteran trial lawyer David Boies is billing $1,950 an hour in a lawsuit alleging privacy violations against Google. This billing rate is part of a fee petition filed after a judge sanctioned Google for litigation misconduct by failing to timely disclose key evidence. The lawsuit claims Google secretly collected user information while they were in "Incognito" browsing mode.

title: Oracle closes $28B deal to buy EHR giant Cerner
summary: Oracle has finalized its $28.3 billion acquisition of health IT company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move to expand into the healthcare market. The deal, which involved Oracle finalizing a stock tender offer with 69.2% of Cerner shares, aims to leverage Cerner as an "anchor asset" to scale Oracle's cloud business in hospitals and health systems. This acquisition positions Oracle to transform healthcare delivery through new information systems and addresses the growing trend of big tech companies investing heavily in the healthcare IT sector.

title: CareBridge Lands $140M from Oak HC/FT, Group of MCOs to Expand Value-Based HCBS Model
summary: CareBridge, a Nashville-based home- and community-based services (HCBS) provider, announced a $140 million funding round led by Oak HC/FT, with participation from four of the largest Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs). The funding, which values the company at over $1 billion, will be used to expand CareBridge's value-based care model for Medicaid and dual-eligible patients with physical or intellectual disabilities nationwide, including building the largest HCBS database and expanding services for I/DD patients. CareBridge utilizes technology, 24/7 clinical support, and data aggregation to deliver better outcomes and reduce hospitalizations for its patients.

title: Google partners up with Figma to bring the popular design tool to Chromebooks
summary: Google for Education is partnering with Figma to bring the web-based design tool to Chromebooks, allowing school districts to manage free licenses through the Google Admin Console. This initiative, starting as a beta for U.S. High Schools this summer, aims to equip students with visual communication and collaboration skills using accessible hardware. Figma's co-founder noted increased student engagement and interest in design careers due to the platform's trial in classrooms.

title: Verizon's cloud continuum meets MongoDB's multicloud deployment model (it's all supercloud, really)
summary: Verizon and MongoDB have partnered to simplify software development and networking, especially for mobile edge applications. They aim to abstract away the complexities of 5G and multicloud deployments through what Verizon calls a "cloud continuum" and MongoDB supports with its multicloud deployment model. This collaboration facilitates easier development by allowing developers to use familiar tools to interact with robust network APIs across various cloud providers.

title: MIGHTY MORPHIN POWER RANGERS #100 Announcement
summary: BOOM! Studios has announced the upcoming release of MIGHTY MORPHIN POWER RANGERS #100, a special oversized issue celebrating the milestone. Written by Ryan Parrott, this issue will culminate years of storytelling and feature a host of returning artists, along with collectible trading cards and an exclusive art print. It marks Parrott's final issue on the main series, promising an epic and climactic battle for the Rangers.

title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split, effective June 22, aiming to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors. This move is expected to boost demand and further increase share prices, building on its impressive 710% return over the past five years. Other tech giants like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA have also recently undertaken stock splits for similar reasons.

title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors, with stockholder approval scheduled for June 17. If approved, the stock price will drop from approximately $300 to $60 per share. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA, aiming to boost demand and potentially increase share prices.

title: Trudeau meets Google boss Sundar Pichai, but no word on whether the tech CEO chewed out the PM over Bill C-18
summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet (Google's parent company), but it's unclear if Bill C-18, a controversial Canadian media compensation bill, was discussed. The bill, criticized by experts like Michael Geist as a "shakedown," aims to make platforms like Google pay for linking to news content, giving the CRTC greater oversight. Google's Canadian head of public policy, Colin McKay, has stated that while Google supports journalism funding, Bill C-18 "would fundamentally and negatively impact millions of Canadians."

title: Google Agrees to Pay $118 Million to Settle Pay Discrimination Case (Published 2022)
summary: Google has agreed to pay $118 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment of women. The settlement covers approximately 15,500 women employed by Google in California since September 2013 and also mandates external oversight of its pay practices. Google denied wrongdoing, stating the settlement was in the best interest of all parties involved after five years of litigation.

title: Google Engineer Claims AI System is Sentient; China's Tech Giants Flourish as Crackdown Eases
summary: A Google engineer has been suspended after claiming that the company's LaMDA chatbot system shows signs of sentience, which Google denies, citing confidentiality breaches. Meanwhile, China's major tech companies like Baidu, Tencent, and Alibaba are experiencing a surge in share value as Beijing eases its regulatory crackdown on the sector. Twitter has also introduced a new "people-first" content moderation process to improve reporting of offensive content, especially amid Elon Musk's previous concerns about fake accounts.

title: Semiconductor giant Marvell plans ‘significant expansion’ of Kanata footprint after acquisition
summary: Marvell, a U.S. semiconductor company, is significantly expanding its presence in Canada, particularly in Kanata, following its acquisition of local microchip design firms. The company plans to build out its offices in Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver to develop semiconductor technology for cloud, 5G, and automotive markets. Marvell expects to leverage Ottawa's tech talent and academic partnerships for its growth, with a focus on cutting-edge technologies.

title: Oracle women stumble in pay bias suit while Google cuts a deal
summary: Women at Oracle Corp. face a setback in their pay disparity lawsuit as a judge tentatively revoked their class-action status, making it more difficult to proceed. Meanwhile, Google agreed to pay $118 million to settle a similar lawsuit alleging pay disparities for more than 15,000 female workers. The Google settlement includes provisions for independent oversight of hiring practices and pay equity studies.

title: Newmark Completes Sale of Moffett Green, Fully-Leased Trophy Campus in Silicon Valley
summary: Newmark has successfully completed the sale of Moffett Green, a 719,037 square-foot, fully-leased trophy office campus in Sunnyvale, California, to CommonWealth Partners, LLC. The transaction, which represents the largest single-asset investment office sale in Silicon Valley history, involved Meta Platforms, Inc. as the long-term tenant. Steven Golubchik and his team at Newmark facilitated the deal, highlighting continued investor demand for prime assets in high-barrier-to-entry markets and the strong performance of Moffett Park.

title: C3 AI & Google Cloud: Optimizing Supply Chains
summary: C3 AI announced a new supply chain software product developed in partnership with Google Cloud to address disrupted global supply chains. The C3 AI Supply Chain Suite leverages Google Cloud AI, infrastructure, and Supply Chain Twin to improve demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and supplier lead time visibility, leading to better on-time customer delivery. This collaboration integrates C3 AI's AI capabilities with Google Cloud's powerful infrastructure and data organization for resilient enterprise AI supply chain solutions.

title: C3 AI Receives Google Cloud AI/ML Partner of the Year Award
summary: C3 AI has been awarded Google Cloud's 2021 Technology Partner of the Year for AI/ML, recognizing the success of their partnership launched in September 2021. The alliance focuses on enabling customers to rapidly deploy enterprise AI applications across various industries, utilizing Google Cloud services like Cortex, Supply Chain Digital Twin, Vertex AI, and LendingDoc AI. This award highlights their joint efforts in delivering innovative, industry-specific AI solutions and accelerating customer value.

title: L3Harris in talks to buy Israeli spyware firm NSO - reports
summary: U.S. defence contractor L3Harris is reportedly in talks to acquire Israeli spyware firm NSO Group, a deal that would require approvals from U.S. and Israeli authorities and L3Harris's board. The potential acquisition raises concerns in the White House due to NSO's controversial Pegasus software, which has been used by governments to spy on individuals, leading to the company being blacklisted by the U.S. Commerce Department. If approved, the deal could potentially remove NSO from the banned list and allow its assets to be exclusively used with the United States and its allies.

title: McDonald's agrees to pay $1.3 bln to settle French tax dispute
summary: McDonald's has agreed to pay $1.3 billion in fines and back taxes to resolve a long-running tax dispute in France, ending a probe into whether the company properly declared its income. The settlement, which covers the years 2009-2020, does not constitute an admission of guilt and concludes both tax and criminal cases against the fast-food giant in France. McDonald's stated it paid over 2.2 billion euros in taxes and created nearly 25,000 jobs in France over that period.

title: Walmart enters shoppable TV via exclusive deal with Roku
summary: Walmart has partnered with Roku to introduce shoppable TV, allowing customers to purchase products directly through their Roku remotes while streaming. This collaboration aims to simplify the shopping experience on the largest screen in the home and integrates with Roku Pay for seamless checkout. This initiative is part of Walmart's broader strategy to expand its livestream shopping efforts across various digital platforms.

title: A closer look at P&G’s ‘water positive’ pledge
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced a "water positive" goal by 2030, aiming to restore more water than its operations and products consume. The initiative includes two new restoration pledges focusing on water consumed during manufacturing and by household product use in 18 water-stressed regions, primarily Los Angeles and Mexico City. P&G is investing in various restoration projects and integrating sustainability metrics into executive compensation, while experts commend the company's rigorous approach to consumer-use impact but call for more engagement with public policy for broader impact.

title: Oracle introduces lower-cost version of its full on-premises cloud stack
summary: Oracle has introduced a more affordable version of its on-premises cloud stack, Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer, alongside a new rack-level offering called Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer. The new Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer reduces the required space and annual cost significantly, making Oracle's full public cloud services, including Fusion applications, accessible to a broader range of global companies for workloads that cannot fully migrate to the public cloud. Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer provides managed on-site computing and storage resources for smaller workloads, similar to offerings from AWS, Microsoft, and Google.

title: Microsoft stops selling emotion-reading tech, limits face recognition
summary: Microsoft Corp announced it will stop selling emotion-reading technology based on facial images and will also limit unfettered access to its facial recognition technology. This move aligns with efforts by leading cloud providers to self-regulate sensitive technologies as lawmakers consider new legal limits. Existing customers of emotion-reading tools will have one year before losing access, and facial recognition services will now require approval for use.

title: How Comscore and YouTube Unlock the Power of CTV
summary: Comscore and YouTube have partnered to measure the effectiveness of YouTube advertising across various platforms, especially connected TV (CTV). Their findings indicate that YouTube provides significant unique reach beyond traditional linear TV, with nearly half of target audiences watching YouTube ads on CTV. This partnership aims to offer advertisers greater transparency and efficiency in cross-platform campaign measurement through Comscore's Campaign Ratings™ (CCR).

title: MinIO extends Snowflake analysis to any data location
summary: MinIO has partnered with Snowflake to enable Snowflake analytics on data stored in any location, not just within Snowflake's own environment. This partnership allows customers to leverage external table support in MinIO for cost-effective analysis of large datasets without moving them to the cloud. This provides flexibility similar to recent Snowflake partnerships with Dell and Pure Storage, offering various options for on-premises or cloud-based data analysis.

title: What Does Shopify’s Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Shopify is set to undergo a 10-for-1 stock split on June 28, the company's first split since going public in 2015. Morningstar senior equity analyst Dan Romanoff anticipates the fair value estimate will adjust from $450 to $45 per share post-split, with the stock maintaining its 4-star rating. This split does not impact the company's narrow economic moat rating and occurs amidst a lowered fair value estimate due to uncertain e-commerce outlook post-COVID and revised growth assumptions.

title: How T-Mobile's 3G shutdown will impact Google Fi and older Pixels
summary: T-Mobile's upcoming 3G shutdown in July will impact Google Fi subscribers, especially those using older devices. While newer Pixels received a VoLTE roaming update, Pixel 1 and 2 users may experience connectivity issues when roaming, and non-VoLTE phones will lose all voice call ability, including emergency services. Google Fi is offering a $200 service credit for affected customers to upgrade to newer devices.

title: Companies paying for abortion-related travel include Dick's Sporting Goods, Google, Disney
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, several major corporations, including Dick's Sporting Goods, Google, and Disney, are offering to cover abortion-related travel expenses for their employees. This move comes as at least 26 states are expected to ban or significantly restrict abortion access, prompting companies to take a stance on reproductive rights despite previously avoiding the issue.

title: Por qué un empresario propone colocar "estatuas de Cristina Kirchner en cada rincón de Uruguay"
summary: A Brazilian venture capitalist, Paulo Passoni, has provocatively suggested erecting statues of Cristina Kirchner across Uruguay. He argues that her policies have inadvertently driven a significant number of Argentine entrepreneurs and tech companies to relocate to Uruguay, appreciating its stable economic environment and clear rules. This migration has fostered a thriving tech ecosystem in Uruguay, benefiting the country by attracting talent and investment.

title: T-Mobile is now selling data on which apps you open
summary: T-Mobile has launched its new "App Insights" program, which sells app usage data to advertisers, allowing them to target users based on the apps installed and engagement patterns. While the program focuses on Android devices, Apple's strict privacy guidelines largely protect iPhone users from data collection, though T-Mobile notes that it is "kicking the tires" on incorporating iOS data in the future. Android users can opt out of the program through the "Magenta Marketing Platform Choices" app.
